jobs.title: Senior Analyst - Nightlife Controls
jobs.description:
The Nightlife Controls Senior Analyst is a hands-on, detail-oriented financial-controls role that supports the Nightlife Controller in monitoring, validating, and reporting on financially significant activity across Wynn Las Vegas Nightlife venues.

Working under the direction of the Nightlife Controller, the Senior Analyst independently performs recurring transaction reviews and exception monitoring, observes venue processes through surveillance footage and other monitoring tools, and supports the calculation and validation of payroll, tips, and commissions. The role also helps confirm that Nightlife payments are processed through approved company systems and supports the Controller with P&L reporting and variance research.

The Senior Analyst is expected to work through assigned reviews with limited day-to-day direction, perform first-level analysis, and bring documented findings and recommendations to the Controller. The Controller retains responsibility for final conclusions, further escalation, and overall oversight.

Why This Role Exists

Nightlife is a high-volume, fast-paced, cash- and comp-intensive business that generates a significant volume of financially relevant transactions every operating night.

Effective oversight of that activity depends on consistent, detailed review at the transaction level, along with timely follow-up on exceptions.

This role exists to provide consistent day-to-day monitoring of Nightlife financial activity, support accurate and policy-aligned compensation and payment processes, identify unusual or unsupported transactions, and give the Controller reliable analysis for reporting and decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Transaction Review & Exception Monitoring

• Independently perform recurring reviews of transaction-level activity and transaction registers to identify unusual, incomplete, inconsistent, or potentially noncompliant activity
• Perform recurring monitoring and exception reviews of point-of-sale activity, including comps, voids, discounts, adjustments, and open checks or open items
• Review comp activity against established authorization requirements and applicable limits, and research transactions that appear inconsistent with approved practices
• Track open items through resolution, following up with the appropriate parties and elevating items that remain unresolved
• Recommend refinements to monitoring procedures, review criteria, and exception thresholds based on observed results

Payroll, Tip & Commission Support

• Calculate or validate tip pools, gratuity and service charge distributions, host and VIP commissions, and other variable compensation in accordance with approved policies, agreements, and established methodologies, as directed by the Controller
• Reconcile compensation calculations to point-of-sale sales, service charges, timekeeping, and payroll data before submission; research and resolve discrepancies
• Prepare and maintain clear supporting documentation for each payroll, tip, and commission cycle so calculations can be reviewed, approved, and traced back to source data
• Coordinate with Payroll, Nightlife Operations, and Finance on submission timing, adjustments, and questions, under the direction of the Controller

Payment Controls

• Review Nightlife-related payments—including commissions, promoter, talent, and vendor-related payments—to confirm they are processed through approved company systems with appropriate authorization and supporting documentation
• Identify and escalate payments made outside the system, outside established approval requirements, or without adequate support
• Maintain trackers and records of payment reviews, exceptions, and resolutions
• Support the Controller in documenting and reinforcing payment procedures

Process Observation & Validation

• Perform venue and process observations, primarily through review of surveillance footage and other monitoring tools, to validate whether established procedures and financial controls are being followed
• Compare observed activity to transaction records, system information, supporting documentation, and established procedures
• Validate specific transactions and events selected by the Controller, such as comp authorizations, bottle deliveries, check settlements, and voids
• Coordinate with Nightlife Investigations and other departments as needed and as directed by the Controller
• Perform in-venue observations when requested by the Controller

Financial Reporting and P&L Support

• Prepare recurring schedules, reconciliations, and supporting analysis for monthly Nightlife financial reporting and the Controller’s monthly Nightlife Controls Report
• Research unusual P&L items and variances identified by the Controller, tracing them to transaction-level detail and summarizing findings
• Perform trend analysis on revenue, comp, payroll, and monitoring results to help identify patterns that may indicate a process or control weakness
• Support the Controller with ad hoc projects, analysis, and venue reopening and ongoing venue-control activities as needed

Documentation, Escalation & Coordination

• Document observations, exceptions, calculations, and follow-up items in a clear, objective, and organized manner, including preliminary assessments and recommendations for the Controller’s review
• Escalate unusual activity and potential control issues to the Nightlife Controller promptly
• Maintain trackers, working files, and supporting records for monitoring, compensation, payment, and reporting activities
• Handle sensitive information—including employee compensation, guest, and transaction details—with professionalism and confidentiality
• Work with Nightlife Operations, Finance, Accounting, Payroll, Compliance, Investigations, Inventory Control, IT, and other departments as needed, under the direction of the Controller
• Refer matters that may require investigative, disciplinary, or security action to the Controller for appropriate routing

Required

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration, hospitality management, or a related field
• 3–5 years of relevant experience in hospitality or casino finance, revenue audit, payroll, accounting support, internal controls, or nightlife or food-and-beverage operations with significant financial or transaction-review responsibilities
• Experience performing calculations, reconciliations, or reviews that tie operational activity to financial or payroll records
• Working understanding of how revenue, comps, payroll, and other operating activity flow into a departmental P&L
• Intermediate to advanced Excel skills, including pivot tables, lookups, conditional formulas, and working with large data sets
• Familiarity with point-of-sale systems and transaction processing
• Strong attention to detail and ability to recognize when information or activity does not appear consistent, complete, or properly supported
• Ability to manage recurring, deadline-driven work—such as payroll and month-end cycles—accurately and on time
• Ability to work independently with limited day-to-day direction, prioritize competing assignments, and follow established procedures
• Ability to document findings and communicate questions, issues, and recommendations clearly
• Ability to work outside standard business hours, including evenings, weekends, and holidays
• Ability to obtain and maintain required licenses or work cards applicable to the position

Preferred

• Experience calculating or reviewing tips, gratuities, service charges, or commissions in a casino, hospitality, or nightlife environment
• Experience supporting monthly financial reporting
• Familiarity with payroll, timekeeping, procurement, or ERP systems, as well as systems for inventory management, surveillance, or transaction monitoring
• Experience in a Las Vegas Strip or comparable premium hospitality environment
• Familiarity with nightlife or food-and-beverage operations, including comps, bottle service, and check settlement

Working Conditions

Work is performed in both a standard office environment and Nightlife venues. The position requires extended periods of computer use, including review of transaction data, system reports, payroll and compensation data, and surveillance footage, and involves recurring deadline-driven work tied to payroll and month-end reporting cycles. Because Nightlife venues operate primarily during late nights and weekends, the role will require work outside standard business hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays. When in-venue presence is required, the environment may be loud, crowded, low-light, and alcohol-service oriented. Must be able to stand and walk for extended periods during observations.

Wynn Resorts is an equal opportunity employer committed to hiring a diverse workforce and sustaining an inclusive culture. Wynn Resorts does not discriminate on the basis of disability, veteran status or any other basis protected under federal, state or local laws.

jobs.title: Senior Electrical Engineer (Prism)
jobs.description:
About Northwood:

Northwood is a modern space infrastructure company bringing the benefits of space to the masses through advanced communications technology. We are building a global network of phased array ground stations that enable real-time, reliable communication for satellite missions such as national security, global connectivity, and disaster response. With a vertically integrated approach, Northwood designs, builds, and rapidly deploys scalable systems that power the next generation of space missions. If you like solving complex challenges and seeing your work deployed around the world with real impact, Northwood is the place to do it.



Role: 
Northwood is looking for a Senior Electrical Engineer to own the non-RF electronics design for Prism, our 2.4-meter parabolic antenna for high-throughput satellite links. You will design the digital compute, power, embedded, and mixed-signal hardware that sits alongside Prism's RF chain- from block diagram and component selection through schematic, layout, bring-up, and production release.



Responsibilities

 - Own the electrical design of Prism's non-RF electronics: high-speed digital, power electronics, embedded control, and mixed-signal circuits

 - Architect and design high-density boards built around FPGAs, microcontrollers, high-speed data converters, and their peripherals, including DDR memory, multi-gigabit SerDes, and 10/100G Ethernet

 - Define clocking architectures: reference selection, clock distribution, jitter budgets, and synchronization across boards and subsystems

 - Design power trees end to end, from input power and conversion stages to point-of-load regulators, sequencing, monitoring, and protection

 - Design mixed-signal interfaces between digital and analog/RF domains, including ADC/DAC front ends, control loops, and sensor and telemetry circuits

 - Drive schematic capture, define PCB stack-ups, and lead layout of complex multilayer boards with a focus on signal integrity, power integrity, and EMI/EMC

 - Lead board bring-up and design verification, characterizing performance in the lab and iterating designs for performance, cost, and manufacturability



Basic Qualifications

 - Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering or a related engineering discipline

 - 5+ years of professional experience designing electronics hardware, with ownership of boards from schematic through bring-up

 - Hands-on design experience with high-speed digital systems built around FPGAs and/or microcontrollers

 - Experience designing board-level clocking and power distribution for complex digital systems

 - Proficiency in schematic capture, PCB stack-up definition, and layout of complex multilayer boards

 - Working knowledge of signal integrity, power integrity, and EMI/EMC design practices



Preferred Qualifications

 - Design experience with dense, high-pin-count FPGAs (e.g., AMD/Xilinx UltraScale+ or RFSoC) and the DDR, SerDes, and JESD204B/C interfaces around them

 - Low-jitter clock design: PLLs, jitter cleaners, clock fan-out, and clocking for high-speed data converters

 - Power electronics design: DC-DC converters, multiphase and point-of-load regulators, sequencing, hot-swap, and protection circuits

 - Embedded hardware design for microcontroller-based control and monitoring, with common interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, and Ethernet

 - Mixed-signal design, including precision analog, data converter front ends, and sensor interfaces

 - Lab skills with oscilloscopes, spectrum and network analyzers, and electronic loads, plus soldering and hot air rework

 - Python (or similar) for test automation and data analysis
   
   

Compensation:

Electrical Engineer/Level 3: $122,400-$153,000 per year

Electrical Engineer/Level 4: $144,000-$180,000 per year

Electrical Engineer/Level 5: $180,000-$225,000 per year



Additional Information:

If you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.



To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.



Northwood Space is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with Northwood Space is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Sales Manager, Gallery Partnerships (New York)
jobs.description:
Artsy is looking for a Sales Representative who will engage with galleries across the US, educating and consulting them on their online presence and digital strategy, and ultimately winning new business for Artsy.

This role is a part of our New Business Team, responsible for growing our marketplace supply by bringing new galleries onto Artsy’s platform. This is a target-oriented team where your contributions have a direct impact on Artsy’s bottom line.

In this quota-carrying sales position, you will be responsible for the full sales cycle, pitching Artsy's value proposition to Galleries and driving subscription revenue. You will focus on selling to emerging and Blue-Chip Galleries, requiring art industry expertise and a deep understanding of gallery sales motions and operations.

Working on the New Business Team provides a unique opportunity to expand Artsy’s global gallery network, supporting our goals of expanding the art market to support more artists and art in the world. 

This is a hybrid role with office attendance required three days per week in our New York office. 

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO AT ARTSY: 

 - Drive business development efforts by devising, implementing and conducting effective lead generation strategies, engaging with high-value prospects

 - Consistently achieve and surpass monthly and quarterly revenue targets for new gallery acquisitions

 - Manage the end-to-end sales cycle, from initial outreach to closing deals, while maintaining a strong focus on building and nurturing long-term relationships with key prospects

 - Build and oversee a robust sales pipeline, utilizing Salesforce and Outreach, and ensure high conversion rates for both inbound and outbound leads

 - Demonstrate expertise in objection handling, effectively addressing client concerns and positioning Artsy as the premier solution for their needs

 - Cultivate trust and credibility through timely and personalized follow-up, fostering strong and enduring partnerships with prospects

 - Collaborating with the Sales Development Associate to strategize on which markets to target based on events, art happenings and seasonality

 - Utilize AI and automation tools to increase process efficiency and provide better solutions to partners

 


THIS ROLE IS A FIT FOR YOU IF:

 - You are currently authorized to live and work in New York

 - Can work three days per week in our New York office

 - ~Approximately 5 years of art industry experience in a revenue-driving, client acquisition, retention, or account management role.

 - You have direct knowledge and understanding of Gallery sales motions

 - You are a consultative sales professional who prioritizes understanding and meeting customer needs in every interaction

 - You are solutions-focused and a creative problem solver, with strong negotiation skills

 - You are highly organized and able to manage sales pipeline efficiently and effectively; strong time management skills

 - You are an effective verbal and written communicator with the ability to effectively engage with VIP clients

 - Metrics-driven and highly results-oriented

 - Affinity for and interest in using AI and automation tools

This role is unlikely to be a good match if you….

 - You are not comfortable with sales, pitching, and negotiating

 - Prefer to work outside of a team setting

 - Are not interested in a target-heavy role

 - Are not interested in art or the art market

We know no one is a perfect match on paper, so if you’re passionate about this role, please apply! We’re excited to learn how your skills, experiences, and insights could make a difference.

 


WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Opportunity to reimagine the art industry while working with a talented, diverse, international team.

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Flexible time off: our culture of trust and empowerment allows employees to take the time they need away from work while still excelling in their roles

 - We are a global hybrid team: most employees work from our NYC, London, or Berlin offices 2-3 days per week. (In-person expectations vary by role)

 - Healthcare & benefit options vary by location. 

 - Professional development, including: mentoring, lunch & learns, regular training, 1:1 management, and an open feedback culture

 - Engaging opportunities and internal programming globally, to foster new relationships and build upon our collaborative community. Including: happy hours, holiday parties, global "All Hands" meetings, "Artsy Salon" (a yearly exhibition of our team's creativity), attendance to art world events, and more

The base salary range for this role is $65,000.00-$78,000.00 annually. In addition, you will be eligible for the company’s commission plan, with an annual variable compensation opportunity $30,000.

All compensation packages include meaningful Artsy equity and competitive health benefits. Please see our “What We Offer” above for more detail, or speak to our Talent Acquisition Team to learn more!


ARTSY AND ARTNET VALUES

Our values guide how we work, shape our decisions, and bring us together as one team. They keep us aligned and help drive us toward our mission: to expand the art market, support more artists, and bring more art into the world—helping us create a future where everyone is moved by art, every day.

Own the Outcome: We need all of us to achieve our mission. We take individual responsibility for team results, and we push to get the job done.

Move Fast, Learn Fast: We are building and reinventing every day, iterating quickly on multiple ideas to find what drives impact. We believe learning happens by doing and seeing what works.

Be Direct, Be Kind: We trust our colleagues and treat them with respect. Solving hard problems requires having hard conversations, and we support one another by being candid and kind.

Build for the Customer: We believe the art market has to evolve in order to flourish. We have a unique role to play in that growth, so we work hard to deeply understand the industry and build tools that solve real user needs.

Embrace Change: Achieving our mission in a dynamic tech environment demands constant change. We lean in to opportunity, face ambiguity bravely, and model to others and the industry a state of constant innovation and evolution.



Artsy is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, disability, and veteran status.

jobs.title: QC Lab Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

We are Sila, a next-generation battery materials company. Our mission is to power the world’s transition to clean energy. To create this future, our team is building a better lithium-ion battery from the inside out today. We engineer and manufacture ground-breaking battery materials that significantly increase the energy density of batteries, while reducing their size and weight. The result? Smaller more powerful batteries that can unlock innovation in consumer devices and accelerate the mass adoption of electric cars to eliminate our dependence on fossil fuels. We're tackling one of the biggest challenges of our time every day, and together we're redefining what's possible. Are you ready to be a part of a team committed to changing the world?

Who You Are

As a Quality Control Lab Manager, you will oversee the quality and reliability of our manufacturing output by leading high-throughput laboratory operations, rapid test execution, and rigorous material release workflows. You will manage day-to-day testing cadence, oversee instrument uptime and analytical method integrity, and spearhead continuous improvement initiatives across data integrity, sample management, and lab safety. This role is responsible for hands-on coaching, setting high standards for safety, maximizing equipment uptime, and establishing predictive maintenance strategies to support production targets. You will drive operational improvements and support the growth of the people, processes, and systems for the QC team, ensuring on time delivery of Sila’s material to high profile customers. The role will be based in Alameda, CA.

Responsibilities and Duties

• Operational & People Leadership: Lead, recruit, onboard, and retain skilled laboratory technicians; drive a culture of safety, continuous improvement, set clear KPIs, provide regular performance feedback, and allocate resources to meet fluctuating production volumes.

• Daily Lab Operations & Cadence: Direct day-to-day testing operations to support 24/7 manufacturing, development, and research needs, turnaround time (TAT) targets, and non-routine analytical investigations.

• Method & Equipment Ownership: Oversee routine maintenance, calibration, verification, and troubleshooting of analytical instrumentation; drive operationalization and transfer of new test methods to routine testing. Partner with key development teams to run initial predictive/preventive maintenance (PdM/PM) and Root Cause Analysis (RCA), establishing core reliability workflows to extend asset lifecycle.

• Quality Systems & Compliance: Champion laboratory data integrity, sample retain workflows, OOS/OOT (Out-of-Specification / Out-of-Trend) investigations, and root-cause analysis in full alignment with the Quality Management System (QMS).

• Measurement Systems & Studies: Direct Measurement System Analysis (Gage R&R), method precision studies, and stability/shelf-life testing programs to validate measurement reliability.

• Standard Work & Training: Author, standardize, and maintain SOPs and test protocols; manage laboratory training matrices to ensure verified analyst qualification and audit readiness.

• Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Analytics, Production, Process Engineering, Product, and Corporate Quality to resolve nonconformances quickly and prevent production bottlenecks.

• Financial & Asset Management: Manage departmental O&M budgets and critical MRO inventory.

• Goal Alignment & Performance Management: Set clear expectations, allocate responsibilities, track progress against key metrics, and support direct reports in navigating operational roadblocks.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements

• Education & Experience: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related technical discipline; 8+ years of industrial work experience, including 2+ years directly managing non-exempt personnel.

• Industry Domain Expertise: Extensive background in chemical or materials manufacturing, with deep operational knowledge spanning analytical instruments, particle analytical technologies, measurement system analysis principles, and lab operations.

• Quality Systems: Experience working within a quality management system; strong understanding of quality control systems and processes. Strong understanding of ISO9001 and ISO17025 preferred.

• Lean & Continuous Improvement: Advanced command of Lean Manufacturing methodologies and a proven track record of applying continuous improvement frameworks to maximize asset uptime and operational throughput.

• Leadership & Talent Development: Accomplished leader adept at coaching, mentoring, and developing teams, while instilling a proactive safety-first culture and operational accountability.

• Systemic Problem-Solving: Strategic, solution-oriented approach to diagnosing technical issues, leveraging Root Cause Analysis (RCA) to eliminate recurring failures across operations.

• Communication & Stakeholder Alignment: Exceptional communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with a demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional alignment and collaborate effectively across business units.

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

• Wear personal protective equipment including, but not limited to, a lab coat, gloves, safety glasses, and steel toe safety shoes.

• Move long distances (such as from building to building) and be stationary for extended periods of time.

• Operate a computer and other office equipment, such as a laptop, copier/printer, etc in a fixed location.

jobs.title: Staff Attorney, Senior Staff Attorney, or Senior Counsel, National Prison Project
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States; San Francisco, California, United States; Washington, District of Columbia, United States
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE JOB

The ACLU seeks applicants for the full-time position of Staff Attorney, Senior Staff Attorney, or Senior Counsel in the National Prison Project of the ACLU’s National office in Washington, DC, San Francisco, CA, or New York, NY. This is a hybrid role that has in-office requirements of two (2) days per week or eight (8) days per month. This is a two-year term-limited position.

The National Prison Project works to ensure that conditions in prisons, jails, juvenile detention centers, and immigration detention facilities comply with the Constitution, domestic law, and international human rights principles. The Project has successfully litigated on behalf of incarcerated people in more than 25 states, and is the only organization litigating conditions of confinement cases nationwide. Our priorities include reducing overcrowding, improving health care, eliminating violence and maltreatment, and increasing oversight and accountability in prisons, jails, and other places of detention. We also work to reverse the policies that have given the United States the highest incarceration rate in the world and led to extreme over-representation of people of color in the incarcerated population.

This position is part of a collective bargaining unit. It is represented by ACLU Staff United (ASU).

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Reporting to the Deputy Project Director for Immigration Detention, the Staff Attorney, Senior Staff Attorney, or Senior Counsel will contribute to all aspects of the Project’s litigation and non-litigation work, with a special focus on the Project’s immigration detention work.

YOUR DAY TO DAY

• Litigate in federal and state courts, including appellate courts, throughout the country

• Carry a substantial caseload in federal and state court, working closely with other staff attorneys and local counsel

• Conduct legal research and write legal memoranda

• Analyze legislation for potential litigation

• Draft pleadings and briefs, engage in discovery and motion practice, and conduct evidentiary hearings and oral arguments

• Provide technical assistance and expert legal advice to local ACLU affiliates, cooperating attorneys, and others who seek assistance from the Project

• Conduct policy advocacy on immigration detention, prisoners’ rights, and criminal justice issues

• Develop new cases, identify and work with potential plaintiffs and witnesses

• Engage in public speaking to a variety of audiences on a broad range of immigration detention, prisoners’ rights, criminal justice, and civil liberties issues

• Travel as required for litigation, case management, conferences, and client development

In addition to:

• Engage in special projects and other duties as assigned

FUTURE ACLU'ERS WILL

• Be committed to advancing the mission of the ACLU

• Center and embed the principles of equity, inclusion and belonging in their work by demonstrating commitment to diversity with an approach that respects and values multiple perspectives

• Be committed to work collaboratively and respectfully toward resolving obstacles and conflicts

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

• J.D. degree from an ABA-accredited law school

• Demonstrated litigation experience

• Admission to practice (based on office assignment)

• A demonstrated ability to work independently as well as within a team. Ability to foster and contribute to a collaborative team environment is essential

• Excellent legal research and writing skills

• Demonstrated ability to perform complex legal analytical work

• Demonstrated ability to write and speak clearly and persuasively

• Self-motivated, diligent and able to meet strict deadlines while under pressure

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Familiarity with issues related to conditions of confinement preferred

• Proficiency in Spanish preferred

COMPENSATION

The ACLU has a litigator scale that determines pay for attorneys in our Legal Department. The range of salaries are the following, based on year of law school graduation (please consult the hiring manager for specific salary details, based on individual circumstances)

• 0-2 years since law school graduation: $96,069 - $120,009

• 3-5 years since law school graduation: $134,414 - $158,579

• 6-10 years since law school graduation: $165,839 - $187,087

• 11-15 years since law school graduation: $190,585 - $201,403

• 16-20 years since law school graduation: $203,304 - $208,540

• 21-25 years since law school graduation: $209,595 - $213,890

• 26-30+ years since law school graduation: $214,920 - $219,104

The ACLU is committed to equity, transparency, and clarity in pay. These salaries are reflective of positions based in New York, NY where are National Offices are headquartered.  Salaries are subject to a regional pay adjustment if authorization is granted to work outside of the location listed in this posting.

For details on our pay structure, please visit: https://www.aclu.org/careers/ACLU_Geographic_Pay_Structure-July_2024.pdf

WHY THE ACLU

For over 100 years, the ACLU has worked to defend and preserve the individual rights and liberties guaranteed by the Constitution and laws of the United States. Whether it’s ending mass incarceration, achieving full equality for the LGBTQ+ community, establishing new privacy protections for our digital age, or preserving the right to vote or the right to have an abortion, the ACLU takes up the toughest civil liberties cases and issues to defend all people.

We know that great people make a great organization. We value our people and know that what we offer is essential not just their work, but to their overall well-being.

At the ACLU, we offer a broad range of benefits, which include:

• Time away to focus on the things that matter with a generous paid time-off policy

• Focus on your well-being with comprehensive healthcare benefits (including medical, dental and vision coverage, parental leave, gender affirming care & fertility treatment)

• Plan for your retirement with 401k plan and employer match

• We support employee growth and development through annual professional development funds, internal professional development programs and workshops

OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY, EQUITY, DIVERSITY & INCLUSION

Accessibility, equity, diversity and inclusion are core values of the ACLU and central to our work to advance liberty, equality, and justice for all. For us diversity, equity, accessibility, and inclusion are not just check-the-box activities, but a chance for us to make long-term meaningful change.  We are a community committed to learning and growth, humility and grace, transparency and accountability. We believe in a collective responsibility to create a culture of belonging for all people within our organization – one that respects and embraces difference; treats everyone equitably; and empowers our colleagues to do the best work possible. We are as committed to anti-oppression, anti-ableism, and anti-racism internally as we are externally. Because whether we’re in the courts or in the office, we believe ‘We the People’ means all of us.

With this commitment in mind, we strongly encourage applications from all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, marital status, citizenship, disability, veteran status and record of arrest or conviction, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

The ACLU is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If you are a qualified individual with a disability and need assistance applying online, please complete the Accommodation Request Form

If you are selected for an interview, you will receive additional information regarding how to request an accommodation for the interview process.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Senior Technical Project Manager

Location: San Diego

Hybrid / Onsite

The Senior Technical Project Manager is responsible for leading the planning and delivery of large, complex, and high-impact technical programs and cross-functional initiatives across SIE’s global People Technology platform.

This role operates as a senior individual contributor within People Technology Services (PTS), owning end-to-end program delivery and serving as the hands-on Scrum Master for the team’s established two-week sprint cadence. The role creates the governance, alignment, and delivery discipline needed to coordinate multiple workstreams, strengthen predictable sprint execution, and ensure strategic priorities translate into clear, executable plans.

Working within a globally consistent Agile product delivery model, the Senior Technical Project Manager partners with Human Resources, Payroll, Product Leads, Managers, Technical Leads, IT, Data, Security, vendors, and other cross-functional teams to align portfolio priorities, capacity, scope, timelines, decisions, and delivery outcomes. The role uses Jira, integrated delivery plans, dashboards, and sprint and program metrics to identify trends, advise leaders on trade-offs, and drive continuous improvement.

This role is suited for individuals who combine deep Agile, Scrum, and technical program management expertise with systems thinking, technical fluency, executive communication, and the ability to lead across teams, mentor others, and influence decisions without direct authority.

Key Responsibilities

Agile & Scrum Leadership

• Serve as the hands-on Scrum Master for the People Technology Services Team, leading a consistent two-week sprint cadence and facilitating sprint planning, daily stand-ups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews or demonstrations, and retrospectives.

• Own and continuously improve the team’s Agile operating rhythm, working agreements, backlog readiness standards, and sprint governance to strengthen focus, transparency, accountability, and predictable delivery.

• Partner with Product Leads, Managers, and Technical Leads to align priorities, capacity, dependencies, and sequencing across project work, operational support, intake demand, and unplanned work before sprint commitments are made.

• Facilitate clear sprint goals and realistic commitments; monitor progress, impediments, scope changes, carryover, and unplanned work, and lead timely resolution or escalation when outcomes are at risk.

• Use retrospective insights and delivery data to identify systemic bottlenecks, ensure improvement actions have accountable owners, and measure whether changes improve flow, quality, and predictability.

• Coach Product Leads, team members, and delivery partners on practical Agile and Scrum practices, reinforcing role clarity and shared accountability while adapting the framework thoughtfully to enterprise needs.

Technical Program Delivery Leadership

• Lead large, complex technical programs and high-impact initiatives from discovery and business case through planning, execution, testing, deployment, stabilization, transition, and closure.

• Establish program outcomes, scope, success measures, integrated roadmaps, milestones, governance, decision rights, delivery plans, and communication rhythms in partnership with sponsors and stakeholders.

• Maintain integrated schedules, RAID and decision logs, dependency maps, resource plans, and action trackers, surfacing issues early and assigning accountable owners.

• Orchestrate delivery across Product, Integrations, Data, Security, Architecture, Human Resources, Payroll, vendors, and other teams, ensuring workstreams remain aligned to shared outcomes.

• Partner with technical leads to evaluate estimates, sequencing, architecture and integration dependencies, technical risks, and delivery options; drive resolution while respecting technical ownership.

Strategic Planning, Capacity & Dependency Management

• Translate strategic priorities and portfolio commitments into realistic program, release, and sprint plans aligned with capacity, business value, technical sequencing, and operational needs.

• Advise leaders on scope, sequencing, capacity, and trade-offs; establish governance for changes and prevent unplanned demand from destabilizing committed delivery.

• Identify and manage complex cross-program dependencies, resource constraints, sequencing conflicts, and decisions; bring forward clear options, recommendations, and impact assessments.

• Contribute to portfolio planning and governance by assessing initiative health, challenging assumptions, and recommending reprioritization or corrective action when needed.

Delivery Analytics & Executive Communication

• Define and maintain Jira boards, integrated dashboards, and reporting standards that provide a reliable view of sprint execution, program health, milestones, dependencies, risks, decisions, and outcomes.

• Use sprint and program metrics—including sprint goal achievement, committed versus completed work, carryover, throughput, cycle time, blocked work, milestone performance, and trend data—to improve forecasting and delivery decisions.

• Translate complex technical progress, delivery risk, and cross-functional impacts into concise executive updates, decision materials, and data-backed recommendations for senior leaders and governance forums.

• Identify systemic delivery trends and emerging risks across initiatives, leading practical improvements to planning, workflow, governance, and team predictability.

Required Qualifications

• 8+ years of technical project or program management experience leading complex software, platform, integration, or infrastructure initiatives.

• Extensive experience as a hands-on Scrum Master for technical teams operating in recurring sprints and facilitating all core Scrum ceremonies.

• Deep knowledge of Agile and Scrum, including backlog readiness, story decomposition, estimation, capacity planning, sprint goals, impediment management, retrospectives, team coaching, and continuous improvement.

• Proven ability to lead large, complex, multi-workstream programs encompassing scope, roadmaps, schedules, governance, risks, dependencies, decisions, testing, change readiness, and release delivery.

• Advanced planning tool (i.e. Jira) experience, including board and workflow design, sprint administration, queries, dashboards, roadmaps, and program-level reporting.

• Demonstrated use of delivery data and sprint or program metrics to improve forecasting, influence priorities, communicate risk, and drive measurable improvement.

• Strong technical literacy across the software development lifecycle, enterprise platforms, cloud services, and release practices, sufficient to lead technical delivery and understand complex dependencies.

• Executive-level stakeholder management, facilitation, and communication skills, with the ability to translate between technical teams, business leaders, and senior decisionmakers.

Preferred Qualifications

• Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Advanced Certified ScrumMaster (A-CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM), PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP), Project Management Professional (PMP), or comparable certification.

• Experience within People Technology or HR Technology, including Workday or comparable enterprise platforms.

• Experience with Jira reporting extensions or visualization tools such as eazyBI, Power BI, Tableau, or comparable platforms.

• Demonstrated success mentoring others, resolving conflict, and influencing outcomes without direct authority in global, matrixed environments.

• Experience coordinating globally distributed teams, strategic vendors, or enterprise programs with significant organizational change and cross-functional complexity.

Profile

• Senior delivery leader and hands-on Scrum Master who creates structure, clarity, and momentum across complex initiatives without adding unnecessary process.

• Operates as a senior individual contributor, owning high-impact outcomes while aligning teams to governance, strategy, and broader People Technology priorities.

• Strong systems thinker and facilitator who connects portfolio priorities, sprint execution, technical dependencies, and business outcomes.

• Practical and delivery-oriented, balancing disciplined Agile execution with the judgment and flexibility required in a dynamic enterprise environment.

• Data-informed and skilled at turning Jira and program data into credible forecasts, executive insights, decisions, and improvement actions.

• Technically fluent and able to engage credibly with architects and technical leads, challenge delivery assumptions constructively, and respect technical ownership.

• Trusted advisor to Human Resources and technology leaders, with strong consulting, negotiation, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Comfortable leading through ambiguity, mentoring others, and influencing beyond immediate responsibilities in a global, evolving operating model.

At SIE, we consider several factors when setting each role’s base pay range, including the competitive benchmarking data for the market and geographic location.

Please note that the base pay range may vary in line with our hybrid working policy and individual base pay will be determined based on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

In addition, this role is eligible for SIE’s top-tier benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k), paid time off, wellness program and coveted employee discounts for Sony products. This role also may be eligible for a bonus package. Click here to learn more.

The estimated base pay range for this role is listed below.

jobs.title: Senior Cost Manager / Quantity Surveyor - Data Center Construction

Turner & Townsend are looking for an experienced Senior Cost Manager and/or Quantity Surveyor to act as the key, day to day client interface on a major, mission‑critical hyperscale data center construction project, ensuring that client objectives are met through the delivery of a value-added cost management service.

• Developing cost plans and estimates through the design phase, delivering updated cost plans at appropriate design milestones.
• Providing commercial input to design optioneering and input into value engineering exercises.
• Reviewing contractor and subcontractor pricing and leading negotiations on behalf of the client to drive fair contract prices.

• Ensuring that post-contract cost variances and change control processes are managed effectively.

• Carrying out the production of monthly cost reports for presentation to the client.
• Ensuring that final accounts are negotiated and agreed upon in a timely manner.

• SOX control responsibilities may be part of this role, which are to be adhered to where applicable.

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, cost management, quantity surveying, engineering or field related to construction.

jobs.title: Alliances Manager
jobs.description:
WHY MINTLIFY?

We're on a mission to empower builders. 

 - Massive reach: Our docs platform serves 100 million+ developers every year and powers documentation for 20,000+ companies, including Anthropic, Microsoft, PayPal, Spotify, Coinbase, X, and over 20% of the last YC batch.

 - Small team, huge impact: We recently passed 65 employees and raised a $45 million Series B led by A16Z and Salesforce Ventures. Each new hire has a huge impact on shaping the company's trajectory. 

 - Culture of slope over y-intercept https://mattrickard.com/hire-slope-not-intercept: We value learning velocity, grit, and unapologetically unique personalities.

We grew in value faster than headcount and we’re looking to align the two quickly.


WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON HERE

 - Seller team ownership → Own a dedicated set of AWS seller teams that are mapped one to one with a specific Mintlify sales team, whether that's an industry vertical or a segment, assigned by the Alliances Lead, and be personally accountable for adoption and pipeline results inside that paired book, not the AWS org broadly.

 - Account mapping execution → Build and keep current the AWS account overlap map for the seller teams they own, cross referenced against the accounts owned by their paired Mintlify sales team so AWS coverage and our own go to market motion are mapped against the same accounts, and turn it into a working list of named reps worth knowing.

 - Rep relationships at volume → Run a high meeting count with their assigned seller teams' account reps and solutions architects. This role earns credibility by showing up repeatedly inside their book, not by depth of a handful of relationships.

 - Co-sell execution → Set up co-sell meetings with their assigned sellers, run them, and follow through so they turn into real joint opportunities in deal registration.

 - Pipeline mining → Find opportunities inside their paired Mintlify sales team's pipeline where one of their assigned AWS sellers should be involved, and get our AE and that rep in the same room.

 - Field presence → Host fewer lunch and learns and tertiary events than the Lead's calendar might suggest, and instead index heavily on one on one touchpoints with AWS sellers tied to specific, active pipeline deals. Group events stay mostly on the Lead's calendar; this role's time goes to the highest volume of individual co-sell touchpoints on the team.

 - Program hygiene → Win wires, deal registration, and clean partner data for their book, so the reporting the whole AWS investment case depends on actually reflects reality.

 - Funding requests → Identify and submit AWS MDF and funding opportunities tied to their assigned seller teams, alongside the Alliances Lead and the PDM, and keep them tracked.



WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TABLE

 - 1+ year in the AWS ecosystem, either at AWS or a partner

 - Additional skills: Experience with Marketplace transactions or private offers.

 - Industry experience: Developer tools or working with technical buyers.

 - Technical skills: Enough product fluency to hold a credible conversation with a solutions architect. Salesforce comfort for account map and pipeline hygiene. Able to identify and submit AWS funding and MDF requests with the PDM to help prove out program ROI through cost reduction.

 - Experience requirements: 1+ year in the AWS ecosystem, either at AWS or at a partner. Comfortable with high volume outbound to internal AWS contacts without needing a warm intro to start.

 - Behavioral competencies: Wants to be 100% in the field. This is an execution seat, not a stepping stone into strategy on day one. Organized, this role lives in account maps, pipeline reviews, follow through and funding request administration, and it falls apart without discipline there. Wants to learn the alliance motion from the Lead and grow into owning a book, a cloud, or a strategy seat over time, but is genuinely motivated by the field work now.


COMPANY BENEFITS:

 - Competitive compensation and equity

 - 20 days paid time off every year

 - 401k with Employer Match

 - monthly wellness stipend

 - 100% employee coverage for Health, Dental, Vision

 - Commute stipend to help get you to and from work

 - Free lunch and dinners

 - Annual team offsite (previously went to Alaska, Hawaii, Jackson Hole)

jobs.title: Performance Manager
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Asset Living is a third-party management firm and a proven partner in fostering thriving communities nationwide. Founded in 1986, Asset Living has decades of experience delivering exceptional value to our partners. Since the beginning, our undeniable passion has driven our organic growth from a small property management firm to one of the most trusted allies in real estate. Asset Living's growing portfolio includes a multitude of properties across the country that span the multifamily, single-family home rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, active adult, and student housing divisions.

Asset Living is a fast-growing company made up of talented individuals from diverse backgrounds that differentiate us and help us drive innovation and results for our clients and communities across the US.  At Asset Living, we wholeheartedly believe 'Together We Lead, Together We Succeed’. We empower each other to lead by example, collaborate, and evolve – inspired by our belief that we can continually improve as individuals and as an organization. Together, we create an environment where every voice is heard, every idea is valued, and every individual experiences opportunities to grow as our company grows. When you join Asset Living, you become part of a dynamic team that thrives on unity, unique talents, and a universal culture of winning.

Recognized as one of the nation's Best and Brightest Places to Work and ranked in the NMHC top 50 professionals, join Asset Living because of its reputation as the most trusted partner in real estate, workplace culture, and growth opportunities. Asset Living is a member of The Institute of Real Estate Management (IREM) and is recognized as an Accredited Management Organization (AMO). Together, we lead the way, and together, we achieve excellence in all that we do. Join a workplace where success is a collective journey and leadership is a shared responsibility.

Performance Manager

The Performance Manager plays a pivotal role in enhancing employee performance and driving organizational success through comprehensive training, coaching, and performance management initiatives. This position is responsible for developing and executing effective learning programs, coaching individuals and teams, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and professional growth.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Communication

• Actively participate in organizational change initiatives, collaborating with various departments to ensure training initiatives support broader strategic objectives.

• Collaborate with other trainers or subject matter experts to enhance training content.

• Communicate effectively with stakeholders, providing updates on training outcomes and addressing any concerns.

Customer/End User Service

• Ensure learning solutions are engaging, effective, and tailored to meet the needs of various employee groups.

• Establish a continuous feedback loop with program participants to gather insights for refining and customizing learning programs.

Business Acumen

• Effectively use training technologies, such as Learning Management Systems (LMS) and multimedia tools.

Team Effectiveness (Training)

• Execute a comprehensive regional coaching plan each month driven by KPI results and global organizational objectives.

• Assist with delivering diverse learning programs, including leadership development, technical skills training, and onboarding.

• Support the implementation and utilization of learning management systems (LMS) and other relevant platforms.

• Deliver coaching sessions with clarity, ensuring participants understand the content.

• Enhance training content by incorporating real-world examples and case studies.

• Apply a blended learning approach, seamlessly combining in-person and online training modalities for optimal learning outcomes.

People Development (Global)

• Foster a culture of continuous learning and professional growth across the organization.

• Lead workshops to enhance individual and team performance through effective performance coaching processes.

• Identify, groom, and accelerate the development of high-potential individuals within the organization.

Problem-Solving

• Monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure the impact and effectiveness of learning and performance initiatives.

• Cultivate strong relationships with external vendors, consultants, and subject matter experts.

Role Execution (KPIs)

• Contribute to lower employee turnover.

• Improve tenure in each individual role.

• Increase internal promotions.

• Improve overall employee engagement.

• Maintain a high number of properties achieving Property KPIs.

Education & Experience

• Proven experience in employee training, coaching, and performance management, preferably in a field-based environment.

• Strong understanding of learning and development principles and best practices.

• Excellent presentation, facilitation, and communication skills.

jobs.title: Lead Space System Engineer
jobs.description:
Lead Space System Engineer

About the Team: The Sensors Division develops advanced solutions in radar, space-based sensing, electronic warfare, and underwater acoustics. Within the Space Missions and Sensing (SMS) Sector, we focus on advancing space sensing, space control, and counter-sensing technologies for critical national security missions.

The Role: Lead Space System Engineer

The SMS Sector is seeking a Lead Space System Engineer to leverage their systems engineering expertise in a dynamic Research & Development environment. In this role, you will be an integral part of a team dedicated to the development of a cutting-edge space-based sensing system platform.

You will architect the system and define requirements for the constellation, encompassing command and control (C2), intersatellite communications, ground processing, spectrum allocation, and satellite sensor modes. You will drive the critical decision-making process on how functionality is partitioned between space and ground segments, balancing mission performance against key constraints such as SWAP-C and security.

As the system engineer, you will collaborate closely with program leadership and external partners to establish and execute the program’s objectives, requirements, and development plan. You will also play a key role in assessing current and future system capabilities and providing technical development insights for business development initiatives. This position offers significant opportunities for career growth within a fast-paced and rapidly expanding company.

What you will do:

• Lead systems engineering and requirements development/management for a team building a space-based sensing platform.

• Architect and drive detailed analysis to derive command and control, data transport, and processing requirements.

• Collaborate with other team leads and subcontractors on the technology roadmap to test and integrate complex subsystems.

• Define mission partitioning between the system under development and other government systems, authoring the Interface Control Documents (ICDs) that govern these critical interactions.

• Provide guidance, coaching, and mentoring to junior staff to elevate the team's overall technical capability.

Who you are:

• Clearance: Active Top Secret (TS) security clearance (U.S. citizenship required).

• BS with 7+ years of experience or MS with 5+ years of experience in Computer Science, Physics, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Electrical Engineering or related field. With a proven track record in a System Engineering role.

• Sensing Expertise: Deep technical expertise in one or more of the following:

• Space-based RF/RADAR processing (including signal processing, spectrum allocation, or electronic warfare).

• Space-based Optical sensing and processing (including focal plane arrays, optical trains, or image processing).

• Flight Software: Proven experience with satellite flight software architectures, including real-time software development and hardware-software interface definition.

• Systems Lifecycle: Multi-disciplinary knowledge in mission modeling, systems design, hardware/firmware integration, and testing.

• Leadership: Skilled at directing the activities of development teams and managing technical deliverables.

• Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical requirements into actionable plans.

Even Better:

• Prior experience working on SCI (Sensitive Compartmented Information) or SAP (Special Access Programs).

• Experience designing, integrating, and testing optical communications hardware.

• Experience providing technical contributions to business development and proposal efforts.

• Experience with field test planning and execution.

jobs.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is looking for a Real Estate Analyst to join our team to help build and run our physical footprint. Every new market we launch starts with a building — a distribution warehouse to stage and service batteries, and eventually manufacturing and office space to grow into. Today that footprint spans a manufacturing campus in Austin, a distribution network across multiple states, and a headquarters. On every deal, you work with the teams who will use the building to scope what they actually need, then source the options, underwrite them, and negotiate the deal through a certificate of occupancy. This is a hands-on seat: you build the models, redline the leases, run the deal and walk the buildings.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Deals:

 - Scope new sites with the teams who will use it before we tour anything: footprint, power, dock doors, clear height, battery storage and fire code requirements, parking, and timing

 - Source and execute distribution warehouse launches in new markets, offices and manufacturing from site selection through certificate of occupancy

 - Build the underwriting on every deal we look at: base rent, opex, tenant improvements, escalations, abatement, parking, and yield on cost, with side-by-side scenario analysis so we know what we are trading away

 - On larger projects, build the lease versus own, build-to-suit, and yield-on-cost comparisons so leadership can weigh the options side by side

 - Redline and negotiate LOIs, leases, and amendments alongside our brokers and in-house counsel

 - Evaluate state and local incentives before we commit to a site

Portfolio:

 - Get ahead of expansion in existing markets by flagging which facilities are running out of room before it becomes an operations problem

 - Right-size the network: partner with deployments to produce utilization metrics for every distribution facility, then downsize or exit the ones that are not earning their footprint

Process:

 - Build the internal motion for real estate sourcing so deployments, launch, operations, and finance all plug into one process instead of five side conversations

 - Maintain the system of record for the portfolio: commencement dates, renewal windows, ROFO and ROFR rights, certificates of occupancy, insurance, and landlord contacts

 - Write the playbook as you go, so each new launch runs faster than the last and can be handed to the team running that market




WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 2–5 years in real estate, corporate development, investment banking, private equity, or an in-house real estate function

 - Strong Excel. You can build lease economics from a blank sheet and defend every assumption in it

 - Comfort reading a lease and forming a view on what is worth pushing on and what is market

 - You can sit with an operations team, work out what they need from a building, and push back on requirements that are not real

 - Project management instincts. You track long lists of open items across brokers, architects, general contractors, and landlords without dropping any of them

 - You build the process without being asked. You have taken a messy, manual workflow and turned it into something other people rely on

 - You adapt quickly. You can move from a lease redline to a credit discussion to a permitting call in the same day and do each one well




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Infrastructure & Development team is responsible for the planning, execution, and delivery of all capital construction projects required for Base Power to operate and scale. The team manages a portfolio that currently includes factory renovation, new factory construction, and office headquarters development, functioning as the owner's representative across all active projects. The team is structured to provide dedicated project management per active project, with shared procurement, cost management, and process support functions across the portfolio.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

Do work that matters, every single day.

Picture a toddler asking for “agua, please,” or a three-year-old proudly zipping her own coat and announcing “¡Lo hice!” At Guidepost Montessori, moments like these happen all day long, and as a Bilingual Assistant Guide, you help make them possible.

jobs.title: Learning & Education Specialist
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role:

The Support Operations team at Anthropic is dedicated to optimizing and scaling the Product Support function to deliver exceptional user experiences. As a Support Operations Specialist focusing on Learning and Education, you will be one of the first members of our Learning & Education function, helping own the programs that develop and grow the Product Support team's capabilities. This includes maintaining and evolving our existing onboarding program for new team members, program managing continuing education initiatives (such as "booster" trainings on complex topics or areas needing reinforcement), and partnering on enablement around product releases. You'll also work closely with the broader Product Support team on our internal knowledge management strategy, ensuring our team has the expertise to handle any question that comes their way.

Responsibilities:

• Maintain and continuously improve the onboarding program for new Product Support team members, keeping content current as our products and team evolve and adapting the program based on new-hire feedback and outcomes

• Program manage continuing education initiatives, including identifying training needs, developing curriculum, and measuring effectiveness

• Partner on release enablement efforts, ensuring the Support team has the resources and knowledge to support new products and features

• Co-own our internal knowledge management strategy, ensuring our team can efficiently access and contribute to shared expertise

• Build feedback loops to understand where the team needs additional support or training

You might be a good fit if you:

• Have 4+ years of experience in learning & development, enablement, support operations, or similar roles in a technology company

• Demonstrate a data-driven approach, using metrics and insights to continuously improve programs and measure training effectiveness

• Possess strong communication skills with the ability to distill complex technical concepts into engaging learning experiences

• Excel at cross-functional collaboration, particularly with Product, Engineering, and Support teams

• Are proactive and solutions-oriented, with excellent program management abilities

• Are comfortable joining a small, growing team early, building on existing programs and helping shape how the function operates

• Thrive in a fast-paced environment and can adapt quickly to evolving products and priorities

• Have a passion for AI technology and helping others build their expertise

Strong candidates may also have:

• Background in instructional design or adult learning principles

• Experience scaling or evolving onboarding or L&D programs as a team grows

• Experience with support or customer-facing teams specifically

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$1—$2 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.
