jobs.title: Head of Design, Product Design
jobs.description:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role will require being full-time onsite at our Palo Alto office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

BitGo is looking for a design leader who still designs. You will manage and mentor the design team, own the design system, and sit next to the Chief Product Officer on business strategy.

This is a player-coach role, and we mean it literally. You will carry your own design surfaces and ship them, alongside leading the team. Expect roughly 50% hands-on IC work to start, decreasing as the team scales. It will not go to zero — the person setting the craft bar should be practicing at it.

We are not a design-forward company today. We intend to become one, and we want you to lead that shift.

The team you will lead

The design team is small, senior, and self-sufficient. Each designer owns a wide vertical outright — trading, staking, DeFi vaults, earn, wallets, financing — with deep product context and strong opinions about the work. They are running at capacity, which is part of why this role carries real IC load: you will pick up the retail mobile experience and design system rather than distributing that work across a team that is already full.

What they have asked for is specific, and we are hiring against it: a leader who gets into the work early with product and engineering rather than arriving at the end, who can critique craft because they still practice it, who tells them plainly what the next level requires, and who gives the team air cover so they can do the deep work instead of patching to hit dates.

What you will own

• Your own design work. You will own surfaces directly and ship them at the quality bar you are asking of everyone else. Discovery through spec, in Figma, in the reviews, on the hard problems.

• The team's growth. Invest in each designer individually. Be explicit about what the next level requires and give people the work that gets them there. Feedback should be candid, specific, and about the craft. Respect the ownership designers already have — autonomy is how this team works best, and your job is to raise the ceiling, not take the pen.

• Design's standing in the company. Amplify the team's visibility, voice, and strategic impact. Represent design in strategy, roadmap, and architecture conversations, and push for the client experience when nobody else in the room will.

• Upstream involvement. Join product and engineering at discovery, not at handoff. Shape long-term roadmaps with PMs so the team builds toward a direction instead of absorbing late changes.

• The design system. Own the system and component library end to end: tokens, patterns, governance, contribution model, and adoption across product teams. Translate company strategy into a system flexible enough that teams ship scalable experiences rather than one-off patches.

• Systems design. Our platform spans seven product areas with shared primitives — accounts, wallets, assets, entitlements, approvals. Design the system, not the screen.

• The discipline. Establish UX and systems thinking as a practice the whole organization runs on, not a stage a design team owns. Product managers, engineers, and business leads should be able to frame a client problem, map the system it lives in, and evaluate a solution against real client needs. That is how we ship value to every client type we serve, in every market we operate in — rather than a set of features that work for the loudest account.

• How we work. Establish the processes a small team needs to move fast without losing quality: critique, documentation, design review, and clean handoffs with engineering. Set the quality bar and hold it, including for AI-assisted work.

• Technical depth. Read a technical design, understand the constraint, and decide with engineering where to compromise, where to hold, and where a broader change is worth the cost. Get into the mechanics with the team on the hard edge cases — the crypto ones and the design ones.

• The face of design. Be present and known internally, and represent BitGo design externally with clients, partners, and candidates.

What success looks like

By six months: the design system has a clear owner, a versioned component library, and measurable adoption. Product teams stop reinventing patterns. You have shipped design work of your own that the team points to as the standard. Every designer knows what their next level requires and has work that supports getting there.

By 12 months: design is in the room early on strategy, not late on execution. Product and engineering partners frame problems in client terms without being asked. The team has grown in size and capability. At least one flagship surface has shipped with a coherent, systemized experience clients notice.

Who you are

• Experience leading design in financial services. Digital assets, or another domain of genuinely complex technical flows, strongly preferred.

• You have built and owned a design system at scale, not just used one.

• Hands-on in Figma and a role model for craft. You are shipping design work today, not describing work you shipped four years ago. You can sit in a critique and give feedback that is specific enough to act on.

• Deep in UX. Strong product thinking, logical reasoning, and decisions grounded in data rather than taste alone.

• You have managed designers and made them better. You care about how the team is doing, not only what it ships.

• Technically literate. Comfortable with APIs, data models, and engineering trade-offs.

• Direct communicator. You can hold a position with a Chief Product Officer, an engineering lead, or a client, and change your mind when the argument is better.

• You want the mandate. Turning a technical, compliance-heavy platform into a design-led one is the appeal, not the obstacle.

Helpful, not required

• Regulated environments: broker-dealer, trust company, bank, or qualified custodian.

• Experience with complex permissioning, approval workflows, or multi-entity account structures.

• Design leadership at a company that went through the same shift you would lead here.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

• Competitive base salary, bonus, and stock options

• 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents

• Up to 4% 401k company match

• Paid parental leave, Paid vacation

• Free commuter/parking pass

• Free custom lunches and snacks

• Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs

• Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $210,000 and $250,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

About Guidepost Montessori

jobs.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Developer Productivity
jobs.description:
Build AI contracting at enterprise scale. Ship it fast.

Ironclad is building AI on one of the most consequential datasets in enterprise software: over 2 billion contracts across thousands of the world's largest organizations. Contracts run every dollar, deal, and business relationship on the planet, and the AI transformation of this space is still largely uncharted. Engineers here are building agentic solutions to problems that haven't been solved yet, in a category that's still being defined. The feedback loop is short, the data is rich, and the people closest to the work are the ones deciding what gets built next. That ability to deliver impact quickly is why the the companies at the forefront of AI choose Ironclad to manage their contracts.

We’re consistently recognized as a leader in the industry: a Leader in the Forrester Wave and Gartner Magic Quadrant for Contract Lifecycle Management, a Fortune Great Place to Work, and one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Workplaces. Ironclad has also been named to Forbes’ AI 50 and Business Insider’s list of Companies to Bet Your Career On. We’re backed by leading investors including Accel, Y Combinator, Sequoia, BOND, and Franklin Templeton. For more information, visit www.ironcladapp.com http://www.ironcladapp.com or follow us on LinkedIn.




THE ROLE

As a Senior Staff Engineer on the Developer Productivity team, you’ll lead improvements to how Ironclad engineers build, test, and ship software. Our team owns local development tooling, build and test systems, release automation, and our Backstage developer portal. We work closely with SRE at the intersection of developer tooling and infrastructure.


We’re looking for a hands-on technical leader with deep JavaScript/Typescript build and test experience, a background in SRE or infrastructure, and a track record of delivering projects that other teams adopt.


You’ll help shape the team’s technical direction and roadmap, working closely with engineers across Ironclad to understand where development slows down and what would make the biggest difference. You’ll turn those problems into practical tools and features, lead implementation and adoption, and use feedback to guide what comes next. You’ll also mentor engineers and share responsibility for supporting the tools we own.

As a Senior Staff Software Engineer at Ironclad, you’ll take broader ownership of the team’s direction, align priorities across teams, and lead improvements that benefit engineering as a whole.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Make JavaScript/TypeScript builds and tests faster and more reliable across webpack, Jest, and Vitest. Improve our Bazel build system, including remote caching, and lead the remaining migration off NX.

 - Build Kubernetes tooling that lets product teams make routine application changes independently.

 - Own the path from commit to production, including CI, environment promotion through Kargo, verification, and rollback.

 - Extend Backstage with plugins that connect deployment, monitoring, and incident data.

 - Make local development environments quick to start and consistent across engineers’ machines.

 - Use build times, CI reliability, lead time, and deployment frequency to identify problems and prioritize improvements.

 - Help set the team’s technical roadmap in partnership with other engineering teams. Identify problems, define solutions, and lead delivery and adoption, keeping engineering leadership informed of priorities, progress, and tradeoffs.

 - Lead technical discussions, mentor engineers, and participate in the team’s support rotation.

Our stack includes TypeScript, React, Node.js, and Docker containers running on Kubernetes in Google Cloud Platform.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 12+ years of experience, with at least 3 years in SRE, infrastructure, build systems, CI/CD, or developer tooling.

 - Deep experience with JavaScript and TypeScript build and test tools, such as webpack, Jest, or Vitest, including diagnosing slow builds and flaky tests at scale.

 - Production experience with Kubernetes and containers on GCP, AWS, or Azure, and CI systems such as CircleCI or GitHub Actions.

 - Strong programming skills in TypeScript, Go or Python, and comfort with shell scripting.

 - Experience leading technical projects that required adoption across teams, as a tech lead or engineering manager while staying hands-on.

 - Clear written communication, including design documents, technical proposals, and migration guides engineers can follow.

 - Alignment with Ironclad’s values: drive, intent, integrity, and empathy.




HELPFUL EXPERIENCE

 - Bazel or Nx, particularly migrations of JavaScript or TypeScript monorepos.

 - Kargo, Argo CD, or other GitOps tooling.

 - Building Backstage plugins.

 - Infrastructure as code, such as Terraform or Pulumi.
   
   
   

Base Salary Range: $245,000 - $270,000; offers company bonus

The base salary range represents the minimum and maximum of the salary range for this position based at our San Francisco headquarters. The actual base salary offered for this position will depend on numerous factors, including individual proficiency, anticipated performance, and the location of the selected candidate. Our base salary is just one component of Ironclad’s competitive total rewards package, which also includes equity awards (a new hire grant, along with opportunities for additional awards throughout your tenure), competitive health and wellness benefits, and a commitment to career growth and development.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.

Endor Labs is the third company from Founder & CEO Varun Badhwar, who built Prisma Cloud, the platform that helped define cloud security, from $0 to $300M ARR at Palo Alto Networks. We’ve raised $163M from Lightspeed, Coatue, DFJ Growth, Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital.

Software runs everything around our lives today - banking, hospitals, airports and power grids. AI now writes more of it every day, and our mission is to make sure the world can trust that software. Come build that future with us.

About the Role

At Endor Labs, building the most technically rigorous and developer-friendly AppSec platform (AURI) requires product leaders who can go deep into the details while keeping an eye on the bigger picture. As a Senior Technical Product Manager, you’ll own the definition and delivery of AI product capabilities across Endor’s platform, specifically the integration and connection of our Application Security features into the AI developer tooling.

AI is not an add-on at Endor—it’s the core execution fabric of the platform. You’ll be responsible for productizing agentic capabilities that make security teams meaningfully faster and more accurate, translating real AppSec use cases (auto-triage, reachable-only findings, secure design review, PR feedback, remediation suggestions) into reliable agent workflows with clear inputs, outputs, SLAs, and success criteria. This role goes beyond writing requirements and focuses on delivering intuitive, enterprise-grade, AI-first product experiences for modern AppSec teams.

How You'll Make an Impact

• Strategy and Vision: Own your product area’s vision, strategy, and success, aligning it with user needs and business goals. Directly engage with customers and prospects to gather feedback, understand user problems, and shape the product roadmap.

• Product Lifecycle Management: Define and prioritize features, while working with engineering, from ideation and discovery through execution, launch, and iteration.

• AI-First Platform: Enhance Endor’s agentic platform–define which agents to build, which tools to add, keeping in mind the trade-offs between cost and latency.

• Go-to-market: Work with product marketing, sales enablement and other teams to develop messaging and positioning for product launches, and create materials to support the sales team.

• Data-driven decision making: Use quantitative and qualitative data to track product performance, identify opportunities, and measure the success of the product area.

What You Bring to the Table

• Strong technical product management experience in developer-facing platforms

• Experience with modern developer workflows (CI/CD, IDEs, source code analysis); familiarity with application security concepts is a plus

• Hands-on experience productizing AI or agent-based systems, including defining workflows, guardrails, and success metrics

• Ability to go deep technically while maintaining strong product judgment and execution focus

• Proven ability to partner credibly with engineering, sales engineers, and customers

Why Endor Labs?

We’re building at the intersection of developer productivity and security — one of the fastest-growing spaces in software. Our dev-loved platform has real ROI, strong momentum, and customers who care about doing things right.

At Endor Labs, we think big, start small, and learn fast. We take ownership, move with purpose, and always start with the customer’s success. We debate with data, make the complex simple, and challenge each other with kindness and candor. We celebrate wins, learn from misses, and have fun along the way — because when our customers win, we all win.

Endor Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Even if you don't fit every requirement above, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and experiences, so we encourage all talented individuals to apply—there's no one-size-fits-all here.

Compensation: For candidates who receive an offer at the posted level, the compensation is expected to be between $180,000 - $240,000. This may include incentives/variable compensations such as commissions, stock options and/or bonuses, depending on the position. Final compensation will vary based on seniority and relevance of experience, location, and position requirements.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer
jobs.description:
BUILT ON FLAVOR.  FUELED BY PEOPLE.

What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it! Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

About The Role

We are a fast-growing company working hard to bring amazing flavor solutions that are as exciting and delicious as they are simple to use to our consumers whether they are experienced cooks or first timers in the kitchen. We are obsessed with quality and are 100% committed to being the most innovative company in any market we serve. Our mission is to bring awesome flavor to consumers whenever and wherever they are looking for it and whatever for they are looking for it in (seasonings, sauces, gravy, marinades, or anything else we can come up with). We have experienced tremendous growth over the last 5 years, but we think we are just getting started. We love our consumers and are fired up to be part of their flavor journey. And we need more great folks to help us continue to raise the bar for what they think is even possible in their own kitchens.

Today, we have over 100 products sold nationwide at retailers including Costco, Walmart, Sam’s Club, Whole Foods, Sprouts, Kroger, Safeway and many more. While we have been around for over 75 years, we have experienced explosive growth in the last 5 years and are now a top 5 brand in the U.S. in multiple flavor categories including seasoning blends, BBQ sauce, and wing sauce. To keep our momentum rolling, we need more passionate flavor advocates and builders to come and join our team and help us reach every kitchen across the U.S. and maybe even the world.

How you'll have an impact at Kinder’s

The Packaging Engineer provides technical/engineering support for all packaging development activities for sauces, seasoning/rub, innovation projects, and pallet displays from exploratory concept design through commercialization.

Key Responsibilities

· Lead the design, development, and qualification of primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging for new and existing products.

· Gather secondary and display design parameters from internal team/customer specification and communicate to 3rd party corrugate suppliers for design work

· Develop, present and optimize structural primary, secondary and merchandising packaging designs with our Brand team

· Work closely with packaging suppliers to meet Kinder’s and our manufacturing partners criteria for success

· Conduct structural integrity packaging studies to ensure package and pallet integrity while optimizing economics

· Communicate case coding requirements to copackers per customer specification, review and sign off on copacker case coding first articles/samples

· Evaluate and approve alternate packaging suppliers for both cost savings, supply chain redundancy and enhanced consumer experience

· Develop specifications for internal and external partners and develop associated documentation

· Develop and maintain master data related to primary and secondary packaging

· Provide packaging data for Kinders finished goods specifications and EPR reporting

· Review and approve finished goods specifications

· Review artwork proofs for die-line accuracy

· Collaborate with Product Development team to evaluate new primary packaging product, package interaction and associated shelf-life

· Execute continuous packaging improvement projects

· Work closely with both packaging suppliers and our contract manufacturing partners to improve package machinability, decrease labor, reduce cost and maximize throughput

· Independently lead packaging trials and qualifications at manufacturing facilities.

What You Bring to the Table

· BS Degree in Packaging Engineering or related field

· 3-5 years of food packaging or related field

· Strong problem-solving skills related to packaging structural design and machinability

· Demonstrated attention to detail

· Strong Knowledge of food packaging design and machinability fundamentals are required

· Excellent time management skills, sense of urgency, and desire to complete all assignments on a timely basis.

· Must be able to travel up to 30% of time

Highly Desired:

· Structural package testing experience

· Knowledge of Packaging Dynamic, barrier properties and manufacturing

· Understand key food packaging quality attributes and inspection methodologies

· Experience creating effective packaging design solutions

· Strong understanding of range of packaging substrates i.e. flexible packaging, corrugate, paperboard, bottles, labels etc.

· Personal Characteristics

· Thrive in a dynamic, lean, and agile environment.

· Comfortable in both the food plant and headquarters environment

· Self-starter who takes initiative and speaks their mind.

· Collaborative, technical packaging resource

· Excited to be part of a fast-moving team with the ability to be a leader and a follower

Location and Travel

We would consider remote work for this position based on the value add of the candidate and location, otherwise you would be based out of our office in Walnut Creek, CA. We strongly believe in the power of culture and community and have a hybrid work structure with 4 days in the office on a weekly basis to encourage collaboration and personal connections that will allow us to better serve our customers and consumer and to have more fun. Fridays are flex days with employees having the opportunity to choose to be either in the office or to work from home based on what makes most sense for them.

Typical travel includes industry conferences, trade shows and supplier operations visits.

Pay Transparency

The expected starting salary range for this role is $105,000- $115,000 per year. The salary range posted for this role reflects the good-faith base pay range Kinder’s reasonably expects to offer at the time of posting and may vary based on the location of the role. Individual compensation within the posted range will be determined based on factors such as relevant education, experience, qualifications, skills, and business needs.

SEASONED FOR SUCCESS:

• No two days here are the same.

• We try to be good team members and good communicators, but we don’t live by hierarchy and structure – everyone is a difference maker here.

• We make a lot of decisions in the face of incomplete information – our team embraces ambiguity and tries to make good decisions fast rather than great decisions slow.

• We believe our job is to take smart risk, not to eliminate risk.

• We believe in growing our skills and becoming a better company with more managerial expertise, but we are an entrepreneurial company at heart.

• We aren’t trying to be average – we want to do exceptional things, and we are willing to work hard to achieve them.

BENEFITS THAT BRING MORE TO THE TABLE:

We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, 401k, bonus / incentive eligibility, equity grants, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits, including parental leave. Kinder’s benefits vary based on eligibility and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

OUR RECIPE FOR BALANCE:

We believe great culture starts with people. We’re a people-first company built on connection, collaboration, and balance. Most of our work happens in the office to spark creativity and community, but we also offer flexibility so team members have the autonomy to work outside the office when needed to support their work-life balance and personal commitments.

WHERE EVERY INGREDIENT MATTERS:

Kinder's is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, gender, citizenship, marital status, religion, age, disability, gender identity, results of genetic testing, veteran status, as well as any other legally-protected characteristic. If you have a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act or similar law, and you need any accommodation during the application process or to perform these job requirements, please reach out to us at careers@kinders.com

jobs.title: Product Manager, Growth
jobs.location: San Francisco, NYC, or Fully Remote
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Office Hours is an on-demand marketplace for verified human knowledge. We connect leading organizations with trusted experts who earn income by sharing their knowledge through advisory work, research, and AI model training.

We're a fast-growing, profitable company building new ways for people and AI agents to access human expertise. We are headquartered in San Francisco, with offices in Brooklyn and Bangalore, and backed by leading marketplace investors and operators from companies like DoorDash, Airbnb, Pinterest, and Affirm.




WHAT WE BELIEVE

Human knowledge is the world's most valuable asset. Yet most of it remains inaccessible and underutilized.

We're building a world where anyone can get paid for what they know, and anyone can access trusted human expertise on demand. We believe great products can make this exchange effortless, creating more opportunities for experts and more valuable answers for the people who need them.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Product Manager, Growth who combines exceptional creativity with strong analytical instincts. We're open to candidates at both the Product Manager and Senior Product Manager levels, and care more about demonstrated ability, impact, and potential than years of experience or previous titles.

You'll help more people discover Office Hours, experience its value, and keep coming back. Initially, you'll focus on growing engagement across our expert network, improving everything from acquisition and onboarding to activation, retention, and repeat earning opportunities. Over time, your work may extend across both sides of our marketplace.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves understanding why people behave the way they do, identifying opportunities to accelerate growth, and turning ideas into measurable results. You'll partner closely with engineering, design, marketing, and operations to dig into data, form hypotheses, run experiments, and ship improvements that move the business forward.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Find opportunities for growth. Analyze user behavior, conversion funnels, and cohort data to identify friction, uncover insights, and prioritize the highest-impact opportunities.

 - Experiment relentlessly. Develop creative hypotheses, design experiments, measure results, and iterate quickly. Know when to run a rigorous A/B test and when a simpler experiment can help you learn faster.

 - Improve activation and engagement. Help more experts successfully onboard, discover relevant opportunities, earn their first dollar, and return regularly.

 - Build compounding growth loops. Explore new ways to drive acquisition, referrals, engagement, retention, and reactivation through product experiences that create lasting value.

 - Turn insights into shipped products. Work closely with engineering and design to prototype, build, launch, and refine solutions, balancing speed with a high standard for product quality.

 - Own outcomes, not output. Define clear success metrics, build dashboards, track performance, and use what you learn to continuously improve the product and our growth strategy.

 - Collaborate across the business. Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing, and Operations to connect growth initiatives with our broader company goals.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 3+ years of relevant professional experience in product management, growth, analytics, engineering, or a related field. We care more about demonstrated ability and impact than a specific career path.

 - Creative and quantitative instincts. You enjoy finding unconventional solutions to difficult problems and using data to understand whether they work.

 - A scientific mindset. You're naturally curious, comfortable forming and testing hypotheses, and willing to change your mind when the evidence suggests a better approach.

 - Strong analytical skills. You're comfortable working with funnels, conversion rates, cohorts, and product analytics tools, and can independently investigate problems using data.

 - A bias toward action. You're resourceful, proactive, and comfortable taking ideas from early exploration through execution without waiting for perfect information.

 - Strong product judgment. You care about the people using your product and understand that sustainable growth comes from delivering genuine value, not simply optimizing metrics.

 - Clear communication and collaboration. You can explain complex problems simply, bring people together around a solution, and take ownership of outcomes.




BONUS EXPERIENCE

 - Experience working on growth, activation, engagement, or retention at a consumer product, marketplace, or product-led software company.

 - Experience with experimentation platforms, SQL, PostHog, Metabase, or similar analytical tools.

 - Experience building products, prototypes, or side projects using AI-assisted development tools.

 - Entrepreneurial experience, whether founding a company, building an independent product, or leading a new initiative from scratch.




BENEFITS + PERKS

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Medical, dental, and vision coverage

 - 401(k)

 - Monthly wellness and fitness stipend

 - Flexible vacation time and company holidays

 - Annual company offsites

 - Flexible remote work policy

 - Paid parental leave




PAY TRANSPARENCY NOTICE

Full-time offers include base salary, equity, and benefits.

The expected base salary range for this role is $160,000–$220,000, depending on relevant experience, skills, and scope.

We're open to hiring at either the Product Manager or Senior Product Manager level and will calibrate title and compensation accordingly.

jobs.title: Regional Equipment & Fleet Maintenance Manager
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Regional Equipment & Fleet Maintenance Manager is responsible for leading the maintenance strategy, repair execution, compliance, reliability, and lifecycle support of company-owned, leased, and rented equipment and fleet assets across the assigned region. This position provides regional leadership for maintenance operations, mechanic resources, vendor partnerships, preventative maintenance programs, service standards, inspections, and asset readiness to ensure equipment and fleet assets remain safe, compliant, reliable, and available to support operations.

The Regional Equipment & Fleet Maintenance Manager reports directly to the National Equipment & Fleet Manager and works closely with the National Equipment & Fleet Financial Coordinator, area equipment and fleet managers, operations leadership, project teams, procurement, safety, and finance to reduce downtime, improve maintenance compliance, control repair costs, standardize maintenance practices, and strengthen equipment and fleet performance across the region.

Key Responsibilities

Regional Maintenance Program Leadership

• Lead regional maintenance programs for equipment and fleet assets across assigned areas, yards, shops, and active project locations.

• Develop, implement, and standardize preventative maintenance practices, inspection routines, service intervals, and repair workflows.

• Monitor equipment and fleet condition, readiness, reliability, downtime, and repair status across the region.

• Establish maintenance priorities that support safety, compliance, operational needs, and asset availability.

• Ensure maintenance records, service history, repair documentation, and inspection results are accurate and current in company systems.

• Drive consistent maintenance execution across regional locations and support continuous improvement in maintenance performance.

Repair Operations & Asset Readiness

• Coordinate regional repair planning, shop scheduling, field service support, and emergency breakdown response.

• Partner with area equipment and fleet managers to prioritize repairs based on operational impact, safety risk, project needs, and asset criticality.

• Ensure equipment and fleet assets are inspected, serviced, and ready for deployment, transfer, mobilization, and demobilization.

• Review recurring failures, high-cost repairs, downtime trends, and reliability concerns to identify corrective actions.

• Support root-cause analysis, repair-versus-replace recommendations, and lifecycle decisions for regional assets.

Maintenance & Compliance

• Ensure regional compliance with OSHA, DOT, manufacturer recommendations, company maintenance standards, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory requirements.

• Maintain oversight of annual inspections, DOT inspections, registrations, certifications, service documentation, and required compliance records.

• Partner with Safety and Operations to remove unsafe, non-compliant, or unreliable assets from service until corrective action is completed.

• Support incident investigations related to equipment or fleet condition, mechanical failure, or maintenance practices.

• Promote a maintenance culture focused on safe work practices, field accountability, and proactive risk reduction.

Financial Management

• Manage regional maintenance budgets, repair spend, parts costs, vendor costs, warranty recovery, and maintenance-related financial performance in close coordination with the National Equipment & Fleet Financial Coordinator.

• Monitor maintenance cost trends, downtime cost impacts, replacement needs, and high-cost assets.

• Identify opportunities to reduce repair costs through preventative maintenance, warranty utilization, vendor negotiation, improved diagnostics, and asset standardization.

• Support annual capital planning, major repair planning, disposal planning, and replacement forecasting.

• Provide financial and operational input for equipment acquisition, lifecycle planning, and fleet standardization decisions.

Vendor, Parts & Shop Coordination

• Oversee approved maintenance vendors, repair shops, mobile service providers, tire vendors, parts suppliers, and warranty service partners across the region.

• Establish service expectations, turnaround standards, documentation requirements, and vendor performance review practices.

• Coordinate parts availability, critical component planning, and shop support needs to reduce downtime and improve repair efficiency.

• Collaborate with Procurement, Operations, and Finance to support vendor selection, pricing controls, and maintenance service agreements.

• Evaluate vendor quality, responsiveness, cost performance, and compliance with company standards.

Team Leadership

• Lead, coach, and support regional maintenance personnel, base mechanics, field mechanics, shop personnel, fleet maintenance coordinators, and other assigned equipment and fleet maintenance resources.

• Set performance expectations, provide technical guidance, and support development of maintenance staff.

• Develop standard operating procedures, training materials, escalation practices, and process documentation for regional maintenance operations.

• Foster a culture of safety, accountability, responsiveness, technical excellence, and customer service to operations.

Technology & Reporting

• Utilize fleet management, equipment management, maintenance, telematics, and reporting platforms to monitor asset condition, preventative maintenance status, repair history, downtime, utilization, and operating performance.

• Generate regional maintenance reports, downtime reports, repair cost summaries, PM compliance reports, vendor performance reports, and asset reliability metrics.

• Analyze trends and recommend actions to improve uptime, maintenance compliance, cost control, safety, and asset lifecycle performance.

• Support implementation of new maintenance technology, telematics, inspection tools, and tracking solutions for equipment and fleet assets.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

The Regional Equipment & Fleet Maintenance Manager will be measured on:

• Preventative maintenance compliance

• Equipment and fleet uptime

• Downtime reduction and repair turnaround performance

• Maintenance cost performance and budget adherence

• Repair quality and repeat-failure reduction

• DOT, OSHA, inspection, and company compliance metrics

• Vendor performance and service response times

• Asset readiness and deployment support

• Maintenance record accuracy

• Customer satisfaction from operations and area leadership

Minimum Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor's Degree in Business, Construction Management, Equipment Management, Supply Chain, Logistics, or related field preferred.

• Or Equivalent industry experience may substitute for formal education.

Experience

• 7+ years of equipment, fleet, maintenance, heavy equipment repair, shop operations, or fleet operations experience.

• 3+ years of leadership, supervisory, or regional maintenance management experience preferred.

• Experience supporting construction, industrial, energy, utility, infrastructure, heavy equipment, or fleet-intensive operations.

• Experience managing preventative maintenance programs, repair planning, maintenance compliance, vendor relationships, and repair budgets.

• Proficiency with fleet/equipment management software, maintenance systems, telematics platforms, and reporting tools.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Strong understanding of equipment and fleet maintenance management, repair operations, diagnostics, preventative maintenance, and asset lifecycle planning.

• Knowledge of OSHA, DOT, fleet compliance, inspection requirements, and equipment safety standards.

• Ability to evaluate maintenance trends, downtime drivers, repair costs, and asset reliability data.

• Strong leadership, vendor management, financial, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent communication and organizational skills with the ability to support multiple areas, shops, yards, and project locations.

• Ability to manage competing priorities in a regional, multi-state operating environment.

• Advanced Microsoft Office, reporting, and data analysis capabilities.

Preferred Qualifications

• Certified Equipment Manager (CEM)

• Certified Fleet Manager (CFM)

• ASE certifications, manufacturer training, or heavy equipment technical certifications

• Lean, Six Sigma, or Continuous Improvement training

• Experience with telematics, maintenance management systems, ERP systems, or fleet platforms such as SAP, Oracle, Viewpoint, or similar systems

• Multi-site or multi-state regional maintenance leadership experience

Physical Requirements

• Ability to walk uneven terrain and inspect equipment.

• Occasional lifting up to 50 pounds.

• Ability to travel throughout assigned territory.

Benefits

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay

• Life and disability insurance

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

jobs.title: Digital Primary Care Physician (Pacific Time Zone, Evenings)
jobs.description:
About Us

Galileo is a team-based medical practice working to improve the quality and affordability of health care for all. Operating across 50 states, Galileo offers high-touch, data-driven, multi-specialty, longitudinal care to diverse and complex patients—on the phone, in the home, and everywhere in between. Regional and national health plans, employers, and Fortune 500 organizations trust Galileo as the leading solution to improve population health. Founded by Dr. Tom X. Lee, the healthcare pioneer behind One Medical and Epocrates, Galileo is a team of leading innovators from healthcare, technology, and human-centered design. Our mission is to apply that talent and scientific thinking to transform society by solving our largest, toughest healthcare problems, while at the same time bringing patient and provider closer.

About The Role

Galileo is looking for culturally sensitive clinicians to join our digital-first, primary care medical group. In this role, you will use asynchronous text-based chat and synchronous video to provide high-quality, comprehensive and evidence-based primary care. As a part of our collaborative clinical care team, you will leverage data, technology, and operational rigor to optimize great patient outcomes while offering highly personalized care and shared decision making with patients.

Here’s What You'll Do:

• Provide best-in-class care for Galileo patients managing complex and chronic illnesses through our innovative, proprietary app and technology and your excellent clinical judgment.

• Provide compassionate and empathetic care to patients from age 0-100 across all needs, including complex, chronic medical conditions such as: diabetes, hypertension, obesity and mental health.

• Work with a diverse patient population. We pride ourselves on fostering a culture that is inclusive of all backgrounds.

• Solve patient problems in an efficient, nimble manner by drawing on resourcefulness, collaborating with team members to leverage their expertise, and a “can-do” approach.

How We Work

Galileo is a 24/7 medical group utilizing asynchronous text-based chat and synchronous video to provide high-quality, comprehensive primary care. We work in 4-hour shifts (mornings, afternoons, evenings, overnight on weekdays and weekends) and require a minimum of 14 hours a week (alternating 12 and 16 hour weeks). At 24+ hours you will be considered full-time and benefits eligible. Providers are required to work at least two 4 hour shifts each weekend, in addition to their weekday hours.

We're currently hiring for a physician who is based in PST and can work evening hours on Saturdays and during the week.

Compensation:

$140/hour (regular rate) and $150/hour (premium rate)

About You

We look for passionate clinicians who are invested in solving complex problems that impact millions of lives and are excited about fixing what’s broken to improve care quality and health outcomes for everyone. We believe in a culture that fosters teamwork, excellence, and sound decision-making—one that is based on mutual respect and trust. We appreciate individuals who are open and honest about what they’re looking for so we can ensure it’s a fit on both sides.

We would love to hear from you if you have the following or equivalent experience:

• Have 4+ years of clinical experience post residency in complex care, chronic care management, or primary care.

• Are experienced in or have an appetite for learning digital-first healthcare (e.g. virtual medicine).

• Are interested in new, innovative models of care that balance evidence-based approaches with creative ideas.

• Are highly comfortable with using technology and various applications to deliver care to patients virtually. Our current tech stack is:

• Proprietary built clinician-patient platform

jobs.description:

Join NORY, the premier STEM camp provider in NYC and Boston, where we shape the future leaders, innovators, and problem-solvers. WE'RE SEEKING A ROCKSTAR SCHOOL BREAK DAY CAMP CODING LEAD TEACHER

Are you enthusiastic about inspiring young minds through coding and hands-on STEM experiences? We're looking for School Break Day Camp Coding Lead Teachers with demonstrated experience teaching coding to children. This is a part-time role for educators who can confidently lead coding lessons while creating a safe and memorable experience for our campers. You'll help campers ages 8-12 bring their ideas to life through Scratch-based coding, interactive games, and hands-on robotics projects using Arduino boards, sensors, and NORY's robotic systems. Beyond coding, you'll foster curiosity, creativity, and confidence as campers explore STEM in a fun and supportive environment.




WHY WORKING AS A CODING LEAD TEACHER ROCKS:

 - NORY Certification: Elevate your resume with our recognized STEM training program. Being NORY-certified offers a competitive edge in your future career pursuits in NYC's educational landscape.

 - Personal and Professional Development: Benefit from dedicated support from our educational team and camp leaders, who provide constructive coaching and positive reinforcement to foster both your personal and professional growth.

 - Rapid Advancement Opportunities: Our professional development pipeline is designed to quickly enhance your leadership skills and help you reach your full potential.

 - Memorable Experiences: At NORY, we're passionate about creating joyful and lasting memories for both our campers and staff. Join us for School Break Day Camps filled with fun, learning, and impactful experiences.




SCHOOL BREAK DAY CAMP CODING LEAD TEACHER RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Facilitate Coding Lessons: Lead engaging lessons using Scratch-based or comparable block-based programming tools. Help campers apply coding concepts to interactive games, robotic behaviors, and creative projects while explaining their thinking and testing their ideas.

 - Coach Engineering Projects: Guide campers as they connect code to hands-on inventions using Arduino boards, sensors, and NORY's robotic systems. Help them understand how inputs trigger programmed responses, troubleshoot code and hardware, and improve their designs.

 - Mentorship and Guidance: Lead campers through interactive coding and STEM activities, supporting both their educational and personal development.

 - Safety and Supervision: Maintain a safe and welcoming environment for all campers while adhering to camp safety guidelines.

 - Activity Coordination: Help organize and lead camp activities, ensuring each day is dynamic, engaging, and enriching for every camper.




SCHOOL BREAK DAY CAMP CODING LEAD TEACHER QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Experience with Children: You have 1+ years of experience working with children ages 8-12 and enjoy fostering their curiosity and creativity.

 - Coding Teaching Experience (Required): You have a strong track record of teaching coding to children and can share specific examples of lessons taught and student projects. You know how to make technical concepts clear, engaging, and accessible to learners with different experience levels.

 - Coding Instruction Skills (Required): You can confidently teach sequencing, loops, events, and conditional logic using Scratch or comparable block-based programming tools. You can adapt lessons for children ages 8-12, help campers debug their code, and guide them as they test and improve their projects.

 - Positive and Solution-Oriented: You maintain a positive outlook, always seeking solutions and welcoming constructive feedback to foster personal and professional growth.

 - Fun and Energetic: Your energetic and fun-loving nature matches the dynamism of our campers, creating an exciting and engaging learning environment.

 - Empathetic Mentor: You act as a role model, providing guidance and encouragement while fostering a supportive environment where children feel safe to explore, invent, and innovate.




JOIN OUR VISION:

If you're passionate about making a difference and ready to contribute to a team that values motivation, unity, empathy, and innovative problem-solving, we'd love to see how you align with our core values at https://www.nory.co/value/ https://www.nory.co/value/.




SCHOOL BREAK DAY CAMP CODING LEAD TEACHER COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

 - Schedule: Part-time, 7:30 AM - 12:15 PM on scheduled School Break Day Camp days throughout the school year. Coding instruction primarily takes place during the morning, with time within the shift for material setup, lesson preparation, camper arrival, and wrap-up. Camp dates and locations vary. Share your available school breaks when applying; you do not need to commit to every camp day.

 - Compensation: $30/hour.

 - Location: Manhattan and Brooklyn.




READY TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE?

To apply, please send your resume and a brief cover letter to Liza@nory.co. Describe your experience teaching coding to children, including the ages taught, programming tools used, and a specific lesson or student project you led. Please also include your availability for School Break Day Camps and any special reasons for wanting to join our team.




ADDITIONAL OPPORTUNITIES:

Beyond School Break Day Camps, NORY offers opportunities to stay involved year-round through summer camps, afterschool programs, birthday parties, and special events. These roles provide a unique opportunity to continue growing with our team, embrace our core values, and make a lasting impact on campers throughout the year.



NORY New York is a proud equal opportunity employer and values diversity at our company. We encourage applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other category protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

Tigard, OR - Bridgeport Village

At Rothy’s, we believe there’s a better way to do business—one that puts the planet and its people first. That’s why we’ve transformed millions of plastic bottles into stylish, sustainable shoes and bags, creating wardrobe staples that look just as good as they feel.

In our retail stores, clienteling, and genuine connection are at the heart of everything we do. As we grow, we’re cultivating not just a workplace, but a community. It’s a place where careers can grow, ideas are shared, and people feel a true sense of belonging. jobs.title: Partner Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About G2 - The Company


G2 is the world's largest and most trusted software marketplace. When you join G2, you’re joining the industry’s leading team that helps businesses reach their peak potential by powering decisions and strategies with trusted insights from real software users.



Now, we have joined forces with Capterra https://www.capterra.com/, SoftwareAdvice https://www.softwareadvice.com/, and GetApp https://www.getapp.com/ to create the largest source of online data and software insights to fuel intelligent buying in the age of AI. With 200M+ combined annual visitors and 6M verified reviews, we are now the centralized place to enable software buyers to make better and faster decisions with confidence.



And we are just getting started! We are setting out to transform the global B2B software industry and become the most trusted data foundation for buyers and sellers of software for the age of AI.



Does that sound exciting to you? Come join us as we try to reach our next PEAK!



About G2 - Our People



At G2, everything we are and what we do is grounded in our  PEAK values— (Performance + Entrepreneurship + Authenticity + Kindness. Working at G2 means you are part of a value-driven, growing global community that climbs PEAKs together. We cheer for each other’s successes, learn from our mistakes, and support and lean on one another during challenging times. With ambition and entrepreneurial spirit we push each other to take on challenging work, which will help us all to grow and learn.



You will be part of a global, diverse team of smart, dedicated, and kind individuals - each with unique talents, aspirations, and life experiences. At the heart of our community and culture are our people-led ERGs, which celebrate and highlight the diverse identities of our global team. As an organization, we are intentional about our DEI https://company.g2.com/dei and philanthropic work (like our G2 Gives https://company.g2.com/gives program) because it encourages us all to be better people.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The Partner Product Marketing Manager crafts the narrative for G2's partnerships and Buyer Intent product line, translating complex integrations into clear value propositions and sales enablement. Partnering closely with Product, Sales, and Partnerships, this role aligns market insights with product strategy to drive partner adoption and remove usage barriers.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: 

The Partner Product Marketing Manager works closely with Partnerships, Product, Sales, Marketing, and the Senior Partner Marketing Manager to translate complex technical integrations, data partnerships, and joint offerings into a clear “better together” story. The role helps define why G2 and a partner’s capabilities are more valuable together, the customer problems they solve, and the outcomes they enable.

This role is focused on our partners, along with our Buyer Intent product line. G2’s partnerships, including technology integrations, data relationships, and channel and ecosystem partners, are a growing way to put G2 buyer intent data in front of buyers inside the tools they already use. The Partner Product Marketing Manager owns customer and market insight, positioning, messaging, joint value propositions, and sales and partner enablement for G2’s partner offerings. This role also represents the voice of the customer to Partnerships and Product, helping those teams understand customer needs, adoption barriers, and opportunities.

You will work side by side with the Partnerships team, who own the relationships and deal structure, and with the Growth Marketing Senior Partner Marketer, who owns partnership marketing strategy and activation. You are the strategic and storytelling counterpart to both.



Partner go-to-market Strategy:

 - Develop and validate positioning, messaging, joint value propositions, and priority customer use cases for each partner offering.

 - Own messaging strategy and enablement readiness for partner-related feature  launches, and identify the core narrative, proof points, and sales materials required. Partner with the partner marketer on the marketing launch plan and with Product and Partnerships on offering readiness.

 - Assist Partnerships with prioritization by defining the market case for each partner (audience, differentiation, and expected customer value).

 - Draft workflow guides, technical docs, and setup resources with Partnership and Product teams, maintaining content ownership while technical leads validate accuracy.

 - Develop and maintain the core content G2 sellers and partner teams need to understand, position, sell, and promote our joint offerings, including joint value propositions, ‘better together’ narratives, pitch decks, one-pagers, FAQs, and materials.

 - Create content for partner audiences, such as partner sales teams, solutions engineers, and partner marketing contacts, not just G2’s own.

 - Keep all partner content consistent with G2’s brand voice and core Buyer Intent positioning.

 - Work with Sales Enablement to build and deliver internal and partner enablement: pitch guidance, battlecards, objection handling, integration use cases, and customer proof points.

 - Collaborate with the Senior Partner Marketing Manager, Growth Marketing, and Events to develop content and enablement for partner launches, training sessions, and G2’s presence at partner events.

 - Define positioning, messaging, customer evidence, and subject-matter content for partner events, making sure it ties back to the partner’s GTM strategy.

 - Manage Partnerfleet and product messaging across partner pages, marketplace listings, and docs. Set listing standards, assist partners with G2 pages, and keep resources up to date.

Supporting Buyer Intent  and other Partner Launches:

 - Define the target customer profile, messaging, and positioning for Buyer Intent features and other partner-based features across the full suite to differentiate our offering in the market.

 - Develop comprehensive GTM launch plans across all customer-facing channels, aligning product messaging with key buyer pain points

 - Own positioning, messaging, customer use-case validation, and sales and partner enablement for each data-enabled partner offering. Equip the partner marketer to develop the marketing launch and activation plan that best addresses the customer's pain points and market opportunity.

 - Work with Buyer Intent Product and Partnerships to determine how G2 buyer intent data can power a partner’s platform or workflow, and which use cases create the most customer value.

 - Translate that data connection into a clear story for the partner’s customers and for G2’s sellers: what the data is, how it shows up in the partner’s product, and what outcome it drives.

Customer, Sales, and Market Insight:

 - Establish an ongoing feedback loop through customer interviews, sales conversations, win/loss analysis, partner feedback, and competitive research.

 - Analyze partner adoption data and cross-functional feedback with Product, Partnerships, and CS to identify usage barriers. Use these insights to optimize onboarding, enablement, and joint adoption programs.

 - Synthesize unmet needs, objections, adoption barriers, and emerging use cases into recommendations for Partnerships and Product. Track how those insights inform offering development, prioritization, positioning, and enablement.

 - Define success metrics for partner launches and events, such as partner-enabled use-case adoption, enablement usage, partner activation, and message resonance, and report learnings to Partnerships, Product, and Growth Marketing.




MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

We realize applying for jobs can feel daunting at times. Even if you don’t check all the boxes in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. 

 -  5+ years in product marketing, partner marketing, or a closely related GTM role, ideally in B2B SaaS or data and intent products.

 - Experience building go-to-market strategies and launching offerings with technology, data, or channel partners.

 - Strong writing skills, with the ability to create clear, persuasive content for external partner audiences as well as internal teams.

 - Ability to translate data-driven products into clear customer value.

 - Proven ability to build sales and partner enablement that gets used.

 - Excellent cross-functional collaboration with Partnerships, Product, Sales, and Marketing, and comfort working through influence rather than direct authority.




WHAT CAN HELP YOUR APPLICATION STAND OUT:

 - Familiarity with buyer intent data, sales and marketing technology ecosystems, or ABM and revenue platforms.

 - Experience in a data-licensing, integration-heavy, or ecosystem-driven business.

 - Experience managing sales enablement libraries, partner directories, or web content using platforms such as Highspot and  Partnerfleet.

 - Experience creating interactive demos, recorded walkthroughs, or visual explainers for technical offerings is a plus.

 - Comfort with CRM, enablement, and analytics tools.



Our Commitment to Inclusivity and Diversity



At G2, we are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where people of every background can thrive and feel welcome. We consider applicants without regard to race, color, creed, religion, national origin, genetic information, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, or marital, veteran, or physical or mental disability status. jobs.title: Principal - Accounting Platform
jobs.description:
BitGo (NYSE: BTGO) is the digital asset infrastructure company delivering custody, wallets, staking, trading, financing, stablecoins, and settlement services from regulated cold storage. Since 2013, BitGo has focused on accelerating the transition of the financial system to a digital asset economy. BitGo maintains a global presence and multiple regulated entities, including BitGo Bank & Trust, National Association, the first federally chartered digital asset trust bank owned by a publicly traded company. Today, BitGo serves thousands of institutions, including many of the industry's top brands, financial institutions, exchanges, and platforms, and millions of investors worldwide. For more information, visit www.bitgo.com.

This role requires being full-time onsite at our NY, NY office to support collaborative team dynamics and innovative problem-solving.

If you have spent your career in SOX, internal controls, audit, controllership, or financial close, and you want to build the systems that fix what you find instead of only testing them, this role is for you.

Why this role exists

Every product BitGo ships eventually becomes a number: a balance, a fee, a statement, a journal entry, a regulatory filing. As a public company and a federally chartered trust bank, we have to prove those numbers are right every period, across many products, legal entities, and jurisdictions.

You will own the product strategy for the financial and accounting platform that makes those numbers right by construction, as we add products, entities, and asset types. You will turn accounting requirements into scalable, auditable, self-service platform capabilities that product, engineering, finance, and compliance can build on.

Digital assets make this harder, and more interesting, than it is at a traditional bank. On chain activity, custody structures, staking, tokenized assets, and settlement each move through our systems differently, and each has to land correctly on the books. The industry is still writing the playbook for much of this. You will help write it.

Level

We are hiring at Senior or Principal level, depending on experience. The core scope is the same at both. At Principal, you have already set platform strategy, led accounting systems, or established control standards that multiple teams adopted, and you will own the crossproduct standards and the working relationship with finance and audit leadership with more independence from day one.

Two paths to this role

There is more than one way to be great at this job. You may come from product management and built financial compliance platforms. You may come from audit, controllership, or accounting systems and have spent years finding where numbers break, and then built the thing that fixed it. We are just as interested in the second group. If you are an auditor or accountant with a builder mindset, you will be evaluated on the same scope and the same bar as a product manager. What matters is that you have shipped: tools, automation, control frameworks, or systems that other teams adopted and kept using.

What you will own

• The financial data and accounting platform roadmap: Define and deliver the shared capabilities that make financial data trustworthy by construction: ledger and sub-ledger integrity, balance and activity reconciliation, fee and revenue calculation, client reporting, and the feeds into the general ledger and the financial close.

• Controls built into the product: Partner with finance, internal audit, and external auditors to turn SOX and internal control requirements into product capabilities instead of manual procedures. When a control needs a build, you own the requirements, the plan, and the timeline, delivered in step with the audit calendar.

• Platform standards across products and entities: Make sure new products, new asset types, new legal entities, and acquisitions plug into the platform instead of creating bespoke accounting workarounds. You set the standards, interfaces, and data contracts that product teams build against.

• Regulatory and audit readiness: Work with compliance, legal, and risk so the platform supports regulatory reporting, books-and-records requirements, and examiner and auditor requests. You run dated plans against external deadlines and flag early when a timeline is at risk.

• Close, reporting, and operational efficiency: Reduce the manual effort, elapsed time, and risk in month-end and quarter-end close. Establish the metrics that show whether the platform is working: reconciliation breaks, close duration, audit adjustments, manual journal volume, and time to onboard a new product.

What success looks like in the first two quarters

• A documented map of how each major product's financial activity reaches the general ledger, with manual steps and gaps identified and prioritized.

• A dated platform roadmap agreed with finance, engineering, and compliance, with external deadlines (audit, regulatory, and reporting) built into the plan.

• One high-impact capability shipped end to end, such as automated reconciliation for a key product, that measurably reduces manual work or control risk.

Who you will partner with

• Finance and Accounting leadership own accounting policy and judgment. You translate their requirements into platform capabilities and make the product the system of record.

• Engineering leadership owns architecture, estimates, and delivery. You partner on sequencing, platform design, and tradeoffs without positional authority. Product Managers across Custody, Trading, Staking, and Financing need the platform to support their products without becoming a bottleneck.

• Compliance, Legal, and Risk own regulatory judgment. You build the delivery process behind it.

• Internal and external audit rely on you to plan control-related work clearly and deliver it on schedule.

• Commercial and client teams need accurate statements, reporting, and billing that clients can trust.

What we're looking for

• 6+ years of experience (typically 9+ for Principal) building or scaling systems, platforms, tooling, or control frameworks that multiple internal or external teams relied on, including 3+ years as the owner. You might have done this as a product manager, or from audit, controllership, or accounting systems. At Principal, you have set strategy or standards that other teams adopted.

• An accounting or finance foundation: a CPA or equivalent, an accounting degree, or hands-on experience in financial reporting, audit, controllership, or accounting systems. You can read a trial balance, follow a journal entry through a ledger, and discuss revenue recognition or reconciliation with a controller without a translator.

• Experience building scalable platforms such as ledgers, billing, payments, reporting, data infrastructure, reconciliation tooling, or controls automation. You think in data models, interfaces, and reuse, and you know when a one-off fix will cost us later. If you come from audit or accounting, this may look like automating reconciliations, building controls into a system, or designing data models and tooling with engineers, rather than a formal product title.

• Experience in a regulated financial environment. You have worked with auditors, examiners, SOX controls, or control programs, and you understand how public company obligations change how products are built and shipped.

• Technical credibility with Engineers. You can follow an architecture discussion, pressure-test an estimate, and write precise requirements for data-heavy systems. Familiarity with SQL and financial data pipelines is a plus.

• Crypto or digital-asset experience is a requirement. If you do not have professional experience, passion projects with breadth and depth across digital assets could be a good fit.

• A writing-first approach: your default artifacts are clear specs, data flow maps, and decision documents.

What will make you fail here

• Building bespoke solutions for each product or blockchain instead of platform capabilities that scale.

• Needing positional authority to get things done. Engineering, finance, and compliance sit on separate reporting lines, and you will coordinate across all three every day. You need to find ways to unblock yourself.

• Optimizing for process over outcomes. We have little patience for ceremony. Here, a control built into the product is an outcome; a new manual review step usually isn't.

Why Join BitGo?

Disrupting an industry takes vision, innovation, passion, technical chops, drive to deliver, collaboration, and execution. Join a team of great people who strive for excellence and personify our corporate values of ownership, craftsmanship, and open communication. We are looking for new colleagues who bring innovative ways of thinking and problem-solving, and who want risks to be part of the team that changes the world’s financial markets.

• Competitive base salary, bonus, and stock options

• 100% company-paid health insurance for employee, partner, and dependents

• Up to 4% 401k company match

• Paid parental leave, Paid vacation

• Free commuter/parking pass

• Free custom lunches and snacks

• Computer equipment and workplace furniture to suit your needs

• Great colleagues and an inspiring environment

Benefits may vary based on location.

Pay Transparency Notice:

Depending upon your leveling and location, the compensation for this role averages between $230,000 and $260,000 USD base salary. Equity, an annual performance bonus, and the benefits outlined above are also part of this role’s package.

Cryptocurrencies are the most disruptive change the financial services industry has seen in years. Join us and you'll be able to look back and say you were part of the team that transformed investing.

jobs.title: Test Engineer
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.



The Role

Test Engineering is a brand new team at Hadrian, built from the ground up with no legacy test framework to work around. As a Test Engineer, you'll be the responsible engineer and technical lead for all proof and functional testing on a large manufacturing program for complex weldments.

You'll set the test strategy for the program and decide what we test, how, and why. You'll use engineering first principles to decide which requirements we meet, exceed, or push back on, and you'll make the calls on cost, schedule, quality, and safety. You'll lead the design of the test equipment, make sure every test is safe, and coordinate the engineers and technicians who build and run it. You'll be on the floor for first articles, hand each test off to production, and set the standards the team carries to the next program.

The program is in its development phase today, and scope will grow as it moves into production. Many of the test capabilities will take 6 to 12 months to build, so the work you do now shapes how the factory runs later. If you like building a test program from an empty floor, leading through your expertise, and owning the outcome, this role is for you.



What You’ll Do

 - Own the test strategy and test plan for every program requirement, from customer spec to final data package

 - Interpret customer test specs, and negotiate changes when you disagree

 - Lead the selection, purchase, and integration of hydrostatic, proof, and functional test equipment into the work center. Design custom pressure systems, fixtures, and data acquisition when nothing off the shelf fits.

 - Own test safety: hazard analysis, stored energy calculations, and engineering controls for every test you stand up

 - Set the data collection, labeling, storage, and traceability requirements for program testing, and work with our controls, software, and data teams to build the tools

 - Write test automation, process plans, work orders, and training materials, and set the standard the rest of the team follows

 - Hand each test off to production with clear accept/reject criteria and trained technicians

 - Deliver a complete test data package to the customer showing compliance with every agreed requirement

 - Lead customer reviews and witness tests

 - Mentor engineers and technicians on pressure testing, test design, and safety

 - Work with build engineering, factory automation, factory planning, production, and workforce training to keep testing in step with the build. The line should never be waiting on a test result.



What We’re Looking For

 - Bachelor's degree in mechanical, electrical, aerospace, or chemical engineering

 - 5+ years in test, launch, controls, integration, or fluid systems engineering

 - Deep pressure test experience. You've planned, run, and signed off on hydrostatic or proof tests on large, complex hardware.

 - Strong command of pressure system design: P&IDs, relief sizing, stored energy, and codes like ASME BPVC Section VIII, B31.3, and PCC-2

 - Experience specifying, installing, and commissioning test equipment and data acquisition systems (NI, Dewesoft, HBK, or similar)

 - Test automation in Python, LabVIEW, or similar

 - A record of leading test programs or cross-functional projects from start to finish
