jobs.title: Principal Research Scientist I
jobs.description:
AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through Early-Stage Clinical Development.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.

Position Description:

For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.

The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.

This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.

Responsibilities:

• Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
• Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
• Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
• Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
• Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.
• Design and deliver intuitive applications, dashboards, reports, and automated workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and enable scientists to obtain timely insights from their data.
• Mentor, guide, and develop data scientists and scientific colleagues; provide technical coaching, peer review, and hands-on support, and create learning opportunities that strengthen data literacy and analytical capability across the organization.
• Lead or coordinate a portfolio of data science initiatives, establish priorities and delivery plans, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, value, and recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.
• Establish and promote standards for analytical data assessment, model validation, software development, documentation, version control, testing, data governance, and sustainable solution support.
• Build and foster a global network with Analytical R&D, Development Sciences, statistics, enterprise data science, IT, and external partners; connect teams to the appropriate expertise and facilitate effective cross-functional execution.
• Identify high-value opportunities, generate new scientific proposals, evaluate emerging AI/ML and digital technologies, and champion responsible innovation that advances scientific understanding, development speed, quality, and operational efficiency.
• Communicate complex methods and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences through decision-focused presentations, reports, visualizations, and scientific publications where appropriate.
• Ensure solutions and activities comply with applicable safety, quality, regulatory, data-integrity, privacy, security, and AbbVie requirements.

• Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Chemometrics, Computational Science, Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline, typically with a minimum of 14 years (BS), 12 years (MS), or 6 years (Ph.D.) of relevant industry experience.
• Demonstrated experience applying data science, AI/ML, statistics, or advanced analytics to scientific, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or other complex R&D problems.
• Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R and strong working knowledge of relevant data-science libraries, statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, and reproducible analytical workflows.
• Experience integrating, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing complex and heterogeneous data; working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, APIs, and modern data-management practices.
• Demonstrated ability to build and deliver production-quality analytical applications, dashboards, automated workflows, or reusable data products. Experience with tools such as Streamlit, Shiny, cloud platforms, workflow automation, or equivalent technologies is desirable.
• Strong understanding of model development and evaluation, experimental design, uncertainty, validation, interpretability, and the limitations and appropriate use of AI/ML methods.
• Demonstrated leadership through mentoring, technical direction, project or portfolio leadership, influence across functions, and delivery of complex initiatives. Prior direct people-management experience is beneficial but not required.
• Proven ability to partner with domain scientists, quickly learn scientific workflows, translate ambiguous needs into tractable analytical problems, and balance technical rigor with practical, fit-for-purpose delivery.
• Experience with software-development practices such as Git/version control, modular coding, testing, documentation, code review, deployment, and lifecycle management.
• Excellent analytical problem-solving, project-management, written and oral communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to diverse audiences.
• Self-motivated, collaborative, and adaptable, with demonstrated scientific curiosity, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
• Knowledge of pharmaceutical development, CMC, analytical laboratory workflows, regulated environments, data integrity, or scientific data standards is strongly preferred.
• Experience with computational chemistry and molecular modeling approaches to investigate molecular properties, structure–property relationships, or other scientific questions relevant to pharmaceutical development is desirable.

Applicable only to applicants applying to a position in any location with pay disclosure requirements under state or local law: ​

Individual compensation paid within this range will depend on many factors including geographic location, and we may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. ​

jobs.title: Hospital Manager- Sugar Land, TX
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

As a Hospital Manager, you’ll guide your people and operate your hospital the VEG Way, with a strong sense of ownership and the freedom to shape an environment constantly on the frontlines of change. You’ll be a constant presence in your hospitals, advancing culture, engagement, efficiency, growth, and financial health by finding ways to say yes to your VEGgies—equipping them with the tools, support, education, and autonomy they need to thrive. Using the VEG framework to guide your decisions, you’ll ensure your hospital performs at the highest level, while fostering an inclusive workplace where VEGgies feel they belong, take pride in their roles, and invite friends to join. You’ll also build collaborative, mutually rewarding partnerships with referring vets and local businesses, making VEG the go-to for emergency pet care in your community.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Actively recruit, hire, onboard and continuously develop the right people for VEG and your hospital

• Ensure your hospital delivers a mind-blowing experience for patients, customers, and VEGgies at your hospital

• Ensure your hospital is compliant, well-maintained, and operationally sound

• Drive performance at your hospital, making it a high-revenue, high-margin business that challenges the status quo and achieves financial targets

• Help grow VEG’s reputation locally and throughout the industry, online, and in the media

WHAT YOU NEED

• Leadership experience, including overseeing and scheduling teams of 50+, recruiting, training, facilitating developmental meetings, performance management, and building effective teams

• Financial management experience, including full P&L oversight consisting of budgeting, payroll, and accounts receivable

• Operations management experience, including inventory and facility management

• A desire to be coached and develop personally

• When on the floor, you're consistently available, accessible, and approachable; this is not a remote position

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors

• Availability to work nights, weekends and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Competitive compensation, including base and 401K match

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Clinical student loan repayment so you don’t need to worry about your student debt

• Paid parental leave, up to 12 weeks at 100% of regular salary and inclusive fertility and family-building care for all types of families

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

• Generous employee referral program, so our awesome people can bring in more awesome people

• And the little (big) things, like comfy scrubs, cool VEG swag, and food in the fridge for when you’re hungry

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

You take pride in keeping things clean, organized, and on time so patients and customers get high-quality products when they need them.

jobs.description:
Datavant is the data collaboration platform trusted for healthcare. Guided by our mission to make the world’s health data secure, accessible and actionable, we provide critical data solutions for organizations across the healthcare ecosystem - including providers, health plans, researchers, and life sciences companies. From fulfilling a single patient’s request for their medical records to powering the AI revolution in healthcare, Datavanters are building the future of how data is connected and used to improve health.

By joining Datavant today, you’re stepping onto a driven and highly collaborative team that is passionate about creating transformative change in healthcare.

The Vice President, Service Delivery is a regional operational leader responsible for delivery excellence across multiple markets and teams. This leader drives regional KPIs—including TAT, OTD, quality, productivity, and staffing—and is accountable for implementing standardized workflows across all assigned sites. The VP partners with Workforce Planning, NOC, Training, and Implementation to ensure strong operational execution and readiness for new processes and tools. This role manages Managers and Supervisors and plays a critical part in scaling high-performing operations across the region.

You will:

• Lead regional operations across multiple markets, Managers, Supervisors, and frontline + Global staff

• Own regional KPI performance, including TAT, OTD, quality, productivity, and standardization

• Ensure adherence to standardized workflows and compliance requirements across all sites

• Partner with Workforce Management (WFM) to forecast labor needs and ensure appropriate staffing

• Interpret regional KPI trends and create action plans to improve performance

• Lead regional continuous improvement initiatives and support transformation pilots

• Respond to operational escalations routed through Account Management

• Partner cross-functionally with Network Operations Center (NOC), Training, Implementation, and Product teams

• Coach and develop Managers and emerging leaders within the region

• Drive adoption of digital and global workflows across operational teams

• Design and evolve the service delivery operating model to support business growth and client expectations

• Lead large-scale delivery transformations, including standardization, automation and technology enablement

• Ensure delivery capabilities scale without linear increases in cost or headcount

• Partner closely with Account Management, Go-To-Market, Product and Compliance

• Review, assess and provide resolution to all negative and neutral customer services surveys.

• Analyze monthly regional budgeting and accounting reports to include Cognos to maintain adherence to annual budget and expenditure controls with emphasis on sales, compensation and site performance.

• Analyze reports to ensure appropriate monitoring of financial performance and quality and explain any variances in financial data.

• Oversee employee management to include, hiring, training, motivating, coaching, developing, disciplining, and terminating of associates within the reporting structure.

Success Metrics

• Consistent achievement of SLA’s, quality and cost targets

• Improved delivery scalability and operational leverage

• Successful execution of transformation initiatives

• Strong engagement and retention

What you will bring to the table:

• Significant experience leading multi-site healthcare or large-scale operations teams

• Strong leadership capabilities with the ability to develop leader-of-leaders

• Fluency in operational KPIs and data-driven decision making Experience leading compliance-driven, standardized workflows

• Ability to manage change and scale new processes across diverse teams

• Strong collaboration skills across cross-functional partners

Bonus points if:

• You have experience in HIM, ROI, or similar regulated operational environments You have experience leading transformation or standardization programs

• You have Lean/Six Sigma background

jobs.title: Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer
jobs.description:
Renesas is seeking a Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer to join our team developing complex power management SoCs. These products integrate digital control, telemetry, fault management, communication interfaces, configurable peripherals, and advanced power-control functions for AI, datacenter, enterprise computing, networking, and high-performance power delivery applications.

You will independently own verification of significant blocks and features from planning through closure. The role combines hands-on UVM development, coverage-driven verification, complex debug, and close collaboration with architecture, RTL design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Responsibilities

• Own verification of complex digital blocks or major SoC features from requirements analysis through coverage closure.

• Develop feature-based verification plans from product, architecture, and microarchitecture specifications; identify gaps, ambiguities, corner cases, and risks.

• Build and extend reusable SystemVerilog/UVM environments, including sequences, monitors, scoreboards, checkers, assertions, and coverage models.

• Develop constrained random and targeted tests for normal operation, error handling, recovery, and system-level interactions.

• Drive functional, code, toggle, FSM, and assertion coverage closure using regression and coverage data.

• Debug RTL, testbench, assertion, integration, and regression failures; collaborate with design and firmware teams to isolate issues and verify fixes.

• Automate regression, triage, reporting, and analysis workflows using scripting and modern engineering tools.

• Communicate status, risks, dependencies, and closure evidence clearly; provide technical guidance to less-experienced engineers.

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

• 4 or more years of relevant digital design verification experience, or equivalent directly applicable experience.

• Demonstrated ownership of a complex block, subsystem, or major feature from verification planning through closure.

• Strong proficiency in SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained random verification, functional coverage, and SystemVerilog Assertions.

• Experience translating specifications into test plans, test scenarios, checkers, scoreboards, assertions, coverage models, and closure criteria.

• Hands-on experience developing and debugging reusable UVM environments and analyzing complex regression failures.

• Strong RTL and testbench debug skills, with the ability to distinguish design, environment, test, firmware, and specification issues.

• Working knowledge of digital design fundamentals, including state machines, clocks and resets, interrupts, register interfaces, memories, and clock-domain crossings.

• Proficiency in Linux and at least one scripting language such as Python, Bash, Perl, or Tcl.

• Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across architecture, design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience verifying complex SoCs, power management ICs, voltage regulators, digital controllers, or mixed-signal products.

• Experience verifying RTL interfaces to embedded processors, memory-mapped peripherals, and firmware-controlled hardware features.

• Familiarity with PMBus, AVSBus, SVID or SVI3, I2C, SPI, or similar control and communication protocols.

• Understanding of telemetry, fault and alert handling, power sequencing, multiphase regulation, or digital control loops.

• Experience with Cadence Xcelium, SimVision, vManager, JasperGold, Synopsys VCS, Verdi, or comparable tools.

• Experience with formal verification, gate-level simulation, silicon bring-up, or pre-silicon-to-silicon correlation.

• Experience improving regression infrastructure, coverage analytics, failure triage, or verification automation.

What You Bring

• Strong technical ownership and a disciplined approach to verification completeness.

• Ability to reason beyond directed requirements and identify meaningful corner cases and feature interactions.

• Clear communication of technical risk, progress, and signoff evidence.

• A collaborative mindset and interest in improving verification methodology and productivity.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. jobs.title: Staff Quality Control (QC) Engineer
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.




OVERVIEW

Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power and infrastructure are the bottlenecks.

As a Senior Staff Quality Control (QC) Engineer, you will be the senior technical authority for construction quality across Crusoe's mission-critical data center campus. You will own the site-level quality strategy and set the standards, processes, and expectations that general contractors, trade partners, and internal teams execute against — from design review and equipment manufacturing through installation, inspection, commissioning readiness, and final turnover.

This is a high-impact, field-based leadership role at the intersection of construction, MEP systems, engineering, supply chain, and commissioning. You will lead through influence, mentor QC engineers and inspectors, and shape how Crusoe builds quality into its programs as we scale — because at our scale, quality directly drives uptime, performance, speed to power, and long-term reliability.

 

What You'll Be Working On

 - Own and lead the site-level QA/QC program for large-scale, mission-critical data center construction, serving as the senior technical authority on quality for the campus

 - Author, implement, and continuously improve the Site-Level Quality Management Plan, ensuring alignment with Crusoe's enterprise quality standards and contractual requirements

 - Define the standard for Inspection Test Plans, checklists, hold/witness points, and inspection workflows across all scopes; review and approve contractor ITPs and quality plans

 - Lead and perform complex field inspections across civil, structural, electrical, mechanical, controls, and commissioning-related scopes, with deep emphasis on critical MEP systems (medium/low-voltage distribution, switchgear, UPS, generators, liquid and air cooling, and controls)

 - Influence quality upstream by participating in design, constructability, and submittal reviews to identify quality and reliability risks before they reach the field

 - Partner with supply chain and OEMs on equipment quality, including factory acceptance testing (FAT), factory witness tests, source inspections, and receiving inspections for long-lead and critical equipment

 - Audit general contractor and subcontractor quality management systems; drive corrective action and hold partners accountable to contractual quality requirements, escalating when necessary

 - Lead coordination with AHJs and third-party special inspectors on code compliance, inspection sign-offs, and documentation requirements

 - Own the deficiency, punch list, and non-conformance (NCR) process through closure, including disposition of complex or high-risk NCRs in partnership with engineering

 - Partner with commissioning leadership to define and drive pre-functional and functional readiness criteria (L1–L5) and ensure systems enter commissioning with minimal rework

 - Lead structured root cause analysis (RCA, 5-Why, 8D, fishbone) for significant defects, failed inspections, and recurring issues, and ensure corrective and preventive actions are implemented and sustained

 - Establish quality KPIs and dashboards (first-time quality, NCR aging, rework rates, inspection pass rates) and use data and defect trends to drive measurable improvement

 - Capture and share lessons learned across Crusoe's portfolio, contributing to enterprise quality standards, templates, and specifications for future sites

 - Mentor and develop QC engineers, inspectors, and field teams, raising the technical bar and building a culture of quality ownership

 - Ensure turnover documentation — test reports, as-builts, O&M manuals, and quality records — is complete, accurate, and audit-ready

 - Communicate quality status, risks, and trends to project and executive leadership, escalating early to protect schedule, commissioning, turnover, and operations

 

What Success Looks Like

 - The site quality program is clearly defined, consistently executed, and recognized as a model for other Crusoe sites

 - Critical MEP systems enter commissioning ready, with measurable reductions in rework, failed tests, and late-stage defects

 - Quality issues are caught upstream — in design review, at the factory, or at receiving — rather than in the field

 - Contractors and trade partners consistently meet Crusoe's quality standards, with clear accountability and closed-loop corrective actions

 - Deficiencies, punch items, and NCRs are closed promptly, with quality KPIs trending in the right direction

 - Turnover documentation is complete, accurate, and audit-ready on first submission

 - Leadership has clear, data-driven visibility into quality status, risk, and readiness

 - Lessons learned are captured and adopted into enterprise standards, reducing repeat issues across the portfolio

 - QC team members grow in technical capability and ownership under your mentorship

 

Who You Are

 - 10+ years of experience in construction QA/QC, quality engineering, field engineering, or commissioning, including significant time leading quality on large-scale, mission-critical projects

 - Deep technical expertise in MEP systems, including medium- and low-voltage electrical distribution, critical power, mechanical/cooling systems, and controls

 - Proven track record building, owning, and improving site-level quality programs, QMPs, and ITPs on complex, multi-contractor projects

 - Extensive experience with field inspections, punch walks, NCR disposition, deficiency tracking, and contractor quality audits

 - Expert ability to read and interpret drawings, specifications, submittals, test reports, and applicable codes and standards (e.g., NEC, NETA, NFPA, IBC)

 - Demonstrated experience leading commissioning readiness, system turnover, and closeout on mission-critical facilities

 - Experience leading structured root cause analysis and driving sustained corrective and preventive actions

 - Ability to lead through influence and hold general contractors, subcontractors, and vendors accountable without direct authority

 - Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to translate field quality data into clear risk and business impact for leadership

 - Data-driven mindset with experience defining quality metrics and using trends to drive continuous improvement

 - Experience mentoring and developing quality engineers, inspectors, or field teams

 - Strong ownership mentality, sound judgment, and the confidence to make and defend difficult quality calls in the field

 

Nice to Have

 - Data center, hyperscale, or AI infrastructure construction experience at multi-hundred-MW scale

 - Experience in complex construction environments such as semiconductor, healthcare, refinery, central plants, power generation, substations, or heavy industrial infrastructure

 - Experience with equipment manufacturing quality, factory acceptance testing, or supplier quality management

 - Experience building or scaling a quality program across multiple sites or a portfolio of projects

 - Familiarity with Procore, BIM360, Autodesk Build, Bluebeam, or similar construction management platforms

 - Relevant certifications such as ASQ CQE, CQM/OE, CQI, CQA, NETA, PMP, or similar

 - Experience with electrical, mechanical, controls, or integrated systems testing (IST) documentation

 

Additional Expectations

 - Willingness to be on-site full-time in Amarillo, TX

 - Ability to work closely with field teams, trade partners, OEMs, and commissioning teams in active construction environments

 - Ability to hold contractors and vendors accountable to quality standards, including escalation when necessary

 - Occasional travel to manufacturer facilities for factory testing and source inspections, and to other Crusoe sites as needed

 - Commitment to maintaining high standards in safety, quality, documentation, and execution

 

 - Benefits:

 - Competitive compensation and equity packages

 - Restricted Stock Units

 - Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

 - Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

 - Employer contributions to HSA account

 - Paid parental leave

 - Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

 - Professional development & tuition reimbursement

 - Mental health & wellness support

 - Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

 - Cell phone stipend

 - 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

 - Volunteer time off

 - Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

 - Daily meals allowance

 - Additional perks & programs specific to location

 


COMPENSATION RANGE

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000 – $215,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

 

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

jobs.title: Parts Counterperson - North Central Ford
jobs.description:
Purpose:

The Parts Counterperson sells, at retail, parts to all available customers, over the counter, through the shop, or on the phone.

Duties and Responsibilities:

• Assist walk-in customers in selecting required parts, suggest companion requirements, offer specials, and ensure exposure to the full product line.
• Pull purchases from stock, determine availability, and submit emergency orders as requested by customers.
• Answer phone calls, provide price quotes and information, and assist outside sales representatives with their orders.
• Set up orders for daily shipment, delivery, or pick up.
• Verify "will call" and "back order" files weekly; return items to vendors or stock as appropriate and solicit assigned accounts by phone.
• Assist service technicians in selecting parts needed for repairs and open repair order envelopes for new orders.
• Order parts not in stock after discussion with Shop Foremen to ensure parts will be used upon receipt or customer will return for repairs.
• Process all parts charges, returns, and credits, ensuring proper documentation, approvals, and customer payments including cash accounts, credit cards, and tax-exempt sales.
• Replenish assigned inventory daily and maintain clean, organized counter areas; advise Parts Manager of departmental concerns.
• Follow all company safety policies and procedures; immediately report any accidents to a manager or supervisor.

• High school diploma or equivalent.
• One year of experience in an automotive parts department.
• One year of sales experience.
• Ability to read, comprehend, and communicate information clearly.
• Professional personal appearance and willingness to wear a dealership uniform.
• Strong customer service skills with ability to manage multiple customers simultaneously.
• Authorization to work in the USA and valid driver's license.

It's time to make the most important move of your career.  From our cooperative team-based approach; to our more than 1,000 internal advancements each year, it's easy to see the difference. When you join our organization, you'll enjoy comprehensive training, competitive compensation, and unparalleled benefits. Simply put, you'll experience the best that a career in the automotive industry has to offer.

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: (Senior) Applications Engineer
jobs.description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Vertical Semiconductor, a venture-backed MIT spin-out, is leading the development of vertical gallium nitride (GaN) power semiconductors to build the foundational power layer for the next generation of compute and AI.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re hiring a (Senior) Applications Engineer to help customers design in next-generation vertical GaN power devices (100 V – 2300 V) and turn device performance into system-level wins. This is a hands-on role: you’ll build and test power converter hardware, run simulations, characterize fast-switching wide bandgap devices on the bench and support customers directly.

You’ll work closely with our Principal Applications Engineer and Device Engineering team, with growing ownership of customer engagements, evaluation hardware and technical content as you ramp up.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Customer design-in support

 - Support customer design-in activity: simulations, bench testing, troubleshooting and performance optimization.

 - Translate customer specifications into device and circuit requirements, working alongside senior applications staff on strategic accounts.

 - Take technical ownership of selected customer engagements; present results and recommendations to customers.

Simulation and modeling

 - Build and run SPICE and/or PLECS simulations of vertical GaN in realistic converter environments (switching behavior, parasitics, loss/thermal estimation, gate-drive tradeoffs).

 - Correlate simulation with bench measurements and help maintain the team’s library of reusable models and topology templates.

Evaluation hardware and reference designs

 - Contribute to evaluation boards, demo boards and reference designs: schematic/layout, BOM, bring-up, test plans and characterization reports.

 - Perform system-level bench testing and debug, and propose design optimizations based on measured performance.

High-voltage WBG bench characterization

 - Perform hands-on, system-level characterization of fast-switching WBG devices (as distinct from die- or wafer-level characterization), including switching waveforms, thermal performance, parasitic-sensitive measurements and robustness testing.

 - Help develop practical design rules for customers: gate drive, layout/loop inductance, protection and measurement techniques.

Technical content

 - Write and contribute to application notes, design guides, test reports and training material.

Product feedback

 - Document customer requirements, test results and failure-mode learnings, and share them with Device Engineering and Product teams.




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education and experience — one of the following:

 - Ph.D. in EE (Power Electronics) or a closely related field; recent graduates are welcome.

 - M.S. in EE with substantial, specific hands-on power converter work from a thesis, lab or industry project.

Preferred: 2–5 years of additional industry experience in applications engineering, power converter design or power semiconductor characterization.

Technical skills

 - Solid understanding of power converter design: switching loss mechanisms, thermal characteristics, magnetics, layout/parasitics and gate drive.

 - Hands-on bench experience building and testing power electronics hardware; lab experience with high-voltage or high-current wide bandgap (SiC or GaN) devices is a strong plus.

 - Working proficiency with SPICE and/or PLECS for simulating power circuits.

 - Working proficiency with EDA tools for PCB design and fabrication, such as Altium Designer, Eagle or OrCAD.

 - Familiarity with parasitic-aware layout and EMI considerations for fast-switching power stages.

 - Clear written and verbal technical communication, and comfort working directly with customers.




LOCATION & TRAVEL

 - Location: On-site in Somerville, MA.

 - Travel: Occasional (< 20%) travel to customer sites and industry events.




VALUES & CULTURE FIT

Vertical Semiconductor is seeking an engineer who wants to grow quickly and is willing to get involved in the day-to-day execution of a startup. The ideal candidate enjoys tackling complex engineering challenges, is happiest at the bench and in the simulator, learns fast and thrives in a collaborative environment where they can make an immediate impact. We value integrity, initiative, problem-solving, creativity and a passion for creating transformative technology that can change industries and improve the world.

jobs.title: Director - Lifecycle Marketing
jobs.description:
We are looking for a strategic, commercially minded and highly proactive Director of Lifecycle Marketing to lead and evolve Madison Reed's customer lifecycle strategy. This leader will build a best-in-class retention and engagement engine that deepens customer relationships, drives incremental revenue and maximizes lifetime value across our DTC, Hair Color Bar and membership businesses.

This role goes well beyond managing the email and SMS calendar. You will think holistically about the customer journey and the broader business, identifying opportunities to acquire new customers, grow our owned marketing databases, increase engagement and create lasting loyalty. You will bring forward new ideas, challenge conventional approaches, and turn consumer insight into strategies that deliver measurable results.

This is an opportunity for a builder: someone energized by an evolving, high-growth company who can help establish the processes, tools, technology and team capabilities needed to scale. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable setting the strategic vision, rolling up their sleeves to execute, and leading a team through change and growth.

If you're excited by the opportunity to help disrupt a huge industry, improve the lives of thousands of women and build something meaningful alongside an incredibly talented team, this may be the role for you!

This role reports to the SVP of Integrated Marketing, is full time and remote. While remote, this role may travel up to 5% of the time.

The base salary range for this position is between xx and xx. At Madison Reed, we aim to pay competitively. Factors which may affect starting pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

Responsibilities:

Set the Strategic Vision and Drive Business Growth

• Define and drive the overarching lifecycle and retention strategy, roadmap and performance targets to increase customer lifetime value, repeat purchase, engagement and brand loyalty.

• Serve as a strategic growth partner to the broader marketing and leadership teams, translating company objectives into lifecycle strategies that accelerate acquisition, engagement, retention and revenue.

• Own the strategy and performance of key revenue streams, including e-commerce sales, Hair Color Bar appointments and the Madison Reed Membership program.

• Proactively identify emerging consumer behaviors, business opportunities and industry trends, and turn them into lifecycle strategies before anyone asks you to.

Drive Customer Acquisition and Database Growth

• Develop and lead an innovative strategy to grow Madison Reed's owned email and SMS databases through lead generation, partnerships, promotions and on-site experiences.

• Find creative ways to capture consumer interest and build permission-based relationships with prospective customers before, during and after their first purchase or service.

• Partner with Acquisition, Brand, Digital and E-commerce to build database growth into broader marketing initiatives, and design welcome journeys that convert new leads into first-time customers.

Build Best-in-Class Customer Experiences and Retention Programs

• Lead the strategy and execution of all lifecycle communications across email, SMS, push and in-app, delivering personalized, relevant and seamless customer experiences.

• Identify the behaviors that correlate with usage, engagement and affinity, and create automated journeys that guide guests from their first color experience to long-term loyalty.

• Connect the customer experience across DTC, Hair Color Bars, wholesale and membership, so the relationship with Madison Reed feels consistent at every touchpoint.

• Establish a rigorous testing framework using A/B/n and multivariate methodologies to measure incremental lift, and write creative briefs that carry the business objective, the customer insight and the strategic direction.

Innovate, Build and Scale

• Bring forward new ideas, technologies and channels that push past traditional CRM and strengthen our competitive advantage.

• Build the processes, tools, workflows and operating frameworks that let lifecycle marketing scale as the business grows, including clear priorities, planning and measurement.

• Lead requirements for data updates across the ESP and cross-channel platforms, including contact properties, custom events, APIs and data feeds.

• Oversee the lifecycle marketing technology stack, managing vendors, budgets and contractors, and partner with Analytics and Engineering on advanced capabilities such as Next Best Action and churn prediction.

Lead, Develop and Inspire a High-Performing Team

• Lead, coach and develop a high-performing lifecycle marketing team responsible for strategy and execution across all batch and automated communications.

• Build a culture of ownership, accountability, curiosity and continuous improvement, where people are expected to challenge the status quo and bring forward new ideas.

• Stay a player-coach. Set clear goals and expectations, and stay close enough to the work to get into a brief or a campaign setup alongside the team when it matters.

Partner Across the Organization

• Collaborate closely with Acquisition, Brand, Digital, E-commerce, Analytics, Engineering and Retail to drive an integrated customer experience and shared business outcomes.

• Influence leadership and cross-functional partners by turning customer insight, performance data and opportunity into clear recommendations and plans people can act on.

• Keep all CRM programs compliant with legal requirements including TCPA and CAN-SPAM, maintain best practices for SMS and email deliverability, and ensure essential transactional communications are delivered reliably.

Qualifications:

• 10 to 12+ years of marketing experience with deep expertise in CRM, lifecycle marketing and retention, ideally in a DTC or consumer business. Subscription or membership experience is a plus.

• Demonstrated ability to think strategically beyond channel execution, connecting lifecycle work to broader company objectives and commercial growth.

• Proven experience developing customer acquisition and database growth strategies across email and SMS.

• Strong commercial instincts and a track record of measurable improvement in acquisition, engagement, retention, repeat purchase and lifetime value.

• Entrepreneurial mindset with a bias toward action: someone who spots the opportunity, challenges conventional thinking, and carries an idea from concept through execution.

• Experience building and scaling lifecycle programs, teams, processes and technology inside a growing or changing organization.

• Exceptional ability to translate complex data and consumer insight into strategies and measurable results.

• Deep experience with ESP platforms, MarTech integrations, customer data and reporting dashboards.

• Proven track record of developing and coaching talent, and of being a player-coach who executes alongside the team rather than only directing it.

• Strong project management, prioritization and attention to detail, with the ability to move several initiatives forward at once in a fast-paced environment.

• Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to influence leadership and build alignment across departments.

What Success Looks Like:

• A measurable increase in customer lifetime value, repeat purchase, retention and engagement.

• Sustained growth in our owned email and SMS databases, with quality and conversion potential, not just volume.

• Customer journeys that genuinely connect DTC, Hair Color Bars, wholesale and membership.

• A lifecycle marketing function with the processes, tools, technology and talent to scale.

• A culture of proactive thinking, experimentation and accountability that keeps finding new ways to grow the business.

Big on Benefits

The Perks? Glad you asked…

• Comprehensive Healthcare

• 100% Company Paid Short and Long Term Disability

• 401k Participation and Equity Grants

• Continuing Education Contributions

• HSA Employer Contributions and FSA Options

• Parental Leave Program

• Commuter Benefits

• Responsible Paid Time Off Program

• Complimentary Madison Reed Products + Discounts on Hair Color Bar Services

• Company sponsored events

• But wait, there’s more…

We are Madison Reed.

We’re disrupting a $50 billion industry.

Since 2013, we’ve offered our clients the option to truly own their beauty with a revolutionary choice—your place or ours? Home or Hair Color Bar? Our professional hair color is truly omnichannel, with the option to order or subscribe through our website, pick up in-store at our Hair Color Bars, or make an appointment at one of our Hair Color Bar locations (over 20 & growing). At our Hair Color Bars, clients can choose from a variety of color services from licensed cosmetologists—permanent hair color, roots only, hair gloss, highlights and more. With our men’s line launched in 2020, we’re shaking up the $50 billion hair care industry with products that continue to raise the bar for doing hair at home.

We live our values.

Here at our San Francisco headquarters and in every Hair Color Bar, we truly live our values—Love, Joy, Courage, Responsibility, and Trust. Our values inform everything we do, from how we treat our clients to how we treat every member of our fast-growing team. Our founder & CEO, Amy Errett, has fostered a one-of-a-kind culture based on transparency, accountability, and fun; where diversity and inclusion are of utmost importance and every team member feels supported to succeed.

We are hair color that breaks the rules.

Our commitment to the ultimate client experience, paired with our dedication to product innovation and the latest beauty technology, has attracted a devoted, consistently-growing base of fans, converts, and color evangelists. We love what we do—and it shows.

Join us in our mission to live life colorfully and make personal care more personal.

The biologics characterization group develops state-of-the-art analytical techniques for in-depth characterization of therapeutic proteins and other novel biologic molecules using advanced, combined analytical techniques. We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance & FP&A, Senior Associate
jobs.description:
We're hiring a Senior Associate, FP&A to be the analyst behind our marketplace levers — recruiter incentives and retainers, pricing and take rate, unit economics, and vertical P&Ls. You'll run the monthly budget vs. actuals review, maintain the operating model with our VP Finance, and be the analytical partner leadership leans on for pricing and incentive decisions. You'll report to our VP Finance and work closely with our accounting team.

This is a builder role. Marketplace economics are more interesting than a standard SaaS P&L — take rates, recruiter supply, roles posted, time-to-hire, and placement timing all drive revenue — and you'll build the analysis the company runs on. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Maintain the operating model with the VP Finance. Keep the drivers current — revenue, GMV, headcount, OpEx — and support the annual plan and quarterly reforecasts.

 - Model marketplace levers. Recruiter incentives and retainers, pricing and take rate, and fee structures — build the analysis behind each decision and track what happens after it ships.

 - Own unit economics. GMV, net revenue, take rate, recruiter payouts, cohort behavior, LTV:CAC, and payback — the numbers leadership makes pricing and incentive calls on.

 - Run budget vs. actuals. Monthly BvA and department-level flux review with our accounting team, with clear variance explanations for leadership.

 - Build the metrics layer. Partner with RevOps and BizOps to define metrics and build the dashboards leadership uses every week.

 - Automate with AI. We use AI heavily across the company and expect finance to as well — recurring reporting shouldn't be manual.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3–5 years in FP&A, strategic finance, investment banking, PE, or top-tier consulting, with at least 1–2 years building models an operating team actually used.

 - Expert spreadsheet modeling — three-statement, driver-based forecasts, and scenario analysis.

 - Comfortable presenting numbers to executives and turning an ambiguous question into a clear answer.

 - High ownership, low ego, and fast. Your work goes straight to the exec team and board.

 - Bonus: experience at a marketplace, fintech, or usage-based business; a Series B–C fundraise; hands-on with a planning tool (Pigment, Anaplan) or SQL/BI (Metabase, Looker).
   
   


THE IDEAL CANDIDATE BRINGS

 - Experience in multi-sided / marketplace businesses

 - Has owned analysis of a marketing subsidy or incentive program

 - Has built the take-rate or pricing model at a marketplace and defended it to leadership

 - Has run a monthly BvA where department leads had to explain their variances to them

 - Has worked from raw transaction data (SQL or exports), not just a finance system's outputs

 - Has gone through a raise on the company side: model, data room, diligence questions


ABOUT PARAFORM

Paraform is the first end-to-end AI recruiting marketplace, modernizing one of the largest and most fragmented markets in the world: hiring. We connect companies with thousands of specialized recruiters and AI agents that work together to fill roles faster and more accurately.

We believe recruiting works best when human judgment is paired with AI that truly understands hiring. That's why we treat recruiters like entrepreneurs, not vendors, and build the financial, operational, and technical infrastructure that powers their success.

Industry leaders like Decagon, Palantir, Rippling, Abridge, and Hightouch hire through Paraform, and we grew revenue 8× last year. We're backed by Scale, Felicis, A*, BOND, Liquid 2, DST Global, and the founders of YouTube, Instacart, Canva, and more.

Our mission is to make hiring fast, reliable, and scalable for every company in the world. For more on where we're headed, read our company vision https://www.paraform.com/blog/the-talent-company.

jobs.title: Sr. Power Electronics Engineer - High Voltage, Satellites (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

SR. POWER ELECTRONICS ENGINEER - HIGH VOLTAGE, SATELLITES (STARLINK)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and provides fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

SpaceX Gateways are responsible for delivering internet from the ground to the satellites – they must be cost effective, capable of high performance in all weather conditions, and reliable over long periods of time. The traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) team is revolutionizing RF vacuum electronics to power the future of space communications with SpaceX gateways by building hardware an order of magnitude faster than traditional industry and an order of magnitude more cost-effective. In addition, we're developing our own high-voltage power supplies to drive unparalleled performance in these high-frequency, high-bandwidth amplification systems critical to our mission.

As a key player on this team, you'll lead the design of sophisticated kV-level power supplies that drive TWTA systems. From concept to deployment, you'll own the full hardware lifecycle—prototyping, testing, integration, and iteration—while collaborating closely with experts across RF engineering, mechanical design, systems integration, manufacturing, and more. If you're passionate about pushing the boundaries of power electronics and want to contribute to humanity's multi-planetary future, this is your chance to make a tangible impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own hardware from conceptual design through high volume production and ground station operation

• Deliver engineering expertise in designing, analyzing, and rigorously testing of DC-DC power converters built to thrive in harsh environments

• Design power supplies that support 10s of kilovolts and hundreds of watts

• Dive into electrical power system and sub-system design trades, shaping requirements that optimize performance, efficiency, and reliability

• Lead in defining and executing comprehensive verification testing and analysis for electrical power systems

• Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of engineers to define power electronics hardware

• Rapidly iterate on designs, analysis and test to inform high level systems trades and steer overall product direction

• Interact with digital embedded devices, analog sensing and telemetry, system controls, etc.

• Demonstrate extreme ownership of product outcomes at every stage of development and production

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline

• 5+ years of professional experience in power converter development via professional work experience, project/research-based student experience, or a combination of both

• Experience working with magnetics and design of custom transformers and inductors, including planar magnetics

• Experience in modeling, simulation, and testing of power electronics

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Master’s degree in electrical engineering or related field

• Demonstrated full-cycle ownership of a hardware project from concept to implementation

• Strong grasp of analog control and discrete logic design

• Working experience in voltage and current mode control and design

• Strong grasp of DC-DC topologies, with ability to select optimal architectures and components

• Understanding of design for fault tolerance and reliability

• Familiar with failure mode effects and criticality analysis

• Practical skills with in-lab impedance measurement and loop-gain measurement

• Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Willing to work extended hours and some weekends if needed for mission critical deadlines

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 3: $140,000.00 - $235,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law. Company shuttles are offered to employees for roundtrip travel from select Seattle locations to the SpaceX Redmond office Monday to Friday.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: IT Service Desk Lead
jobs.description:
T-Rex Solutions is looking to select an IT Service Desk Lead to support our Department of Commerce (DOC) Office of Solution and Service Delivery (OSSD) customer. Within the DOC, the OSSD provides IT support for the Department of Commerce’s Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), Office of the Secretary (OS), and other bureau partners. Under this program, we will provide comprehensive IT service desk support, ensuring continuous and efficient resolution of technical issues. It includes help desk operations, incident management, service request fulfillment, and escalation handling from Tier 0 through Tier 3 support. Service hours of support are Monday through Friday 7:00am-6:00pm (desk-side support) and (walk-up help desk) or as needed such special events or emergency requirements. Work is performed on-site at the Herbert Hoover building in Washington, DC.

Responsibilities:

• Oversee the day-to-day activities of the Tier 2 service-desk operations to ensure end users receive the IT support required.

• Investigate and resolve escalated incidents from Tier 1 using advanced diagnostic tools, system logs, and root cause analysis. Apply specialized technical knowledge to resolve hardware, software, and system configuration issues in accordance with established SOPs.

• Process and complete service requests requiring elevated privileges or deeper technical intervention, such as complex account configurations, system patching, software deployment, or device management tasks.

• Support problem management activities by identifying root causes and contributing to permanent fixed for recurring incidents.

• Provide onsite service desk support to troubleshoot, repair and resolve issues for laptops, desktops, tablets, mobile devices, and peripherals (e.g. printers, scanners, plotters, monitors, etc.) for customers. This desk is an area that customers visit to receive same day support.

• Provide desk-side support to troubleshoot, repair, and resolve issues for a wide range of installed computer systems such as laptops, desktops, tablets, mobile devices, and peripherals (e.g. printers, scanners, plotters, monitors, etc.) for customers. In cases when a field technician is dispatched to resolve an incident, ensure that the technician is fully prepared to diagnose and resolve the incident on the first visit.

• Provide technical support for remote customers via telephone, online chat, email, or using secure remote access product.

• Escalate unresolved or complex incidents to Tier 3 or vendor support as necessary, ensuring all troubleshooting actions and findings are documented within the ITSM system. Maintain communication with Tier 1 and end users to provide status updates until resolution.

• Support enterprise systems, applications, and infrastructure components as assigned. Conduct configuration reviews, system performance checks, and corrective actions to maintain service stability and reliability.

• Document resolutions, workarounds, and lessons learned to update knowledge base articles and improve Tier 1 troubleshooting capabilities. Provide technical feedback to improve SOPs, workflows, and service efficiency.

• Prior to closing any incident, validate with the impacted end user that the service has been fully resolved.

• Collaborate with IT support teams to identify, analyze, and resolve issues and trends impacting the end-user environment, including proactively addressing recurring incidents and underlying problems to improve service stability and user experience.

• Develop, update, and maintain end-user outreach and communication methods and materials to ensure users are informed of outages and upcoming changes to the IT environment.

• Support approved change implementations and validate post-change functionality for Tier 2 supported systems.

• Provide written input to Tier 1 or other end users including SOP's, "how-to" and troubleshooting guides, and training materials/procedures.

• Coordinate with Tier 0, Tier 1, and Tier 3 support teams to ensure consistent service delivery and knowledge sharing.

• Participate in feedback sessions, quality reviews, and training to improve Tier 2 performance and expand technical proficiency.

• Track and report on Tier 2 performance metrics, using these metrics to identify trends, recurring issues, and opportunities for process improvement.

Requirements:

• Relevant experience managing/leading Tier 1/2/3 Service Desk operations, preferably in a federal government environment

• Active Top Secret clearance required

• Experience managing an incident management system in a performance-based environment complying with ITIL V4 standards.

• Expert level experience re-engineering or setting up service desks according to industry best practices.

Desired Skills:

• Service Desk Institute (HDI) certified as a HDI Support Manager

T-Rex Overview

Established in 1999, T-Rex Solutions, LLC is a proven mid-tier business providing data-centric mission services to the Federal government as it increasingly tries to secure and leverage the power of data. We design, integrate, secure, and deploy advanced technical solutions for our customers so they can efficiently fulfill their critical objectives. T-Rex offers both IT and professional services to numerous Federal agencies and is a leader in providing high quality and innovative solutions in the areas of Cloud and Infrastructure Services, Cyber Security, and Big Data Engineering.

T-Rex is constantly seeking qualified people to join our growing team. We have built a broad client base through our devotion to delivering quality products and customer service, and to do that we need quality individuals. But more than that, we at T-Rex are committed to creating a culture that supports the development of every employee's personal and professional lives. T-Rex has made a commitment to maintain the status of an industry leader in compensation packages and benefits which includes competitive salaries, performance bonuses, training and educational reimbursement, Transamerica 401(k) and Cigna healthcare benefits.

T-Rex is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, sex (including pregnancy and sexual orientation), parental status, national origin, age, disability, family medical history or genetic information, political affiliation, military service, or other non-merit based factors.

In compliance with pay transparency guidelines, the annual base salary range for this position is $90,000 - $120,000. Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. T-Rex considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and business considerations when extending an offer.

T-Rex offers a diverse and collaborative work environment, exciting opportunities for professional growth, and generous benefits, including: PTO available to use immediately upon joining (prorated based on start date), paid parental leave, individual and family health, vision, and dental benefits, annual budget for training, professional development and tuition reimbursement, and a 401(k) plan with company match fully vested after 60 days of employment among other benefits.

 - Hiring Manager Partnership: Meet regularly with hiring managers to understand role requirements and team needs, and keep them updated on pipeline progress.

 - Process & Candidate Experience: Keep the hiring process organized and moving, maintain accurate records in Ashby, and ensure candidates have a positive experience.

 - Market Insights: Share what you’re seeing in the hardware talent market and pipeline data with the TA team and hiring managers.

What you’ll bring:

 - Experience recruiting for hardware or equipment roles in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

 - Proficiency with LinkedIn Recruiter; Ashby experience is a plus

jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer (EHR Integration Team)
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

Natera is building apps and services that run inside the clinician's EHR. This is a hands-on role.
You will build SMART on FHIR apps that launch from Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner) and other
EHRs, the FHIR services and data model behind them, and CDS Hooks services that bring
Natera ordering and results into the provider's workflow. You will work in a small team with
product and our wider EHR integration group, and you will handle patient data under HIPAA
every day.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Build and ship SMART on FHIR apps: EHR launch and standalone launch, OAuth 2.0 with
PKCE, backend services authorization, scopes and token handling.
• Design and build the server side: FHIR R4 APIs, mapping to our internal data model,
profiles and extensions.
• Build CDS Hooks services with prefetch that respond within EHR time limits.
• Take apps through EHR vendor onboarding and go-live, starting with Epic (Vendor
Services and Showroom), then Oracle Health and others. Work with health system IT on
build and testing.
• Handle PHI correctly in storage, caching, logging and tracing: minimum necessary data,
encryption, audit trails, no PHI in logs.
• Work with HL7 v2 and interface engine flows where the EHR needs them.
• Write design docs, review code and mentor engineers.
• Be on call for what you ship.
• This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and have
access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform
the job.
• Must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure
Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30
days of hire.
• Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.

QUALIFICATIONS

• BS in computer science, a related field, or equivalent experience.
• 6+ years of software development, with at least 3 building EHR integrations in production.
• Hands-on SMART on FHIR: you have built and shipped an app that launches inside an
EHR, not only consumed FHIR data.
• Strong FHIR R4: resource modeling, search, and terminology (LOINC, SNOMED, ICD-10).

• Production go-live with Epic. Oracle Health (Cerner), athenahealth, MEDITECH or others
a plus.
• Backend services in Java and Spring Boot or similar, on AWS.
• Experience handling PHI under HIPAA in a production system.
• Clear communication with clinicians, health system IT and product.

• CDS Hooks in production.

ORM/ORU.
• FHIR Subscriptions and Bulk FHIR.
• Interface engines such as Mirth, Rhapsody or Cloverleaf.
• React and TypeScript for in-EHR user interfaces.
• USCDI, Da Vinci implementation guides, or ONC certification work.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

• FHIR R4, SMART App Launch, OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, CDS Hooks
• Java and Spring Boot; REST and event-driven microservices
• AWS services such as SQS, S3, SNS and Lambda
• Relational databases and SQL, preferably PostgreSQL or MySQL
• Docker, CI/CD, Linux fundamentals
• React and TypeScript

jobs.title: Power Electronics Engineer - High Voltage (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

POWER ELECTRONICS ENGINEER - HIGH VOLTAGE (STARLINK)

At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and provides fast, reliable internet to 10M+ users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe.

SpaceX Gateways are responsible for delivering internet from the ground to the satellites – they must be cost effective, capable of high performance in all weather conditions, and reliable over long periods of time. The traveling wave tube amplifier (TWTA) team is revolutionizing RF vacuum electronics to power the future of space communications with SpaceX gateways by building hardware an order of magnitude faster than traditional industry and an order of magnitude more cost-effective. In addition, we're developing our own high-voltage power supplies to drive unparalleled performance in these high-frequency, high-bandwidth amplification systems critical to our mission.

As a key player on this team, you'll lead the design of sophisticated kV-level power supplies that drive TWTA systems. From concept to deployment, you'll own the full hardware lifecycle—prototyping, testing, integration, and iteration—while collaborating closely with experts across RF engineering, mechanical design, systems integration, manufacturing, and more. If you're passionate about pushing the boundaries of power electronics and want to contribute to humanity's multi-planetary future, this is your chance to make a tangible impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own hardware from conceptual design through high volume production and ground station operation

• Deliver engineering expertise in designing, analyzing, and rigorously testing of DC-DC power converters built to thrive in harsh environments

• Design power supplies that support 10s of kilovolts and hundreds of watts

• Dive into electrical power system and sub-system design trades, shaping requirements that optimize performance, efficiency, and reliability

• Lead in defining and executing comprehensive verification testing and analysis for electrical power systems

• Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team of engineers to define power electronics hardware

• Rapidly iterate on designs, analysis and test to inform high level systems trades and steer overall product direction

• Interact with digital embedded devices, analog sensing and telemetry, system controls, etc.

• Demonstrate extreme ownership of product outcomes at every stage of development and production

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, physics, or other STEM discipline

• 1+ years of experience in power converter development via professional work experience, project/research-based student experience, or a combination of both (Internships, co-ops, and project teams can apply)

• Experience working with magnetics and design of custom transformers and inductors, including planar magnetics

• Experience in modeling, simulation, and testing of power electronics

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Master’s degree in electrical engineering or related field

• Demonstrated full-cycle ownership of a hardware project from concept to implementation

• Strong grasp of analog control and discrete logic design

• Working experience in voltage and current mode control and compensation design

• Strong grasp of DC-DC topologies, with ability to select optimal architectures and components

• Understanding of design for fault tolerance and reliability

• Familiar with failure mode effects and criticality analysis

• Practical skills with in-lab impedance measurement and loop-gain measurement

• Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Willing to work extended hours and some weekends if needed for mission critical deadlines

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $105,000.00 - $145,000.00
Level 2: $120,000.00 - $175,000.00

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees in Washington State accrue paid sick time in compliance with state and federal law.
