jobs.title: Sr. GRC Analyst - Internal Governance
jobs.description:
What you’ll be part of

Garner is on a mission to transform the U.S. healthcare system — and we’re the only proven player doing exactly that. We partner with employers to redesign how healthcare works: applying 550+ proprietary clinical metrics across 80+ specialties to a dataset of 320M+ patients to identify the best-performing doctors, then using compelling incentives to steer members to the care that helps them get healthier, faster.

The result is a rare “win win” — better care and lower costs for both members and employers. In just five years, our work has helped over 2.5 million people access higher-quality care and saved $1B in healthcare costs. We recently raised our Series E and have doubled five years running. If you've ever wanted your work to solve a problem that touches every person in this country, this is the opportunity to do exactly that. You'd be joining a team fundamentally reimagining healthcare in the U.S. — and using AI to scale that impact further and faster than anyone else can.

About the role:

We are looking for a Senior GRC Analyst to join our Technical Compliance team and own the recurring risk, vendor, findings, and governance work that keeps Garner’s security program operating well between audits. You will run our risk risk register, manage third party risk, drive security findings to resolution, deliver security training and run the operating cadence of our security governance program. You will partner with all departments across the company so that risks are identified early, decisions are made deliberately, and remediation actually gets done. Our Technology Compliance team safeguards Garner’s sensitive healthcare data and protects the trust of our members, clients, and partners by maintaining a strong control environment and regulatory compliance. The work you do here has a direct impact on our ability to win and retain enterprise customers, expand into new lines of business, and scale securely as we grow.

Where you will work:

This role is open to remote candidates across the U.S. For candidates based in New York City, the position follows a hybrid schedule with in-office work required Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday each week.

What you will do:

• Own Garner’s annual information security risk assessment and risk register, driving risk identification, scoring, treatment, and reporting

• Manage risk exceptions and prepare risk acceptances for leadership decision

• Run third party and vendor risk reviews from intake through approval and periodic reassessment

• Own security findings from vulnerability scanning, penetration tests, audits, client assessments, and incidents, tracking remediation with Engineering, enforcing SLAs, and escalating findings that warrant a risk decision

• Run our security and compliance training program, including annual security awareness and HIPAA training, onboarding, content refreshes, and completion tracking

• Manage the maintenance of our compliance policies, standards, and procedures

• Report on our compliance posture to senior leadership

• Scale our GRC function with AI and automation, building quick wins and scoping requirements for Engineering to fully automate the rest

What you will bring to the team:

• 5+ years of experience in GRC, IT risk management, third party risk management, or information security compliance

• Experience running information security risk assessments and maintaining a risk register using established methodologies such as NIST CSF or ISO 27005

• Hands on experience with vendor risk management and with vulnerability or findings remediation programs in a cloud native engineering environment

jobs.title: Hardware Systems Engineer - AI Hardware
jobs.description:
About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, Texas | Lisbon, Portugal

About The Department

Cloudflare’s Infrastructure group is responsible for building our global network. Our Hardware Engineering team helps research, develop, test, and deploy new equipment enabling 20% of the world’s internet traffic to be served smoothly. Deployed across 330 cities in 120+ countries, the hardware we select helps improve the security, reliability, and performance of the Internet.

About The Role

We need to make thoughtful infrastructure choices affecting a significant portion of the Internet. Hardware we work with includes GPUs, servers and components, as well as PDUs and network hardware. As a Hardware Systems Engineer, you will work with colleagues on the Engineering teams, Product and Performance teams, and Hardware Sourcing teams to design, qualify and maintain Cloudflare’s worldwide fleet of GPU servers.

What You'll Do

• Contribute to the technical requirements and end-to-end delivery of AI infrastructure — compute, networking, storage, power, and cooling — not just the accelerator

• Evaluate, select, and qualify AI hardware platforms (GPUs, custom ASICs, SmartNICs, storage) based on real workload requirements and first-principles analysis

• Design and validate rack-scale GPU systems: multi-node topologies, high-speed interconnects (NVLink, InfiniBand, RoCE), power distribution, and thermal management

• Run hands-on qualification: benchmarking, stress testing, failure mode analysis, and vendor RCA — you close the loop yourself

• Assess and qualify ODM/OEM server platforms; engage directly with vendors and work through the full technical qualification cycle

• Translate AI product and workload requirements into precise infrastructure specifications

• Identify gaps in the existing infrastructure stack and drive solutions across hardware, firmware, software, and operations

• Stay ahead of the AI hardware landscape — new silicon, new interconnects, new form factors — and bring informed, opinionated recommendations

• Build tooling and automation to support qualification workflows, performance analysis, and ongoing operational visibility

• Communicate your results and updates through blog posts and internal talks

Examples Of Desirable Skills, Knowledge And Experience

• Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or Computer Science

• Experience in AI infrastructure, systems engineering, or hardware platform engineering

• First-principles understanding of AI accelerator architecture: compute pipelines, memory hierarchy (HBM, GDDR), interconnect topology, and/or how workload characteristics map to hardware capabilities

• Hands-on experience qualifying AI server platforms — you've run NCCL tests, profiled collective operations, debugged NVLink errors, and chased down PCIe lane misconfigurations

• Understand rack-scale systems: high-density power (kW/rack, busbar, PDU), liquid cooling (rear-door, direct liquid, immersion), high-speed networking infrastructure, and/or physical layer constraints

• Experience with AI/ML frameworks (vllm, sglang) at the systems level — you understand what they demand from the hardware and where bottlenecks actually live

• Familiarity with AI server form factors: HGX, OAC, OAM, UBB, open rack standards, and the tradeoffs between them

• Scripting and automation skills (Python, Bash, Go and Linux sysadmin); you build tooling to support your own work and the team's

• Strong written communication — you can write a rigorous technical specification and a crisp vendor requirements document

• Knowledge of performance benchmarking ; Previous experience in testing, measuring, and/or simulating hardware performance and an understanding of no-stone-left-unturned experimentation

• Knowledge of Redfish, IPMI and server remote management protocols, and experience with firmware updates

• Harness AI tools and automation to fundamentally accelerate the qualification lifecycle, driving exponential efficiency gains and quality standards.

• Possess the organizational skills and interest to manage cross-functional technical projects, ensuring architectural designs seamlessly align with delivery schedules.

• Thrive as a deeply self-motivated engineer in ambiguous environments, demonstrating a strong bias for action and the ability to drive initiatives forward without close supervision.

Bonus Points

• Experience with major AI server ODMs/OEMs and their qualification and customization processes

• Exposure to hyperscaler or cloud infrastructure design — understanding how GPU capacity is provisioned, allocated, and operated at scale

• Experience with RDMA networking, RoCEv2 congestion control, or InfiniBand fabric management

• Understanding of AI workload patterns: LLM training vs. inference, model/tensor/pipeline parallelism, and their memory and bandwidth implications

• Familiarity with open compute hardware programs or OCP specifications

• Experience of performance optimization based on hardware / software codesign

• Experience of kernel development, compiler optimization, or driver development.

• Experience of observability and monitoring tools such as Prometheus and Grafana, as well as the ability to observe trends over time

• Experience with software development tools and processes such as Git, TeamCity and Jira

• Experience in a hyperscale cloud infrastructure role also valuable

• Knowledge of debugging server hardware faults and the ability to engage with our sourcing team and vendors to improve quality

Who You Are

• A self-starter who identifies what needs to be done and executes without waiting to be asked

• Genuinely curious — you read architecture whitepapers, follow chip announcements, and have opinions on why one memory subsystem beats another

• Equally comfortable racking servers in a lab and writing a detailed technical requirements document

• Able to make a defensible technical decision with incomplete information, and communicate the reasoning clearly

Compensation

Compensation may be adjusted depending on work location.

• For Lisbon based hires: Estimated annual salary of €54,000-68,000

Equity

This role is eligible to participate in Cloudflare’s equity plan.

Benefits

Cloudflare offers a complete package of benefits and programs to support you and your family.  Our benefits programs can help you pay health care expenses, support caregiving, build capital for the future and make life a little easier and fun!  The below is a description of our benefits for employees in the United States, and benefits may vary for employees based outside the U.S.

Health & Welfare Benefits

• Medical/Rx Insurance

• Dental Insurance

• Vision Insurance

• Flexible Spending Accounts

• Commuter Spending Accounts

• Fertility & Family Forming Benefits

• On-demand mental health support and Employee Assistance Program

• Global Travel Medical Insurance

Financial Benefits

• Short and Long Term Disability Insurance

• Life & Accident Insurance

• 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan

• Employee Stock Participation Plan

Time Off

• Flexible paid time off covering vacation and sick leave

• Leave programs, including parental, pregnancy health, medical, and bereavement leave

What Makes Cloudflare Special?

We’re not just a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company. We’re a highly ambitious, large-scale technology company with a soul. Fundamental to our mission to help build a better Internet is protecting the free and open Internet.

Project Galileo: Since 2014, we've equipped more than 2,400 journalism and civil society organizations in 111 countries with powerful tools to defend themselves against attacks that would otherwise censor their work, technology already used by Cloudflare’s enterprise customers--at no cost.

Athenian Project: In 2017, we created the Athenian Project to ensure that state and local governments have the highest level of protection and reliability for free, so that their constituents have access to election information and voter registration. Since the project, we've provided services to more than 425 local government election websites in 33 states.

1.1.1.1: We released 1.1.1.1 to help fix the foundation of the Internet by building a faster, more secure and privacy-centric public DNS resolver. This is available publicly for everyone to use - it is the first consumer-focused service Cloudflare has ever released. Here’s the deal - we don’t store client IP addresses never, ever. We will continue to abide by our privacy commitment and ensure that no user data is sold to advertisers or used to target consumers.

Sound like something you’d like to be a part of? We’d love to hear from you!

Please note that applicants who progress to the offer stage of the interview process may be asked to attend an in-person interview within one of the Cloudflare Offices or Cloudflare Hubs.  More details about this will be available at that stage of the interview process.

This position may require access to information protected under U.S. export control laws, including the U.S. Export Administration Regulations. Please note that any offer of employment may be conditioned on your authorization to receive software or technology controlled under these U.S. export laws without sponsorship for an export license.

Cloudflare is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.  We are committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all people and place great value in both diversity and inclusiveness.  All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to their, or any other person's, perceived or actual race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, family care status, or any other basis protected by law. We are an AA/Veterans/Disabled Employer.

Cloudflare provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities.  Please tell us if you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job. Examples of reasonable accommodations include, but are not limited to, changing the application process, providing documents in an alternate format, using a sign language interpreter, or using specialized equipment.  If you require a reasonable accommodation to apply for a job, please contact us via e-mail at hr@cloudflare.com or via mail at 101 Townsend St. San Francisco, CA 94107.

jobs.title: Principal Clinical Scientist, Medical Devices & AI
jobs.description:
MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE

At Neko Health, we are building a future where healthcare helps people stay well through prevention and earlier detection. Our medical devices and AI turn new ways of measuring health into opportunities to improve care. Rigorous clinical science is what makes that translation possible.

We are seeking a Principal Clinical Scientist to own the scientific evidence pathway for our medical devices, AI algorithms and Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), from early concepts and prototypes through clinical validation, regulatory submissions and evaluation after launch.

You will join multiple R&D programmes already underway, combining scientific leadership with hands-on study design, analysis and interpretation. Working alongside engineers, data scientists, medical leads, research operations and regulatory affairs, you will determine what evidence is needed, design pragmatic studies to generate it and use the findings to guide development and clinical use.


WHAT YOU’LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS

 - Take ownership of active programmes. Assess the technology, clinical use cases and existing evidence across priority R&D programmes. Identify the questions and decisions that matter most for earlier detection, better care and meaningful benefits for our members (Member-first, always).

 - Build clear, efficient evidence plans. Define studies, milestones and criteria for progression, aligning product development with clinical and regulatory needs. Find opportunities for studies and datasets to answer multiple questions and accelerate progress across programmes (Chase 10X, not 10%).

 - Move studies into execution. Develop or refine protocols with appropriate populations, endpoints, reference standards and analytical approaches. Work with research operations and clinical partners to secure the necessary approvals and get studies underway.

 - Shape development through clinical science. Guide prototyping and data collection with engineering, data science and medical leads, connecting measurement performance and algorithm outputs to their intended use in clinical practice (Tech-enabled, human-centred).

 - Turn results into decisions. Deliver analyses and scientific reports from existing datasets and studies reaching completion. Challenge assumptions, investigate unexpected findings and make clear recommendations on what should progress, change or stop (Optimistic truth seeking).

 - Deliver evidence for regulatory review. Own the scientific content of clinical evidence packages for programmes approaching submission, working with regulatory affairs to address gaps, substantiate proposed claims and respond to reviewers.

 - Strengthen how the team works. Use AI tools to accelerate research, analysis and scientific writing while retaining scientific judgement and accountability. Mentor colleagues and establish reusable methods that improve the quality and pace of future programmes.


REQUIREMENTS

 - PhD, MD or equivalent doctoral qualification in a relevant clinical, scientific or quantitative discipline. A medical degree is not required.

 - Strong medical and physiological understanding, with the ability to connect device measurements and algorithm outputs to disease processes, clinical pathways and decisions, and critically assess their clinical relevance.

 - Demonstrated scientific leadership of clinical studies, with hands-on ownership from study design and protocol development through analysis, interpretation and reporting. Your work has informed product development, regulatory submissions or clinical implementation.

 - Strong quantitative judgement: you can define and defend sample sizes, endpoints, reference standards and analysis plans. You understand common pitfalls in diagnostic accuracy and AI validation studies, including selection bias, data leakage and inappropriate comparators, and how to address them.

 - Hands-on fluency with AI and data, including practical proficiency in Python or R, an understanding of how modern machine learning and foundation models are developed and evaluated, and regular use of large language models in your work.

 - A working understanding of how evidence maps to regulatory and ethics pathways, including FDA and UK MHRA requirements, EU MDR and ISO 14155. You can translate these into appropriate study designs in partnership with regulatory affairs specialists.

 - Experience in a fast-moving, product-led environment, such as a technology company, medtech scale-up or applied research lab, and a clear preference for working this way. You can work independently, prioritise across programmes and make sound scientific decisions under uncertainty.

 - Clear communication with scientific, clinical, technical and executive audiences, including the ability to explain findings, limitations and their implications for development and clinical use.


PREFERRED

 - Experience developing and validating medical devices, diagnostics or medical AI.

 - Experience with physiological sensing, medical imaging, novel biomarkers or multimodal diagnostic technologies.

 - Experience with clinical studies across multiple sites or countries.

 - Experience mentoring scientists and building productive collaborations with academic and clinical partners.

jobs.title: Risk Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
At Mudflap, we're modernizing the $1 trillion trucking industry, the backbone of the U.S. economy. By helping over 100,000 underserved small businesses save over $1.5 billion on fuel, Mudflap has quickly grown into a profitable fintech platform that processes billions in annual payment volume.



We are seeking a Risk Operations Analyst to own our Risk Ops queue on the evening shift, reporting to the Head of Customer Success. Risk Operations decides, in real time, who gets on and stays on the Mudflap network: verifying identities, investigating suspicious activity, and resolving account blocks. Our job is to stop fraud and losses without turning away good customers. We're the healthy friction, and we're proud of how we treat customers while doing it. You'll work alongside our customer-obsessed teams, resolving cases quickly and fairly. This is an exempt position with minimum coverage expectations of Sunday through Thursday, 12:00–8:00 PM Pacific Time. Your calls land on real fleets and drivers.



Work Location: This role is based in the bay area and involves a hybrid work approach, balancing in-office collaboration with the ability to work remotely.



To support our team, we offer:

 - Commuter benefits to ease your travel

 - Lunches and snacks to keep you fueled

 - A collaborative, high-growth environment where you’ll work closely with talented teammates across the company



Expectations (In this role, you will):

 - Own the Risk Ops queue: claim, investigate, and resolve identity-verification, account-block, and fraud-escalation cases from start to finish

 - Move fast without cutting corners: get to new cases quickly, keep work from going stale, and end each shift with a clear queue and clean handoff notes for the daytime team

 - Investigate using transaction data, identity and device signals, and our case-management tools, and document your evidence and reasoning so every decision is consistent and auditable

 - Make calibrated calls within policy and escalate the ones outside it, weighing the cost of fraud against the cost of turning away a good customer

 - Partner with Customer Success on escalations and handoffs so legitimate customers get unblocked quickly, with clear communication

 - Spot emerging fraud patterns and repeat false positives, and bring recommendations that make our controls smarter and reduce unnecessary friction

 - Contribute to the SOPs, macros, and quality reviews that keep the team's decisions consistent

 - You'll be measured on how quickly you respond to and resolve cases and on the quality of your decisions, which we review together in regular calibration sessions. Collections, disputes and chargebacks, and payment arrangements sit with our Payment Operations team and are outside this role.



Experience (What we look for):

 - 1–3 years in queue-based, judgment-heavy work such as fraud or risk operations, trust and safety, KYC/identity verification, payments support, or escalated customer support

 - Comfortable owning a fast-moving queue and ending each shift with it under control

 - Sound judgment under ambiguity: you stay appropriately skeptical without assuming every customer is a bad actor

 - Clear, concise writing; your case notes are read by teammates and sometimes by customers

 - Comfortable working with data in ticketing systems and spreadsheets; SQL or BI tools are a plus

 - Available to work Sunday through Thursday, 12:00–8:00 PM Pacific Time

 - Experience in payments, financial services, fuel, or trucking is a plus but not required



Perks and Benefits (What we offer):

 - Competitive salary and equity in a high-growth startup

 - Multiple health benefit options

 - Responsible Time Off

 - 401(k) matching

 - Opportunities and support for major career growth

 - Annual company offsite event (Mudfest!)



The salary range for this role is $80,000–$90,000. This information reflects a base salary range for this position based on current market data, which may be subject to change as new data becomes available. The candidate's skills, experience, and other relevant factors will determine the exact compensation.



Company Overview (Who we are):

Mudflap is on a mission to transform the trucking and logistics industry by leveling the playing field for owner-operators and small fleets. Backed by top-tier venture investors—including QED, Matrix Partners, Commerce Ventures, NFX, and 500 Startups—and featured on the Forbes Fintech 50 list, Mudflap offers fleet fuel management solutions. Our core team hails from Disney, Uber, Procore, DoorDash, Google, Meta, Capital One, Affirm, and Brex.



Here are the core values that we believe in and look for in new teammates:

 - Be Customer Obsessed: We deeply understand customer needs and put our customers at the center of everything we do

 - Make It Count: Act like an owner by focusing on the impact of your work

 - Find a Way: Be a creative problem solver who pushes past roadblocks to win for our customers and teammates

 - Sweat the Details: We keep our standards high and achieve them by paying attention to every detail

 - Be Curious: Use a growth mindset to question assumptions, take calculated risks, and stretch the boundaries of what’s possible

jobs.title: Senior Scientist II, Recombinant Peptide Process Development
jobs.description:
AbbVie’s Biologics CMC organization develops processes to support the advancement and manufacture of biologic medicines. AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated scientist to lead development of microbial-based recombinant peptide production processes. This position will serve as a technical lead across expression-system and strain development, fermentation, recovery, purification, and scale-up.

Recombinant production of short peptides can be challenging due to intracellular degradation, low expression, aggregation, and limited solubility. The successful candidate will develop and optimize practical strategies to address these challenges and advance robust, scalable processes for therapeutic peptide production. When aligned with program needs, the candidate will also evaluate and apply genetic code expansion (GCE) strategies to enable the site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids. The role will collaborate with cross-functional partners and contribute to process development, technology evaluation, and technology transfer activities.

Responsibilities:

• Lead recombinant peptide process-development activities, including expression strategy, host and clone screening, process optimization, and scale-up.
• Design and evaluate expression constructs and microbial hosts, including Escherichia coli and yeast, for peptide production.
• Develop and assess fusion-tag and carrier-protein strategies—including His-tag, GST, SUMO, and inclusion-body expression—to improve peptide stability, expression, host tolerance, and recovery.
• Design and conduct clone-screening studies using microscale cultivation, parallel bioreactors, and other appropriate scale-down or high-throughput approaches.
• Develop and optimize peptide recovery processes, including cell harvest and lysis, inclusion-body isolation and processing, and chemical or enzymatic cleavage of fusion partners.
• Troubleshoot peptide-specific process challenges, such as aggregation, low solubility, degradation, incomplete cleavage, and co-eluting impurities; recommend and pursue appropriate solutions.
• Interpret analytical results, including HPLC, UPLC, and LC-MS data, to assess peptide identity, mass accuracy, purity, and process-related impurities; partner with analytical teams to address characterization needs.
• Evaluate emerging technologies and process approaches for recombinant peptide production, including genetic code expansion when relevant to program needs.
• Apply AI/ML approaches, where appropriate, to analyze peptide sequence, structure, and experimental data in support of design, optimization, and candidate prioritization.
• Communicate scientific plans, progress, challenges, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to project teams and other stakeholders.
• Mentor junior scientists and provide technical direction in recombinant peptide bioprocessing.
• Contribute to scientific publications and presentations at conferences, as appropriate.
• Maintain a high level of productivity while managing priorities and timelines; follow applicable corporate standards for safety, quality, and compliance.

• PhD with typically 4+ years of relevant experience, master’s degree or equivalent education with 10+ years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree or equivalent education with typically 12+ years of relevant experience is required.
• Thorough theoretical and practical understanding of relevant scientific disciplines, with hands-on experience in microbial physiology and recombinant expression systems, particularly E. coli and/or yeast.
• Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to address scientific or development questions.
• Experience developing or optimizing expression processes for peptides, small proteins, or other products susceptible to degradation, or instability.
• Experience with strain or clone screening, fermentation, and process optimization; familiarity with bioreactors and scale-down or parallel cultivation approaches.
• Demonstrated experience with preparative chromatography and peptide or protein purification, as well as peptide recovery and fusion-partner cleavage strategies.
• Strong experimental design, data interpretation, troubleshooting, scientific writing, and oral communication skills.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities and timelines and work effectively in a matrixed, cross-functional environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience developing or manufacturing complex therapeutic peptides, particularly GLP-1 or related incretin peptides, in a pharmaceutical or biotechnology company or start-up environment.
• Experience applying genetic code expansion to incorporate non-canonical amino acids at defined positions using engineered orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs and codon reassignment.

We are looking for a Distribution Center Assistant Supervisor to join our Platt team in Sumner, WA!

Summary:

The Distribution Center Assistant Supervisor is responsible for helping coordinate and supervise all activities performed by Distribution Center employees under their charge daily. In the absence of the Distribution Center Supervisor will be responsible for all aspects of the job tasks within their department.

What You'll Do:

Job Duties Disclaimer:

The information contained in this job description is intended to describe the essential job functions required of those assigned to this job. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to perform the job. Please note that management retains the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. jobs.title: Assistant Director, Leave and Accommodation
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Asset Living is a third-party management firm with a proven partner in fostering thriving communities nationwide. Founded in 1986, Asset Living has decades of experience delivering exceptional value to our partners. Since the beginning, our undeniable passion has driven our organic growth from a small property management firm to one of the most trusted allies in real estate. Asset Living's growing portfolio includes a multitude of properties across the country that span the multifamily, single-family home rentals, affordable housing, build-to-rent, active adult, and student housing divisions.

Asset Living is a fast-growing company made up of talented individuals from diverse backgrounds that differentiate us and help us drive innovation and results for our clients and communities across the US. At Asset Living, we wholeheartedly believe 'Together We Lead, Together We Succeed. We empower each other to lead by example, collaborate, and evolve – inspired by our belief that we can continually improve as individuals and as an organization. Together, we create an environment where every voice is heard, every idea is valued, and every individual experiences opportunities to grow as our company grows. When you join Asset Living, you become part of a dynamic team that thrives on unity, unique talents, and a universal culture of winning.

Recognized as one of the nation's Best and Brightest Places to Work and ranked in the NMHC top 50 professionals, join Asset Living because of its reputation as the most trusted partner in real estate, workplace culture, and growth opportunities. Asset Living is a member of The Institute of Real Estate Management (IREM) and is recognized as an Accredited Management Organization (AMO). Together, we lead the way, and together, we achieve excellence in all that we do. Join a workplace where success is a collective journey and leadership is a shared responsibility.

Assistant Director, Leave and Accommodation

The Assistant Director, Leave and Accommodation provides leadership and operational oversight for the organization’s leave of absence and workplace accommodation programs. The Assistant Director leads complex case strategy, serves as an escalation point for high-risk or sensitive matters, and partners with employees, operational leaders, Human Resources, Benefits, Payroll, Employee Relations, third-party administrators, and Legal.

This position directly supervises the Leave & Accommodations Specialists and is accountable for caseload oversight, work allocation, quality review, coaching, process improvement, reporting, and program governance. The Assistant Director also maintains an assigned caseload of complex matters and provides practical guidance when leave or accommodation issues intersect with performance, attendance, discipline, organizational changes, return-to-work planning, or separation decisions.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

• Lead the day-to-day administration of leave and accommodation programs, establish service expectations, monitor workflows, and promote consistent practices across the organization.

• Directly supervise the Leave & Accommodations Specialist, including assigning work, reviewing case strategy and documentation, providing coaching and training, monitoring deadlines and service levels, and supporting professional development.

• Independently manage and provide direction on high-risk or complex cases involving extended or indefinite leave, intermittent leave, medical restrictions, pregnancy-related limitations, mental health conditions, overlapping protections, alternative placement, hardship considerations, and disputed documentation or determinations.

• Guide and document the ADA interactive process; evaluate requested accommodations and effective alternatives; coordinate implementation; assess operational impact and potential undue hardship; and partner with Legal on sensitive or unresolved matters.

• Oversee eligibility, certification, designation, extensions, recertification, exhaustion, reduced schedules, military leave, state paid leave programs, personal leave, disability-related matters, and return-to-work requirements under applicable federal, state, local, and company programs.

• Serve as the primary escalation point when protected leave or accommodation matters intersect with performance management, attendance, discipline, retaliation concerns, organizational changes, or proposed separation. Identify risk and recommend compliant, practical next steps.

• Provide clear, compassionate, and practical guidance regarding employee responsibilities, documentation requirements, timelines, restrictions, available options, and company processes. Coach leaders on maintaining confidentiality and avoiding interference, retaliation, or inconsistent treatment.

• Manage relationships with third-party leave and accommodation administrators, monitor claim handling and service quality, address discrepancies, and coordinate with Benefits, Payroll, Employee Relations, HR leadership, Safety, and Legal.

• Oversee return-to-work planning, medical releases, restrictions, modified duty, transitional work, schedule changes, accommodation implementation, alternative placement considerations, and related stakeholder communication.

• Conduct routine audits of leave and accommodation files, intermittent leave usage, reduced schedules, documentation, designations, restrictions, status changes, and return-to-work activity. Correct gaps and use findings to improve processes and training.

• Develop and maintain reporting on caseload volume, aging, response times, leave types, accommodation activity, return-to-work outcomes, vendor performance, trends, and areas of compliance or operational risk.

• Develop and maintain policies, procedures, templates, resources, manager guidance, and training. Monitor legal and regulatory developments and recommend updates to practices and communications.

• Ensure leave status, return dates, timekeeping, pay-related changes, benefit considerations, restrictions, and employee records are communicated and processed accurately and timely in applicable systems.

• Maintain complete, accurate, and confidential case records, including medical documentation, correspondence, approvals, restrictions, timelines, analyses, and decisions. Limit access to sensitive information based on business need.

• Partner with HR and operational leaders to evaluate staffing impacts, temporary coverage, workforce planning, and business continuity associated with leaves and accommodations.

• Support broader HR compliance initiatives, special projects, audits, acquisitions or transitions, and other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience

• Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred. Equivalent relevant experience may be considered.

• Five or more years of progressive Human Resources experience preferred, including substantial direct experience with leave administration and workplace accommodations. Prior leadership, team-lead, or supervisory experience strongly preferred.

• Advanced working knowledge of FMLA, ADA, USERRA, pregnancy-related accommodation requirements, state and local leave laws, paid leave programs, disability benefits coordination, and the interactive accommodation process.

• Demonstrated ability to administer leave and accommodation matters across multiple jurisdictions and identify when state or local requirements provide additional protections.

• Ability to set expectations, prioritize team workloads, coach performance, review work product, resolve escalations, and build consistent and accountable practices.

• Strong critical-thinking and decision-making skills, including the ability to analyze medical and operational information, distinguish routine from high-risk matters, and escalate appropriately.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain sensitive or complex requirements clearly and professionally to employees and leaders at all levels.

• Ability to manage a high-volume and complex caseload while overseeing team deliverables, competing deadlines, audits, projects, and timely follow-up.

• Ability to analyze trends, maintain meaningful metrics, evaluate vendor performance, and translate findings into practical process improvements.

• Demonstrated discretion in handling medical information and other sensitive employee records in accordance with confidentiality requirements.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and experience with HRIS, case-management, ticketing, payroll, benefits, or leave-administration systems.

• Ability to remain calm, professional, empathetic, and solutions-oriented during difficult conversations and in a fast-paced, changing environment.

This job description should not be considered all-inclusive. It is merely a guide of expected duties. The employee understands that the job description is neither complete nor permanent and may be modified at any time. At the request of their supervisor, an employee may be asked to perform additional duties or take on additional responsibilities without notice.

jobs.title: Director, SOX Compliance & Internal Controls
jobs.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.
Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

Fivetran is building a SOX Compliance function from the ground up. Reporting directly to the Chief Accounting Officer (CAO), the Director, SOX Compliance & Internal Controls will design and stand up Fivetran’s internal controls program using the COSO framework. This will include risk and control matrices (RCMs), narratives, and test plans for both business process controls and IT application controls/IT general controls (ITACs/ITGCs). The individual will own the relationship with third-party control-testing providers and the external audit team (KPMG) as the company moves through its SOX readiness and 404(a) compliance.

This is a highly visible, build-phase mandate. You will have significant latitude and accountability to shape the control environment, tooling, and governance model that Fivetran will operate on. You will partner closely with Accounting, India CoE, FP&A, Legal, HROps, Revenue, IT/Engineering, Security, and every control owner across the business.

This is a full-time, hybrid position based out of our Oakland, CA office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including one day in the office each week to connect and build as a team.

What You’ll Do

SOX Program Build & Governance

▪ Design, build, and lead Fivetran’s end-to-end SOX 404 compliance program in accordance with the COSO 2013 framework and 404(b) integrated audit standards.

▪ Lead the risk assessment and scoping process (significant accounts, processes, and locations) in partnership with the external auditors.

▪ Build and maintain the company’s risk and control matrices (RCMs), process narratives, and flowcharts across key financial processes, including order-to-cash/revenue, procure-to-pay, payroll and equity compensation, treasury, financial close and reporting, tax and entity-level controls.

▪ Design and document control activities (preventive and detective, manual and automated) that are efficient, right-sized, and audit-ready.

▪ Build a SOX/GRC workflow tool using AI to manage controls, testing, issues, and evidence.

ITGC / ITAC & IT Risk

▪ Partner with Engineering, IT, and Security to design and test IT general controls (access management, change management, computer operations/backups) and IT application controls (automated controls, interfaces, system-generated reports/IPE) across in-scope systems (NetSuite, Coupa, Salesforce CRM, Workday, data warehouse, AI-agents built using frontier AI models and other SaaS solutions).

▪ Build segregation-of-duties (SoD) analysis and monitoring across key financial systems.

▪ Serve as the trusted advisor to technical teams on control design for new systems, integrations, and process changes, including evaluating SOC 1/SOC 2 reports from key vendors and determining reliance.

Testing, Third Parties & External Audit

▪ Develop test plans and testing strategies (design and operating effectiveness) for all in-scope controls, both business-process and ITGC/ITAC.

▪ Engage, manage, and oversee third-party co-source/outsource providers performing SOX control testing, including scoping the engagement, setting standards for workpaper quality, and reviewing their results before sharing with external auditors.

▪ Own the primary relationship with KPMG (external auditor) for all SOX/ICFR matters, coordinate walkthroughs, manage the PBC (prepared-by-client) request list, present testing results and evidence, and resolve open items in real time.

▪ Track, evaluate, and drive remediation of control deficiencies (design and operating) through to closure, including root-cause analysis and retesting; assess and present deficiency severity (deficiency / significant deficiency / material weakness) to management.

▪ Prepare periodic reporting on SOX program status, testing results, and open issues for the CAO, CFO, and ultimately the Audit Committee.

Business Partnership & Enablement

▪ Act as the organization’s go-to resource on internal controls, including training and coaching control owners on their responsibilities, control execution, and evidence standards.

▪ Embed controls into new processes, systems, and M&A integrations as the company grows, favoring automation and “preventive at the source” design over manual detective controls.

▪ Monitor changes in the business (new products, new systems, new revenue streams, acquisitions) for control impact and update scoping/documentation accordingly.

▪ Build the long-term operating rhythm as the SOX program matures, which includes quarterly control self-assessments, quarterly sales questionnaire, related party certifications, etc.

Skills We're Looking For

▪ 10+ years of progressive experience in internal audit, SOX/internal controls, or external audit, including meaningful time in public accounting (Big 4 or large national firm) with a SOX/ICFR, IT audit, or integrated audit focus.

▪ Demonstrated experience either taking a company through IPO/SOX readiness and a first-year 404(b) audit, or leading an established public-company SOX program at technology/SaaS industry strongly preferred.

▪ Deep, hands-on knowledge of the COSO Internal Control Integrated Framework and PCAOB auditing standards.

▪ Strong command of both business process controls (O2C, P2P, R2R, Payroll & Equity, Treasury, Tax) and ITGC/ITAC concepts. Able to converse credibly with engineers on system architecture and control design, not just with accountants.

▪ Direct experience managing or co-sourcing control testing with third-party providers, and owning the day-to-day relationship with a Big 4 external audit team.

Bonus Skills​

▪ Preferred Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

▪ CPA, CIA, and/or CISA certification.

▪ Experience with NetSuite (or comparable ERP), Salesforce, and modern data/billing stacks typical of a usage-based business.

▪ Prior experience as the first or founding SOX hire at a pre-IPO company (building the function from zero).

▪ Familiarity with SOC 1 Type II report evaluation and vendor/subservice organization risk.

▪ Project management skills (PMP/PMO exposure a plus) given the scoping, timeline, and cross-functional coordination demands of a readiness program.

jobs.title: Scientist II, Fermentation Process Development – Recombinant Peptides
jobs.description:
AbbVie’s Biologics CMC organization develops processes to support the advancement and manufacture of biologic medicines. AbbVie is seeking a motivated fermentation scientist to contribute to the development of microbial processes for recombinant peptide production. The successful candidate will perform hands-on fermentation studies and help develop, optimize, and scale upstream processes for therapeutic peptides. This role will collaborate with colleagues in strain development, downstream processing, analytical development, and other functions to generate reliable data and support project goals.

Responsibilities

• Independently design, execute, and interpret critical fermentation experiments to answer scientific questions and advance project goals.
• Develop and optimize microbial cultivation and fermentation processes, including work with hosts such as Escherichia coli and yeast.
• Evaluate the effects of media composition, inoculum conditions, feed strategies, induction conditions, temperature, pH, agitation, aeration, and dissolved oxygen on growth and product expression.
• Operate, maintain, and optimize bench-scale bioreactors and support microscale, parallel, and scale-down fermentation studies.
• Apply broad technical proficiency to troubleshoot experiments, instrumentation, and routine process issues; adapt or innovate protocols and techniques as project needs evolve.
• Collaborate with strain-development colleagues to screen and characterize microbial clones and expression systems.
• Analyze fermentation data—including growth, substrate use, process parameters, product titer, and yield—and place findings in the relevant scientific context.
• Troubleshoot experiments and instrumentation, adapting or developing methods to meet changing project needs.
• Collaborate with strain-development, downstream-processing, and analytical teams to assess expression, peptide recovery, and product quality.
• Consult relevant scientific literature and use it to inform experimental design, interpret findings, and solve technical problems.
• Set and meet experimental timelines, communicate plans and results, contribute to technical documentation, and improve laboratory methods and operations.
• Follow applicable corporate standards for conduct, safety, material handling, and GxP compliance, as relevant to the work.

• Master’s degree or equivalent with 5+ years of relevant experience or Bachelor’s degree or equivalent with 7+ years of relevant experience, is required.
• Theoretical and practical knowledge of microbial cultivation and fermentation, preferably using E. coli and/or yeast.
• Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to answer scientific questions.
• Demonstrated ability to develop, adapt, and optimize experimental methods and techniques in response to project needs.
• Experience operating bioreactors and applying fermentation parameters such as pH, temperature, agitation, aeration, and dissolved oxygen.
• Ability to troubleshoot experiments and instrumentation, recognize significant deviations, and determine appropriate follow-up work.
• Strong scientific writing, verbal communication, data interpretation, and presentation skills.
• Ability to consult and apply relevant scientific literature and to communicate findings in the context of project objectives.
• Ability to manage multiple assignments, meet timelines, and work effectively with cross-functional collaborators.

jobs.title: Principal Compensation Partner
jobs.description:
About Checkr
Checkr is building the data platform to power safe and fair decisions. Over 140,000 companies and millions of people rely on Checkr for AI verification in the moments that matter most: getting a new job, a new place to live, a car ride, childcare, even a date. Customers include Uber, Pennymac, Airbnb, Doordash, and Anthropic.

We’re a team that thrives on solving complex problems with innovative solutions that advance our mission. Checkr is recognized on Forbes Cloud 100 2025 List and is a Y Combinator 2024 Breakthrough Company.

About the role

Checkr’s growth is fueled by exceptional talent, and how we reward that talent matters. We are looking for a Principal Compensation Partner to be a senior individual contributor and trusted advisor on compensation and total rewards, helping us attract, retain, and motivate the best people as we scale. You will report to the VP of Total Rewards and People Ops, and partner directly with Executives, Directors, People Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance, and Legal to plan, build, communicate, and administer compensation programs that support Checkr’s overall strategy. Your work will touch our short- and long-term incentives, reward and recognition programs, benchmarking and survey analysis, and more.

This is a builder’s role. You will bring a business mindset, quantitative rigor, and a bias for action to a company that is growing fast, and you will have real ownership over how our compensation approach evolves. Join us and be part of a mission-driven company that is passionate about investing in our people! Hybrid schedule and office location: Denver

In this role you will

• Be a trusted advisor in the room. Partner directly with Executives, Directors, senior HR leaders, and Talent Acquisition to shape compensation strategies that fit Checkr’s philosophy while meeting the needs of each organization, including calibration sessions, offer discussions, and complex pay decisions.

• Own the strategy and the programs. Develop and maintain our compensation and rewards strategy and guidelines, ensuring a fair, equitable, and competitive total rewards approach, and be the subject-matter expert on our bi-annual performance review cycle, pay equity, compensation guidelines, job families, annual salary review, and equity refresh program.

• Take a whole-picture view of total rewards. Help evaluate how cash, equity, benefits, 401(k), leave, and recognition programs fit together, and bring ideas that strengthen Checkr’s overall rewards offering.

• Solve problems that don’t have obvious answers. Develop creative, data-driven solutions to complex compensation challenges, balancing competitiveness, equity, risk, and reward.

• Go deep on the data. Build compensation models, conduct statistical analysis, assess market competitiveness, and model the impact of alternatives so leaders can make informed decisions.

• Use AI and automation to build mechanisms that scale. Partner with Total Rewards and People Ops technology teams to implement tools that improve efficiency, operational excellence, and insight across the function.

• Drive job architecture and market pricing. Lead job evaluation, leveling, and market pricing across all job families and levels, and lead market-based compensation survey participation, annual benchmarking, and the market research review process.

• Educate and communicate. Create policy and program documentation, lead change management for new or updated compensation practices, and teach managers and employees about Checkr’s compensation philosophy, job descriptions, and leveling framework.

• Support executive compensation and provide insight to leadership on executive pay decisions.

• Partner across the company. Work closely with Total Rewards, Stock Administration, Finance, Legal, and third-party vendors to deliver programs accurately and on time, and support pay equity and pay transparency efforts.

• Mentor and lead projects. Coach teammates and partners on the business impact behind compensation decisions, and lead a variety of HR and compensation-related projects, including ad-hoc studies and analysis.

• Be a proactive problem solver. Spot skill gaps, offer solutions before you’re asked, and use judgment about when to move fast and when to slow down.

What you bring

• 8–10+ years of compensation experience partnering with leaders and stakeholders on compensation recommendations and decisions, ideally in a fast-growing, global tech company

• Strong command of compensation fundamentals, including job architecture and leveling, job evaluation methodologies, market pricing, equity mechanics, bonus/incentive and commission plan design, compensation structures, pay ranges, testing, auditing, and reporting

• Experience designing and implementing compensation programs, including salary structures, bonus, and long-term incentive programs

• Expertise in compensation benchmarking and survey methodology (for example Radford, Mercer, Compa, or Pave)

• Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate data and trends into clear insights and recommendations

• Strong executive presence, with the ability to communicate complex topics clearly and to influence decisions without direct authority

• Working knowledge of stock administration, payroll, benefits and 401(k) programs, ideally including experience with self-funded health plans (for example plan cost modeling, stop-loss, or working with a TPA or broker)

• Experience administering equity programs in a pre-IPO stage

• Proven ability to prioritize and drive multiple projects to completion and meet deadlines, with strong attention to detail and organization

• A passion for educating and mentoring partners on the values and business impact behind compensation strategy

• An A-player mindset with a strong bias for action: you raise the bar, move with urgency, stay resilient through ambiguity, and take ownership to deliver meaningful outcomes

Nice to have

• Experience building compensation programs from the ground up in a high-growth, hyper-scaling environment

• Experience leading compensation initiatives in a matrix-led organization

• Experience with mergers and acquisitions, including compensation harmonization and integration

• Experience with sales compensation

jobs.title: Site Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Site Lead to own site readiness, transport, installation and startup coordination for our microreactor deliveries. You will make sure the site, the customer and the delivery team are aligned so that each unit arrives at a prepared site and starts up successfully. You will work closely with Engineering, Program Management, Regulatory, Production, and will report to the Director of Mission Success. The ideal candidate has hands-on field experience, is comfortable with logistics and heavy transport, and can work with customers on their own sites, including DoD installations.

Responsibilities & Duties:

 - Site Readiness: Develop and own the site readiness plan and report its status to required teams.

 - Requirements & Interfaces: Gather site requirements and design interfaces from Engineering and confirm they are met on site.

 - Customer Coordination: Coordinate site access and constraints with the customer.

 - Transport & Installation: Plan and coordinate transport, installation and setup of the reactor system at the customer site.

 - Regulatory Conditions: Make sure site activities meet programmatic conditions set by applicable regulations.

 - Production Alignment: Coordinate site timing with Production’s completion dates.

 - Schedule Input: Provide site milestones to the scheduling team and flag slips early.

 - Startup & Acceptance: Coordinate startup, commissioning and customer acceptance.

 - Safety & Permitting: Make sure site work meets safety and permitting requirements.

Deliverables:

 - Site readiness plan; ongoing regular status updates.

 - Site milestones in the integrated schedule.

 - Completed transport, installation and startup at each customer site.

 - Coordinated startup and acceptance with the customer.

 - Site-level risks documented and shared for the non-technical Risk Register.

Required Qualifications & Skills:

 - Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management or a related field, or equivalent experience.

 - 8+ years of field, construction or operations management experience.

 - Experience with logistics and heavy transport.

 - Knowledge of site safety and permitting requirements.

 - Experience coordinating with customers on their sites.

 - Strong problem-solving skills in the field.

Desired Qualifications & Skills:

 - Experience managing a complex construction project from start to finish.

 - Experience working on DoD installations.

 - Experience in nuclear or other regulated industries.
   

Additional Requirements:

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must be willing to travel 40% or more of total weeks in the year; most travel will be consolidated around reactor delivery and testing

 - Must work onsite at El Segundo HQ whenever not traveling.


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Senior Business Director
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We are an award-winning independent creative solutions company that aspires to be the most culturally-influential company in the world. We help ambitious brands harness the power of culture to solve their biggest challenges. As a unique mix of experts in culture, technology, and storytelling, we are united by a passion to grow brands in ways that advertising alone can never do.

We are an entrepreneurial business – not a traditional “ad agency.” That means we value resourcefulness and tenacity just as much as we value creativity and intelligence. We’re unapologetically ambitious!

We are looking for a Senior Business Director to join Translation!

The Senior Business Director is a senior client and business leader responsible for the success, growth, and health of a significant, complex account. This person has already demonstrated success at the Business Director level and brings greater executive influence, commercial judgment, and organizational leadership. They will serve as a strategic advisor to senior clients, lead integrated teams, and remain close to the work while actively shaping and pushing clients forward in culture.

What You'll Do

• Own the overall health, performance, growth, and senior client relationships for a flagship national account.

• Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to Director-level stakeholders, shaping agendas, influencing decisions, and constructively challenging clients with a clear point of view.

• Translate complex business, consumer, category, and cultural dynamics into clear strategic direction and stronger creative work.

• Lead integrated teams across Business Leadership, Strategy, Context, Creative, Program Management, Production, Analytics, and Partner Agencies, creating clarity around objectives, priorities, roles, and decisions.

• Ensure work meets Translation’s standards for strategic rigor, creative ambition, cultural excellence, and client readiness before presentation.

• Develop and drive the organic growth strategy, identifying and converting opportunities across stakeholders, business units, audiences, and workstreams.

• Co-own account financial health with Program Management, including revenue, profitability, staffing, forecasting, scope performance, and investment recommendations.

• Anticipate relationship, delivery, and commercial risks, intervening before they affect the client partnership, the quality of the work, team health, or profitability.

• Lead, coach, and develop Business Supervisors through clear expectations, ongoing feedback, performance reviews, and meaningful development opportunities.

• Contribute to agency leadership through new business, recruiting, shaping departmental standards, cross-functional improvements, and the development of future Business Leadership talent.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Exceptional business judgment and the ability to connect marketing decisions to broader client goals, organizational dynamics, and commercial outcomes.

• Executive presence and communication skills, including the ability to read complex rooms, tailor counsel to different stakeholders, and navigate sensitive issues with discretion.

• Strong strategic fluency and the ability to turn ambiguity into clear, actionable direction without prescribing the creative solution.

• Commercial acumen across scopes, staffing models, forecasting, profitability, and investment decisions.

• Ability to lead and inspire multidisciplinary teams, resolve tension constructively, and create accountability without relying solely on hierarchy.

• A growth mindset, with the curiosity and proactivity to identify unmet client needs and translate them into meaningful opportunities.

• Cultural fluency and a strong understanding of how contemporary culture, audiences, and communities influence brands and business.

• Sound prioritization and decision-making skills in a high-volume, fast-moving, and highly visible client environment.

• A coaching orientation and the ability to raise the performance, confidence, and judgment of other leaders.

• Ability to balance client needs, creative ambition, executional feasibility, team sustainability, and financial health.

Minimum Qualifications

• 10+ years of experience leading integrated client relationships within a creative, marketing, or communications agency, including demonstrated success operating at the Business Director or equivalent level.

• Proven experience owning senior client relationships, complex integrated campaigns, organic growth, account economics, and cross-functional team leadership for a major consumer brand.

• Demonstrated experience coaching and developing account leadership talent while independently navigating high-stakes client and business decisions.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading a large, complex, or matrixed national account across multiple stakeholders and workstreams.

• Experience in QSR, retail, CPG, telecom, financial services, sports, entertainment, or another high-velocity consumer category.

• Experience working within/leading an integrated agency team or multi-agency ecosystem.

• Experience leading culturally specific or multicultural marketing while connecting the work to a broader brand and business strategy.

• Track record of identifying and converting organic growth opportunities.

• Experience leading scope development, staffing recommendations, forecasting, and profitability management.

• Experience supporting new business pitches, agency initiatives, recruiting, or talent development.

About UnitedMasters, Inc.

UnitedMasters Inc. represents the creative solutions company, Translation, and the leading software and services platform for independent creators, UnitedMasters. UnitedMasters enables ownership, exposure, and new paths for financial return for independent creators, while Translation helps brands leverage the power of contemporary culture to achieve transformational growth. Combined, UnitedMasters, Inc. is the world’s leading marketplace for cultural capital, connecting independent artists and brands to realize a future in which all creators own their future. jobs.title: Staff Backend Engineer - Performance - US
jobs.description:
About Teleport

Don't wait for the future of infrastructure. Be part of it.

Teleport is the AI Infrastructure Identity Company. We're solving one of the hardest problems in security: giving every human, machine, workload, and AI agent a cryptographically secured identity, improving engineering velocity while maintaining security. We make trusted computing simple. This gives you the freedom, power, and autonomy to build and innovate with confidence.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we work with companies like Nasdaq, DoorDash, and Elastic to secure infrastructure for an AI world.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for product-focused systems engineers to work on Teleport Core Product.

You will work on problems ranging from performance and scalability, security and networking, to integrations with external systems.

You will work on the full product lifecycle from working with customers to understand their problems, writing RFDs for your proposed design, implementing, testing, and documenting.

Teleport is an open core project, and most of the code you will write will be open source and written in Go.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Become an expert on scalability, performance, and reliability of Teleport in large deployments.

 - Design, develop, and ship outstanding, high-quality products.

 - Lead a distributed team of outstanding engineers.

 - Write most of the code in Go.

 - Closely collaborate with other teams at Teleport on matters related to scalability and performance.

 - Work directly with our customers to diagnose and remediate performance issues.

 - Grow your technical expertise.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Willingness to work collaboratively with Teleport's engineers on coding challenge in Go https://github.com/gravitational/careers/blob/main/challenges/systems/challenge-1.md as part of the interview process.

 - Builder mentality and experience -- you love being hands-on and building zero-to-one products.

 - Extensive Go experience.

 - Extensive experience developing scalable, reliable, and performant distributed systems and platforms.

 - Strong team leadership.

 - Engineering management experience.

 - Linux systems engineering experience.

 - Knowledge of Identity Management, RBAC, ABAC, and zero-trust security models.

 - Intellectual curiosity and a willingness to master new technologies.

 - Transparency, honesty, and a no-ego mindset.

 - Significant contributions in Open Source is a big plus.




HOW WE HIRE

Our process is designed to be straightforward and respectful of your time. We skip performative rounds and focus on what matters: understanding how you think and what you can do.

For this role, we use a take-home challenge that mirrors real work at Teleport — on your time, your way. You'll have support from the team throughout.

 1. Zoom meeting with a Teleport recruiter. You’ll learn about the company, our products, compensation philosophy, interview process, and key requirements.

 2. Zoom meeting with the Hiring Manager. The Hiring Manager will walk you through the coding challenge and answer your questions.

 3. Coding challenge collaboration. The day after your meeting with the Hiring Manager, you join a Slack channel and complete a coding challenge in Go https://github.com/gravitational/careers/blob/main/challenges/systems/challenge-1.md using GitHub. The challenge usually takes about 2 weeks and ends with a Zoom meeting with the Hiring Manager and a member of the interview team to review your solution.

 4. If your challenge solution meets our bar, you'll receive an offer to join Teleport.
    
    



Why Teleport

You're joining a company where the problem is real, the team is small, and your work shows up directly in the product. We're not a big company, you won't get lost in a crowd. You'll have the freedom and autonomy to do what you're great at, alongside teammates who care about doing it right and want to see you succeed. The work is collaborative, there's real room to grow, and the mission is one worth showing up for.

Remote-first and globally distributed, we're genuinely passionate about what we're building.



The Benefits

At Teleport, we believe your career is more important than a list of perks. That's why we focus on making your day-to-day the best it can be — giving you the autonomy, access, and support to do the best work of your career.

- Extensive health coverage

- Annual expense budget

- Rest and recovery policies that maximize your ability to recharge

- Investment in your future with retirement savings plans

- Professional development opportunities



Teleport is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, veteran status, or any classifications protected by federal, state, or local law.
