The role involves translating strategic objectives into operational processes, overseeing multiple complex projects, and fostering cross-functional collaboration. This position also emphasizes team development, portfolio management, and process optimization to align with organizational goals.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Lead and oversee a diverse team that may include Project Managers, Implementation Consultants, and other roles, ensuring effective recruitment, coaching, mentoring, and performance management.

 - Translate strategic plans into operational processes that impact both the team and cross-functional outcomes.

 - Develop and implement strategic plans aligned with organizational objectives.

 - Manage a portfolio of implementation projects, including intricate technical deployments, and support portfolio management for team members within specific product domains.

 - Identify and mitigate project and customer risks proactively, visiting customer sites as needed to maintain strong relationships and project momentum.

 - Conduct portfolio forecasting and analyze trends impacting project efficiency while monitoring budget health and project delivery.

 - Collaborate with leadership to ensure the team’s skills meet evolving business needs and contribute to improving project management methodologies.

 - Schedule projects, plan resources, manage staffing impacts, utilize metrics, and report effectively to internal and external stakeholders.

 - Support complex customer implementations involving multiple product suites and assist clients in developing and executing testing plans and procedures.

 - Apply extensive business knowledge to resolve significant project challenges, develop innovative solutions, and maintain alignment with professional services methodology.

 - Establish and maintain control over project delivery during escalations, supporting sales processes, and participating in the creation and approval of Statements of Work and Change Orders.

 - Collaborate cross-functionally with sales, customer success, product management, and engineering teams to drive internal initiatives and enhance customer outcomes.

 - Provide leadership and guidance to customers on best practices, use cases, and business process improvements.

 - Develop and maintain implementation approaches, business process documentation, and best-practice onboarding and training materials.




 REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

 - Bachelor’s degree preferred, or equivalent experience demonstrating the ability to perform the outlined tasks.

 - Minimum of 3 years of experience in project delivery, preferably in a SaaS environment.

 - Management Experience: Proven ability to foster team culture, accountability, and professional growth.

 - Excellent written and oral communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and with clients at all organizational levels.

 - Strong leadership capabilities with a focus on strategic thinking, problem-solving, and achieving results.

 - Exceptional organizational skills and ability to manage multiple initiatives with varying levels of complexity and interdependencies.

 - Demonstrated ability to balance profitability with a customer-service mindset and maintain high standards of excellence in project delivery.

 - Ability to understand and articulate product requirements, process logic, and architecture, as well as build and deliver functional presentations.

 - Capacity to adapt to evolving product offerings and address customer needs strategically.

 - Experience with government budgeting concepts, finance/budgeting solutions, procurement, permitting, licensing, asset management, or related fields is a plus.




KEY COMPETENCIES

 - Execution - The drive to achieve results and deliver intended, measurable outcomes for the business and our customers.

 - Communication - The ability to have a positive impact on others–inspiring and persuading them to buy into the vision.

 - Business Acumen - The ability to act like an owner—navigating business challenges and opportunities to deliver productive outcomes and achievement of goals.

 - Team Development - The ability to build a high-performing team–focusing on cultivating top-notch talent.




COMPENSATION 

Chicago, IL: $128,000 - $140,000



On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

 

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.

 




WHY OPENGOV?



A Mission That Matters. 

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust.  Some people say this is boring.  We think it’s the core of our democracy.



Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.



A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.



A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.



Benefits That Work for You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

 - Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families

 - Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions

 - Professional development and growth opportunities

 - A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

jobs.title: Sr Manager Sourcing
jobs.description:
Summary

This position is responsible for leading the Sourcing and Procurement functions for Universal Studios Hollywood, overseeing daily procurement operations, sourcing strategies, and supplier relationships.  The Sr. Manager will deliver procurement efficiency, beneficial spend economics and savings via utilization of sourcing strategies /best practices, on-time ordering accuracy, supplier compliance, and consistent execution across all Food & Beverage categories.  This role will also oversee sourcing readiness and onboarding for all new ventures, ensuring that new concepts are fully supported through SKU setup, vendor engagement, and procurement readiness.  Additionally, this position will serve as the primary liaison to the Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) for all R&D and New Venture sourcing efforts, ensuring alignment with Universal’s sourcing governance framework and overall corporate strategy.

This position requires a candidate with proven leadership ability to facilitate, guide, and implement improvements within the sourcing organization and operation of the company. This position will lead a team of sourcing professionals and must have the ability to motivate others to meet the challenges of a face paced, collaborative, and results driven environment. This position will work to ensure Sourcing initiatives are executed efficiently, industry best practices are adopted, and corporate Sourcing policies are adhered to for Universal’s domestic properties; may require global interaction with stakeholders and other UPR Sourcing professionals.  Travel is required.

Essential Functions

• Lead a high performing team in sourcing and procurement execution for Universal Studios Hollywood (USH) Food & Beverage, ensuring daily operational continuity, cost visibility, and vendor compliance.
• Design and implement sourcing programs, including bid specifications, distributor and manufacturer negotiations, and supplier development strategies.
• Design and execute RFX Processes- RFI, RFP, RFQ - and negotiate economically beneficial contracts with suppliers to deliver competitive product and service pricing across categories.
• Responsible for delivery of on-time ordering and accuracy for replenishment levels of warehouse and direct shipment items for responsible site and New Ventures sites
• Oversee procurement processes within Eatec/S4 to ensure accurate purchase orders, on-time delivery, and full adherence to Universal’s governance model.
• Serve as the primary liaison to the GPO for all R&D and New Venture sourcing efforts, ensuring project transparency, data accuracy, supplier compliance, and measurable value delivery.
• Coordinate cross-functional alignment with Culinary, Operations, Shared Services, and IT for USH and all new venue onboarding, including SKU creation, sourcing timelines, and supplier readiness.
• Partner with the Cost Control team to ensure budget alignment, identify cost-saving opportunities, and support margin expansion initiatives.
• Develop and maintain procurement policies and sourcing procedures to enhance efficiency, transparency, and alignment with Universal’s national sourcing governance.
• Design and execute category sourcing strategies that deliver short and long term benefits across pricing, delivery, storage and supplier utilization/management.
• Design and execute procurement ordering and replenishment strategies and/or playbooks that deliver operational efficiency and cost effectiveness across product portfolio.
• Analyze procurement data and supplier performance to identify cost reductions, supplier consolidation, and continuous improvement opportunities.
• Forecast demand and usage patterns to optimize inventory levels and procurement scheduling.
• Ensure sourcing compliance, sustainability standards, and food safety requirements are met across all vendors.
• Drive completion of key projects by proactively considering new alternatives and applying critical thinking to achieve optimal results.
• Provide leadership and mentoring to the USH Sourcing & Procurement team to promote continuous improvement, accountability, and best-in-class performance.
• Build and foster relationships by collaborating with internal stakeholders, external suppliers, and UDX leadership.
• Understand and actively participate in Environmental, Health & Safety responsibilities by following established USH policy, procedures, training and team member involvement activities.
• Various projects as assigned

Requirements:

• Minimum 7 years of progressive experience in Food & Beverage sourcing or procurement, including at least 3–5 years in a management or leadership capacity.
• Bachelor’s degree required; Certified Professional Food Manager (CPFM) preferred.
• Strong understanding of ERP systems (Eatec/S4) and procurement workflow automation. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Visio.
• Deep knowledge of multi-step strategic sourcing, bid management, and category management strategies. Proven success in cost modeling, supplier negotiation, and analytics-driven decision-making.
• Demonstrated ability to lead teams in a high-volume, fast-paced environment with multiple competing priorities. Skilled in cross-functional partnership and influencing without direct authority.
• Strong analytical acumen with the ability to translate data into insights and actions. Capable of balancing strategic vision with executional precision.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills at all organizational levels, with a focus on clarity, persuasion, and professionalism.
• Highly organized, detail-oriented, and results-driven. Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence.
• Hybrid: This position has been designated as hybrid, generally contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week.

Desired Characteristics

• Strong leader with the ability to motivate and develop a high-performing team in a collaborative, results-driven environment.
• Deep understanding of product life cycle, price elasticity, COGS, and program-building concepts.
• Demonstrated success leading sourcing and onboarding initiatives for new concepts and operational expansions.
• Experience partnering with cross-functional teams, including Culinary, Operations, and Shared Services, to deliver enterprise sourcing solutions.
• Experience working with a GPO or similar sourcing framework to deliver measurable value while maintaining compliance with corporate governance.
• Strong project management skills, including stakeholder management, forecasting, and cost analysis.
• Resourceful problem solver with the ability to prioritize, negotiate, and drive outcomes in ambiguous or high-pressure situations.
• Analytical thinker capable of developing frameworks for planning and implementing organizational change.
• Passionate, positive, and results-oriented with a continuous improvement mindset.

This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $120,000 - $140,000 (bonus eligible)

As part of our selection process, external candidates may be required to attend an in-person interview with an NBCUniversal employee at one of our locations prior to a hiring decision. NBCUniversal's policy is to provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, gender identity or expression, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, disability, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, veteran status, membership in the uniformed services, genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

NBCUniversal will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories, or arrest or conviction records, in a manner consistent with relevant legal requirements, including the City of Los Angeles' Fair Chance Initiative For Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, where applicable.

If you are a qualified individual with a disability or a disabled veteran and require support throughout the application and/or recruitment process as a result of your disability, you have the right to request a reasonable accommodation. You can submit your request to AccessibilitySupport@nbcuni.com.

jobs.title: Commercial Property Manager
jobs.description:
Commercial Property Manager
Cover letter required for consideration. Please highlight your relevant and transferable skills that make you a strong fit for this role.

About Carvana
At Carvana, we’re changing the way people buy and sell cars. With an ambitious vision and a fundamentally different approach designed to be fun, fast, and fair, Carvana became the fastest-growing automotive retailer in history. We expanded nationally, went public on the New York Stock Exchange, sold our 1 millionth car, and reached the Fortune 500, all in just eight years.

Today, with 4 million retail customers and counting, Carvana is both the fastest-growing and the most profitable public automotive retailer, and we’re just getting started. We continue to raise the bar for our customers as we tackle the enormous opportunity still ahead in the largest consumer vertical.

Working here means being part of a team that embraces change, celebrates creative problem solving, and always strives to be better. At Carvana, you’ll have the opportunity to take on meaningful challenges, learn quickly, and help shape the future of automotive retail. If you’re driven to grow and make an impact as part of a collaborative team, you’ll fit right in. Learn more about what it’s like to work here from the people that already do.

About the team and position

Carvana's Real Estate team operates in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment, supporting a rapidly expanding portfolio of commercial properties for Carvana and ADESA. We are looking for a Commercial Property Manager to join our Real Estate team at Carvana's corporate headquarters in Tempe, Arizona. This role blends day-to-day commercial lease administration and portfolio management with hands-on support for core, recurring legal tasks, working closely with our Real Estate Legal team.

This role is built for a commercial real estate professional. Our portfolio consists of all types of industrial and retail facilities. We lease, purchase, sell, finance and maintain a vast portfolio of real estate, and your familiarity with managing a commercial real estate portfolio will be key to your success. Comfort interpreting commercial lease and purchase agreement language, understanding rent roll, tax and insurance payment obligations, working with facilities teams and vendors and recognizing the workflow requiring support in commencing, operating and closing out sites in a manner that is compliant with best practices and lease obligations is essential. Candidates with a background limited to residential or multifamily property management will not have the lease-interpretation and commercial deal experience this role requires.

The ideal candidate has held an in-house/corporate real estate role or a role at a commercial property management or brokerage firm, development company, REIT, or business with a deep investment in its real estate portfolio. The responsibilities require a proactive and detail-oriented professional who delivers accurate, high-quality work quickly, communicates effectively with a wide range of internal and external stakeholders, and knows how to responsibly use AI tools to work faster and smarter. This role requires juggling multiple projects and deadlines in a dynamic environment where priorities can shift quickly.

This person will work closely with Legal, Accounting, and Insurance, as well as Facilities and Construction, demonstrating strong cross-functional collaboration and project management skills. Daily functions are expected to be handled autonomously with limited oversight, while knowing when a matter requires more context for stakeholders or should be escalated to the Manager of Portfolio Management or Legal.

This is a fully on-site position, Monday through Friday, at our corporate HQ in Tempe, Arizona.

What you’ll be doing

• Perform commercial lease abstraction and ensure data integrity of Lease Agreements, License Agreements and Purchase Agreements.

• Audit lease information to ensure key lease administrative deadlines are met and are reflected accurately in internal and external reports.

• Communicate with landlords, including handling landlord escalations and holding landlords accountable to comply with commercial lease language.

• Interpret commercial lease terms in a manner that helps Facilities, Construction and other teams understand core Landlord and Tenant contract responsibilities.

• Recognize when lease interpretations require escalation to the Senior Manager of Portfolio Management, or to Legal, for resolution.

• Serve as a go-to resource for property and portfolio management matters, answering questions and resolving issues independently as appropriate, and building relationships that advance Carvana's standing and rapport with landlords.

• Support property move-in/move-out processes, critical dates management, and related lease administration functions.

• Absorb tasks and projects as needed to work efficiently, prioritizing according to team and business objectives.

• Work with a third-party utility manager to transfer and set up utility services.

• Accurately track property taxes and work with a third-party tax vendor to ensure timely payment.

• Manage COI (certificate of insurance) collection and distribution and support quarterly reporting requirements.

• Review tenant rent and common area maintenance (CAM) charges to ensure accuracy.

• Support recurring rent payment, tax payment, insurance requirements, contractual obligations, and routine "run the business" property management responsibilities.

• Prepare and deliver timely, accurate operational and financial reports to stakeholders.

• Draft, review, and obtain approval for standard legal notices, landlord-tenant communications, and ancillary documents, under the supervision of the Senior Manager, Portfolio Management.

• Support lease administration workflow, including estoppels, SNDAs, access requests, and other routine commercial lease matters.

• Support the management and reporting of critical dates, where needed, while coordinating with landlords on matters such as potential buyouts, early lease terminations, and other lease-related negotiations.

• Utilize AI tools to increase speed and accuracy on lease review, document drafting, and reporting tasks.

• Manage lease setup tasks in the project management system.

• Develop and maintain relationships with contractors, landlords, tenants and stakeholders.

• Other duties as assigned.

What you should have/know

• 8+ years of experience in commercial property management or commercial lease administration — gained in an in-house/corporate real estate department or at a commercial property management or brokerage firm..

• A Bachelor's degree from an accredited undergraduate institution is preferred.

• Strong comprehension of commercial lease/purchase agreement language, with the ability to interpret provisions and identify key obligations, rights, and risks.

• Direct experience with commercial lease administration concepts such as CAM reconciliation, estoppels, SNDAs, and certificates of insurance.

• Self-starter; able to make good decisions and work independently with limited direction or supervision.

• Must be able to work in a fast-paced, results-driven, team-oriented environment with multiple deadlines, and adapt quickly to changing priorities.

• Ability to think critically and take the initiative to develop and improve processes for the team.

• Ability to identify opportunities and provide solutions.

• Ability to comprehend Landlord vs Tenant responsibilities under commercial leases and enforce compliance.

• Strong decision-making skills; able to recognize which functions can be handled autonomously versus which require collaboration or escalation, and to calibrate how much context to provide based on the audience and goals.

• Grasp of or proficiency in risk management and issue-spotting, recognizing which matters require input from team leadership or other groups such as Legal, Accounting, or Insurance.

• Strong team mentality; ability to productively work with varying personalities and experience levels to grow and develop the team.

• Proficient with Microsoft Office, G-Suite applications and AI resources, including Claude and Gemini.

• Working knowledge of Property Works software or similar commercial lease management software.

• Familiar and comfortable with financial review and reporting.

• Enthusiasm and energy to contribute to and thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced atmosphere where roles continually adapt as the company evolves.

Don't Meet 100% of the Qualifications?
At Carvana, we value diverse backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't fit every single bullet point. Give it a shot—we'd love to hear from you!

What we’ll offer in return

• Full-Time salary position.

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits.

• 401K with company match.

• A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more.

• A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy both physically and mentally.

• Access to opportunities to expand your skill set and share your knowledge with others across the organization.

• A company culture focused on high performance and bar-raising, with vast opportunity to learn and grow.

Other requirements
To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

• Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal stuff
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer.  All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.  Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

jobs.title: Preschool Substitute
jobs.description:
Looking for a flexible role working with children in a meaningful, supportive environment?

Join our on-call Substitute Teacher team at Guidepost Montessori!

We’re always excited to welcome a warm, dependable substitute teacher to support our mixed-age Montessori classrooms when our full-time teachers are out. No formal Montessori training is required; we’ll provide training as part of your orientation and onboarding.

About the Role

This is an on-call, as-needed position, ideal for individuals seeking flexible hours while making a positive impact on young children.

As a Substitute Teacher, you’ll support multiple classrooms serving children ages 0–6, helping maintain a calm, engaging, and nurturing learning environment.

Many of our substitute teachers go on to become full-time Assistant Teachers, making this a great opportunity to get your foot in the door at Guidepost Montessori.

What You’ll Do

• Step into classrooms as needed to support children and maintain consistency

• Assist with daily routines and classroom activities across mixed-age groups

• Help create a warm, safe, and engaging environment for children

• Collaborate with school staff to ensure smooth transitions and continuity of care

• Model patience, professionalism, and kindness in every interaction

Schedule & Flexibility

• Hours and days vary based on school needs

• Perfect for those seeking part-time, flexible, or supplemental work

Minimum Qualifications

• Negative TB test within the last 12 months

• Valid state background check

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills

• Warm, friendly, and dependable demeanor

• Passion for working with young children

Preferred (but not required):

• Early Childhood Education (ECE) units

• Recent experience working with children ages 0–6

Why Guidepost Montessori?

Guidepost Montessori is a global community of educators dedicated to transforming education through independence, curiosity, and respect for each child.

We are committed to expanding high-quality, authentic Montessori programs across the U.S. and around the world, creating environments where children and educators alike can thrive.

If you love children, value flexibility, and are looking for a meaningful way to grow in early childhood education, we’d love to meet you.

Apply today and become part of our school community!

Guidepost Global Education and Guidepost Montessori are committed to a policy of Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO). We will not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, color, creed, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, alienage or citizenship, disability, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under applicable federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. jobs.title: Payroll Administrator
jobs.description:
Come join our team! At Unlimited Technology, we are committed to our company's core values of Passion, Collaboration, Innovation and Adaptability. With offices throughout the United States, we are a premier cyber and physical security specialty contractor, and we are growing at a rapid pace. We have a wide range of talented and experienced individuals that deliver cutting edge technology solutions to meet our customers’ ever-changing needs. We secure the facilities and networks of the world’s leading brands and critical infrastructure and are recognized leaders in the physical and IT security, cyber, and managed services industries. UT offers a rewarding career, great benefits, and the chance to learn and work with ground-breaking technology and premier clients.

Are you passionate about payroll? We are looking for a dynamic Payroll Administrator to join our growing team.
The Payroll and People Operations Administrator is a critical support role that combines core HR administration with end-to-end payroll and timekeeping. Success in this role means payroll runs on time and without errors, employee records are complete and audit-ready, and departmental processes and workflows are executed flawlessly.

Responsibilities
Payroll & Timekeeping
This role assists with the following duties:
•    Verify hours worked and pay adjustments each pay period, and post approved information to payroll records.
•    Enter payroll data into the payroll system, and process and issue employee pay and earnings statements.
•    Review timesheets, wage computations, and related records to detect and resolve payroll discrepancies before payroll is finalized.
•    Process certified payroll for covered employees, and ensure compliance with federal contractor payroll requirements, including the Davis-Bacon and Related Acts, McNamara O’Hara Service Contract Act, and Prevailing Wages.
•    Partner with People Operations on matters affecting employee pay, such as compensation changes, leaves of absence, and earnings and deductions changes.
•    Assist employees and managers on the company’s timekeeping system and procedures as needed.
•    Stay current on final pay and changes in tax and deduction laws that affect payroll processing per state.

HR Administration & Employee Lifecycle
This role supports the People Operations team with the following duties:
•    Perform new hire onboarding tasks as the need arises.
•    Conduct reference or background checks on existing employees as directed by customer requirements.
•    Facilitate the employee separation process, including the coordination of final pay, equipment collection, and access shut off.
•    Partner with the company’s employment verification provider to facilitate requests, completing those that fall outside of the provider’s scope.
•    Review and process employee changes in the HRIS, including demographic changes, benefit elections, and process workflows.

Education & Experience Requirements
Required
•    Two (2) or more years of combined experience in payroll processing and HR administration, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
•    Experience processing multi-step payroll, including wage and deduction calculations, timekeeping review, and pay adjustments.
•    Experience processing certified payroll and working with federal contractor requirements, including but not limited to: Davis-Bacon and Related Acts, McNamara-O’Hara Service Contract Act, and Prevailing Wages.
•    Working knowledge of payroll tax and deduction rules and core employment laws (such as FLSA, EEO, and ADA), with the ability to apply them to day-to-day situations.
•    Experience using an HRIS, payroll, or timekeeping platform (for example Paylocity, ADP, Workday, UKG/Kronos, or similar) and Microsoft Excel for reconciliation and reporting.
•    Strong accuracy and attention to detail, including the ability to spot and resolve numerical discrepancies.
•    Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain pay and policy information to people at all levels.
•    Able to handle confidential employee and pay information with discretion and in accordance with company data-protection practices.

Preferred
•    Associate’s or bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, accounting, or a related field. Equivalent experience is fully considered.
•    Professional certification such as Fundamental Payroll Certification (FPC), Certified Payroll Professional (CPP), aPHR, PHR, or SHRM-CP.
•    Experience supporting a multi-state workforce or a federal government contractor environment.

Physical Requirements
The physical demands below represent those needed to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
•    Remaining in a stationary position, typically seated, for extended periods while working at a computer.
•    Operating a computer and other standard office equipment, including frequent keyboard and data-entry work.
•    Reviewing detailed information on screens and in documents for accuracy.
•    Communicating with employees, managers, and external parties daily by phone, email, video conference, and in person.
•    A standard 40-hour work week, with occasional periods of heightened workload around payroll deadlines and period-end close.

Pay Range

$50,000—$60,000 USD

Benefits

• Health, dental, and vision coverage

• Life insurance

• 401 (k) w/company match 100% up to 3% and an additional 50% match of 2%

• Paid time off

• 11 Paid Holidays

• Company Equity after 1 year

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, sex, age, national origin, disability, Veteran status, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Clinical Staff Manager - Dallas, TX
jobs.description:
ABOUT VEG

In 2014, VEG was born with a mission to help people and their pets when they need it most. This meant challenging the status quo and fixing everything that was wrong with the ER experience. Since then, we’ve expanded rapidly, with hospitals nationwide open 24/7, 365 days a year, and created a better emergency experience—not only for people and their pets, but also for everyone who works here—our VEGgies!

At VEG we find a way to say yes to the career you want in veterinary emergency medicine. This means transforming how ER works, from our open-concept hospitals, where you can handle emergency cases of every kind (even exotics!) to our immersive, customer-focused experience, which helps us give people and their pets the care they deserve.

This also means saying yes to creating the greatest experience possible for our VEGgies. Yes to working in an environment where you can find your place and feel valued for the amazing work you do. Yes to having unparalleled opportunities for learning and mentorship so you can grow where you want to go in your career. And yes to making an impact here in ways you never thought possible.

VEG is a 2025 and 2026 certified Great Place to Work®.

THE JOB

The mission of a Clinical Staff Manager (CSM) is to ensure their VEG hospital has an effective support staff team who provide excellent patient care and embody the VEG way. CSMs  provide their VEGgies with equitable support, tools, resources, and autonomy necessary to create an environment of high medical quality and care so that VEG is the best hospital for emergency professionals who will brag about their jobs and make their friends jealous. CSMs collaborate with their local and regional leadership teams to build relationships between all departments and work together to implement VEG wide initiatives and achieve the hospitals’ goals.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

People Empowerment and Development:

Recruitment

• Directly responsible for interviewing, hiring and training a diverse group of new VEG Credentialed Veterinary Technicians and Veterinary Assistants in partnership with the other leadership team members, particularly the Medical Director and Regional Support Staff Director

• Leads onboarding experience for new support staff team members in partnership with Onboarding and Hospital Manager

Leadership and Development

• Directly oversee support staff team and engage as an active and present leader across the hospital with all teams and all shifts

• Foster a learning culture to support learners at every level

• Responsible for educating the veterinary support staff team through formal education track and informal coaching by utilizing Technician Trainers and other training tools

• Serve as the initial point of contact for support staff concerns and seeks assistance from the hospital leadership as needed

• Address interpersonal conflicts in the moment that arise on shift, ensuring that interpersonal conflicts are not affecting workflow or patient care

• Liaise with the leadership to bridge gaps and unify team members

• Incorporates feedback from doctors in guiding the growth and development of support staff team members

• Lead the team of Shift Leads to identify areas for process improvements and present solutions in coordination with the Medical Director and Technician Trainer

• Participate in all group and leadership meetings to promote practice alignment

• Promote a culture of inclusivity and equitable treatment ensuring an environment free of discrimination and harassment for all VEGgies and customers. Promote awareness and proactively managing unconscious bias.

Maintain hospital people processes

• Recruiting (interview cadence, candidate feedback) - in coordination with Talent Partner

• Onboarding activities, including maintaining contact with VEGgies pre-hire and creating a great first day/week/month experience (templated timelines, content and schedules) - in coordination with People Coordinator

• Training and Development (customized plans, documentation, resources)- all credentialed veterinary technician growth plans and development meetings in coordination with Medical Director and Technician Trainer

• HR Operations (complete bi-weekly payroll, complete I9s within 3 days, benefit enrollments, responsibly navigate leave programs and accommodations) - in coordination with Hospital Manager and People Partner

• Performance Management (meeting cadence, documentation, succession planning, accountability) in coordination with Hospital Manager and People Partner

• May be involved in ending employment of a support staff team member, but works with hospital leadership at every step

Product:

Customer Experience

• Partner with hospital leadership on workflow, the Spikes, the VEG Triage and the three dimensions of customer experience

• Assist with immediate customer concerns professionally and to the customers satisfaction and follow up with leadership for long term solution

• May assist with customer concerns related as requested by Hospital Manager

jobs.title: DMG Analyst (Multiple Levels)
jobs.description:
Machinify is a leading healthcare intelligence company with expertise across the payment continuum, delivering unmatched value, transparency, and efficiency to health plan clients across the country. Deployed by over 85 health plans, including many of the top 20, and representing more than 270 million lives, Machinify brings together a fully configurable and content-rich, AI-powered platform along with best-in-class expertise. We’re constantly reimagining what’s possible in our industry, creating disruptively simple, powerfully clear ways to maximize financial outcomes and drive down healthcare costs.

About the Opportunity

Every year, billions in medical and pharmacy claims flow through Machinify. Buried in that data are overpayments, billing errors, and patterns nobody has spotted yet, and the Data Mining Group (DMG) is the team that finds them. Every insight we surface helps health plans recover real dollars and brings down the cost of care for millions of members.

We’re looking for a SQL Server expert who gets a thrill out of making slow things fast. You’ll take queries that grind for hours across billions of rows and make them finish in minutes by reading execution plans, designing smart indexing and partitioning strategies, and tuning the database underneath it all. You’ll own the performance and health of the data platform DMG runs on, and you’ll turn that speed into new data mining capabilities that weren’t possible before. If you’ve spent years as a DBA or database engineer and want your work to have a direct, measurable impact on healthcare costs, we’d love to talk.

We are looking for someone who doesn’t settle for the quick fix. When something looks off, you’ll dig until you find the underlying cause, and you’ll fix it for good. At our scale, that habit pays off in a big way: every root cause eliminated means faster mining cycles, fewer missed overpayments, less rework, and more dollars recovered for our clients. Those gains compound month after month and flow straight to the bottom line.

What you’ll do

• Make big data fast. Tune complex T-SQL against multi-terabyte claims datasets using execution plans, Query Store, wait statistics, DMVs, and Extended Events, and measure the before and after.

• Engineer for performance. Design and maintain indexing (clustered, nonclustered, filtered, columnstore), partitioning, and statistics strategies that cut runtimes and resource usage at scale.

• Keep the platform healthy. Monitor database performance, resolve blocking and deadlocks, tune tempdb and memory, and partner with infrastructure on capacity planning, backups, and high availability.

• Build the foundation. Develop the stored procedures, views, and data structures that power our data mining work, making thoughtful normalization and denormalization choices.

• Find the money. Write, run, and monitor SQL that examines, interprets, and visualizes trends in medical and pharmacy claims, uncovering overpayments and new recovery opportunities.

• Chase the root cause. Investigate every slowdown, data anomaly, and dip in findings until you know exactly why it happened, then fix it for good. Continual root-cause analysis prevents repeat issues, protects recovery dollars, and turns one-time fixes into lasting savings for Machinify and our clients.

• Automate and innovate. Continuously improve our data mining and enrichment processes, building tools and automation that make the whole team faster.

• Lead and level up the team. Own small projects end to end, review SQL and coach analysts on writing efficient queries, and work closely with other departments to align data insights with business goals.

What you bring

• 5+ years of hands-on experience as a SQL Server DBA, database engineer, or performance-focused database developer.

• Expert-level T-SQL and a proven track record of query optimization: you can read an execution plan, pinpoint the bottleneck, and fix it (and you have a story about the time you did).

• Deep knowledge of SQL Server internals, including indexing, statistics, partitioning, Query Store, DMVs, wait stats, and Extended Events.

• A root-cause mindset: you don’t settle for workarounds, and you can show how getting to the bottom of a problem saved time, money, or both.

• Experience working with large-scale data: multi-terabyte databases, billion-row tables, or enterprise data warehouses.

• Solid grounding in database administration fundamentals such as backup and recovery, high availability (Always On Availability Groups), security, and monitoring.

• A proactive problem-solver who can juggle multiple priorities and explain technical tradeoffs to non-technical partners.

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Bonus points

• Experience with medical and pharmacy claims or healthcare payment integrity.

• Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, or cloud database migrations.

• Automation with PowerShell or Python.

• Data warehouse design and columnstore indexing.

What We Offer

• Work from anywhere in the US! Machinify is digital-first.

• Top Medical/Dental/Vision offerings

• FSA/HSA

• Tuition reimbursement

• Competitive salary, 401(k) with company match

• Additional health and wellness benefits and perks

• Flexible and trusting environment where you’ll feel empowered to do your best work

Pay range: $9,000 - $185,000

The salary for this position is based on an array of factors unique to each candidate: Such as years and depth of experience, set skills, certifications, etc.  We are hiring for different levels, and our Recruiting team will let you know if you qualify for a different role/range.

Equal Employment Opportunity at Machinify

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

• Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

• What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

• It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS*

• Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

• Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

YOUR MISSION

True Anomaly is seeking an experienced Insider Threat Director to lead the development, implementation, and management of a comprehensive insider threat program. This critical leadership role will establish and oversee policies, procedures, and technologies to detect, prevent, and respond to insider threats that could compromise our national security missions, sensitive technologies, and classified information.

The Insider Threat Director will work closely with Security, Legal, Human Resources, IT, and operational leadership to create a culture of security awareness while respecting employee privacy and civil liberties. This position reports to the Chief Security Officer and serves as a key member of the security leadership team. This position requires an active security clearance.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Program Development & Leadership

• Design, implement, and manage a mature insider threat program compliant with NISPOM, DCSA guidelines, ICD 503, Executive Order 13587, and other relevant federal requirements

• Develop and maintain insider threat policies, procedures, and standard operating procedures (SOPs)

• Lead and mentor a team of insider threat analysts and investigators

• Serve as the primary liaison with government oversight agencies, including DCSA, on insider threat matters

Threat Detection & Analysis

• Develop behavioral indicators and technical signatures to identify potential insider threats

• Implement continuous evaluation and monitoring programs in accordance with federal requirements

• Coordinate threat hunting activities and proactive risk assessments

• Ensure timely reporting and escalation of insider threat incidents to appropriate stakeholders

Collaboration & Integration

• Work with Physical Security to integrate badge access, visitor logs, and surveillance data

• Collaborate with HR on personnel screening, behavioral concerns, and employee assistance programs

• Coordinate with Legal to ensure compliance with privacy laws, labor regulations, and civil liberties protections

• Engage with Counterintelligence and law enforcement agencies as appropriate

Training & Awareness

• Develop and deliver insider threat awareness training for all employees, contractors, and leadership

• Create specialized training for system administrators, security personnel, and managers

• Foster a security-conscious culture that encourages reporting of concerning behaviors

• Conduct regular tabletop exercises and simulations to test program effectiveness

Technology & Tools

• Evaluate, implement, and manage insider threat detection technologies and platforms

• Leverage advanced analytics, machine learning, and automation to enhance detection capabilities

• Ensure proper configuration, tuning, and maintenance of insider threat tools QUALIFICATIONS

Security Clearance: Active TS/SCI clearance or ability to obtain and maintain

Education: Bachelor's degree in Cybersecurity, Criminal Justice, Intelligence Studies, Information Security, or related field

Experience: Minimum 8 years of experience in insider threat, counterintelligence, cybersecurity, or security investigations, with at least 3 years in a leadership role

Program Knowledge: Demonstrated experience developing and managing insider threat programs in cleared defense or aerospace environments

Regulatory Expertise: Deep understanding of NISPOM, ICD 503, EO 13587, DCSA requirements, and insider threat program standards

Technical Acumen: Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, network security, endpoint detection, and data analytics

Analytical Skills: Proven ability to analyze complex data sets, identify patterns, and assess risk

Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills with ability to brief senior executives and government officials

Judgment: Strong ethical foundation with demonstrated ability to balance security requirements with employee privacy and civil liberties

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

An ideal candidate will also have:

• Active TS/SCI

• Professional certifications such as CIPP (Certified Insider Threat Professional), CISSP, CFE, CDFE, or equivalent

• Experience in the intelligence community, DoD, or law enforcement

• Background in counterintelligence or counterespionage operations

• Experience with space industry or critical infrastructure protection

• Knowledge of behavioral psychology and threat assessment methodologies

• Familiarity with advanced analytics platforms, SIEM tools, and machine learning applications for security

• Experience with incident response and forensic investigations

• Previous work with DCSA, FBI, or other federal oversight and investigative agencies

WHAT WE OFFER

• Opportunity to build and lead a critical security program from the ground up

• Work on cutting-edge space security technologies with national security impact

• Collaborative, mission-focused culture with talented colleagues

• Competitive compensation package including base salary, equity, and performance bonuses

• Comprehensive benefits including health, dental, vision, 401(k) with match

• Professional development and training opportunities

COMPENSATION

• Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave

jobs.title: Industrial and Personnel Security Manager
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

Industrial and Personnel Security Manager | Varda Space Industries

About the Role

Varda is manufacturing medicines in orbit and flying government missions that bring hardware back through hypersonic reentry. It’s some of the most ambitious work happening anywhere, and it only happens if the people, facilities, information, and hardware behind it are protected. That’s the job. You would be the one who makes Varda’s security program real.

As the Industrial and Personnel Security Manager, you will own the day-to-day execution of our industrial security compliance and personnel security programs. This is a builder’s role, not a maintenance role. You’ll design practical processes, keep the program inspection-ready, and work shoulder to shoulder with HR, IT, Legal, Engineering, Mission Management, and Business Development, from the first customer conversation through launch and recovery.

You’ll report directly to the Director of Security, who is also our Facility Security Officer (FSO), and support industrial and personnel security activities as assigned. With designation and completion of required training, you may serve as Alternate FSO, a real path to expanded responsibility. The Director retains primary FSO authority, program oversight, and required certifications. Special program personnel security and COMSEC duties apply as customer requirements are established.

Physical security operations are outside the scope of this role. We plan to hire a dedicated Physical Security Manager after this position, so you can focus on what you do best.

What You’ll Do

Industrial Security and Compliance

• Run the industrial security program in accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), contract requirements, security classification guides, and applicable DoD and Intelligence Community requirements.

• Own facility clearance records and supporting documentation, and prepare updates and government correspondence for FSO review using NISS or the applicable government system.

• Lead annual self-inspections: plan them, maintain inspection evidence, draft reports for the Director’s review and certification, and track corrective actions through closure.

• Be the face of readiness for DCSA security reviews and customer assessments, coordinating deliverables with the FSO and external security advisory partners.

• Review DD Forms 254 and classification guides, and turn requirements into procedures. Partner with Contracts and Business Development to build security requirements into prime contracts, subcontracts, and proposals, shaping programs before they begin.

• Control classified information and material from marking, receipt, storage, and dissemination through inventory, transfer, approved transmission, and destruction when authorized.

• Build the procedures, training materials, and records people actually use, and bring practical improvements to the Director whenever you spot a compliance gap.

Personnel Security

• Manage clearance processing and records in DISS, NBIS, and applicable customer systems, including investigation requests, upgrades, transfers, reciprocity coordination, and Continuous Vetting actions.

• Coordinate SCI nominations, program access requests, and customer-required polygraph scheduling when applicable, and verify eligibility and need-to-know before access is granted.

• Partner with HR on cleared employee onboarding and offboarding, and maintain clearance rosters, access records, personnel security files, and briefing acknowledgments.

• Brief the team: initial, annual, refresher, foreign travel, and termination briefings, plus program indoctrinations and debriefings with authorized officials.

• Process incoming and outgoing visit authorizations and certifications, and verify visitor clearance and access requirements.

• Spot issues early by tracking foreign travel, foreign contacts, reportable changes, and adverse information. Prepare timely reports and elevate sensitive matters to the FSO in coordination with HR and Legal.

• Plan ahead by forecasting clearance needs with hiring and program teams, and track metrics on processing status, overdue reporting, training completion, and inspection findings.

Program Support and Incident Response

• Support insider threat administration under the Director’s ITPSO oversight, including training, referral documentation, and coordination with authorized stakeholders.

• Document security incidents, support inquiries and required reporting, and track mitigation and corrective actions under FSO direction.

• Step in as alternate COMSEC custodian when designated, trained, and authorized, supporting inventory, accountability, and handling requirements.

• Team up with IT and Information Assurance on CUI protection and classified infrastructure, and support program protection planning without assuming ISSM or ISSO authority.

• Be the go-to advisor who gives employees and leaders clear security guidance, and help shape the tools, resources, and future staffing the program needs as it grows.

What You’ll Bring

Experience and Technical Knowledge

• At least 5 years of relevant industrial security experience in a DoD or Intelligence Community contractor environment, including substantive hands-on personnel security responsibilities.

• A track record of ownership: demonstrated experience administering clearance actions, reporting, training, classified information controls, and inspection preparation, and independently owning recurring security processes.

• Strong working knowledge of 32 CFR Part 117 (NISPOM), DD Form 254 requirements, and security classification guides, with the ability to translate requirements into clear procedures.

• Hands-on proficiency with DISS and NBIS, and the ability to use NISS and customer-specific systems applicable to your responsibilities.

• Working knowledge of relevant ICD 704 personnel security requirements when supporting SCI personnel.

• Strong written communication, organization, discretion, and judgment, with the ability to brief employees, executives, and government representatives and to handle sensitive personnel information.

• The ability to work independently, coordinate across functions, prioritize competing deadlines, and build repeatable processes in a growing company.

Clearance and Conditions of Employment

• U.S. citizenship and an active Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility, plus the ability to maintain it and obtain required customer program access.

• Ability to satisfy additional customer access requirements, including a CI polygraph if required by the assigned program. An existing polygraph is preferred but not universally mandatory.

• Ability to work on-site in El Segundo and support other Varda facilities, with occasional domestic travel and mission-driven schedule requirements as needed.

• Completion and maintenance of required role-specific government and customer training. FSO or COMSEC training is required before performing formally designated duties.

Education

• Bachelor’s degree in security management, criminal justice, business administration, or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience. A degree is not mandatory when your experience demonstrates the required capabilities.

Make Us Say “Wow”

• 7 or more years of relevant experience, including prior FSO, Alternate FSO, CPSO, CSSO, or security program leadership responsibilities.

• Direct experience supporting successful DCSA reviews and personnel or industrial security compliance for SCI or SAP programs.

• COMSEC account experience, insider threat program administration, and experience partnering on CUI or classified information system requirements.

• Relevant CDSE FSO course completion or recognized security certifications such as SPeD or ISP.

• Experience building security processes in aerospace, space, advanced manufacturing, or a startup environment.

Compensation and Perks

• Salary Range: $115,000 - $155,000

• Location: El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary are determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance.

• Eligibility for long-term incentives in the form of stock options or long-term cash awards, so you share in the upside as Varda grows.

• Ability to purchase company stock through the Employee Stock Purchase Plan.

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

E-Verify Statement

Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

jobs.title: Director, Activation
jobs.description:
Kepler executes engineered marketing, where every message and ad delivered helps create a more personalized and productive relationship between brands and their consumers. We do this by acting as clients’ agency of record, as their in-house team, or some hybrid of the two – and by harnessing data and technology across all paid digital media and data-driven CRM channels.

Kepler prides itself on being a great place to work. In fact, we’re proud to share that AdAge recognized Kepler among the Best Place to Work in 2022, validating our investment in our team and our clients.

• We're transparent with our employees. You'll hear updates on company financials, how we're performing against bonus goals, and how we're responding to challenges we face.

• We're growing. For you, that means unparalleled growth opportunities and a role in shaping the direction of the company.

• We're fun. You'll work with and learn from the smartest people in the industry and have a blast doing it.

THE TEAM

Kepler’s Activation team is made up of forward-thinking media experts who bring deep platform expertise, analytical thinking, and a passion for driving performance across digital media channels. Our teams develop, execute, and optimize campaigns across paid search, paid social, programmatic display and video, connected TV, audio, digital out-of-home, and other emerging media channels.

We’re more than a media trading desk. We combine hands-on platform expertise with strategic thinking, data-driven insights, and a strong understanding of the evolving digital landscape to help our clients achieve their business goals. Our teams partner closely with clients, media partners, and internal stakeholders to develop innovative media strategies, identify opportunities for optimization, and build scalable solutions that drive measurable impact.

THE ROLE

The Director, Activation will provide strategic and operational leadership for a team of digital media professionals responsible for developing, executing, and optimizing performance-driven media campaigns across multiple channels. This role combines deep hands-on media expertise with strong client partnership and proven people leadership.

You will lead and develop a multi-level team of Associate Directors, Managers, Senior Analysts, and Analysts, setting strategic direction, building leadership capabilities, and ensuring excellence across campaign strategy and execution. As a senior leader within the Activation organization, you will serve as a trusted advisor to clients and internal stakeholders, drive innovation across media platforms, and identify opportunities to improve performance, strengthen team capabilities, and deliver meaningful business results.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Lead and develop a high-performing team: Provide strategic direction, coaching, and mentorship to a multi-level team of Associate Directors, Managers, Senior Analysts, and Analysts, fostering accountability, collaboration, and continued professional growth.

• Drive media strategy and performance: Oversee the development, execution, and optimization of cross-channel media campaigns across paid search, paid social, programmatic, and other digital channels, ensuring alignment with client objectives and business outcomes.

• Bring deep hands-on media expertise: Maintain strong platform knowledge and serve as a subject matter expert, guiding campaign strategy, troubleshooting performance challenges, and identifying opportunities for optimization and innovation.

• Lead client relationships: Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders and media partners, lead strategic discussions, and translate campaign performance and industry trends into actionable recommendations.

• Drive innovation and operational excellence: Stay ahead of emerging media trends, platform capabilities, and technologies while establishing best practices, improving workflows, and identifying opportunities to scale team capabilities and efficiency.

• Partner across the organization: Collaborate with senior leadership and cross-functional teams to develop integrated media solutions, support broader business initiatives, and continually evolve the Activation organization.

DESIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• 8–10+ years of hands-on digital media experience, with deep expertise in performance marketing across multiple paid media channels, including paid search, paid social, and programmatic.

• Experience leading and developing larger, multi-level teams, including Associate Directors, Managers, and senior individual contributors.

• Proven ability to coach and develop other leaders while building high-performing, collaborative teams.

• Extensive knowledge of major digital media platforms, campaign management tools, and analytics solutions.

• Experience developing cross-channel media strategies, overseeing campaign performance, and translating data into actionable business recommendations.

• Strong client-facing experience, including leading strategic discussions, presentations, and senior-level partnerships.

• Strong analytical, communication, presentation, and problem-solving skills.

• Ability to manage competing priorities, drive innovation, and thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

Transparency is fundamental to Kepler’s culture. Our compensation strategy is designed to attract, reward, and retain the talented employees that drive Kepler’s growth and success. We aim to offer competitive direct compensation and a rich indirect compensation program that demonstrates the value we place on our employees and their wellbeing.

Total Compensation:

• Base Salary: $140,000- $160,000

• Target Annualized Discretionary Bonus: 10% ($14,000 - $16,000)

• Target Total Cash: $154,000- $176,000

Benefits:

• Healthcare/Dental/Vision

• Unlimited PTO

• 401k Contributions

• $75/mo Wellness Stipend

• $100/mo Mobile Phone Stipend

• $50/mo Internet Stipend

• $500/yr Annual Learning Stipend

• $2,000/yr Annual Tuition Stipend

• One-time $200 New Hire Home Office Equipment Stipend

• Parental Leave - 16 week primary caregiver / 6 week secondary caregiver leave

• Annual Work From Anywhere 4 weeks per year

Studies show that imposter syndrome can prevent women and people of color from applying unless they meet every single qualification. jobs.title: Lead Preschool Children's House Teacher
jobs.description:
Inspire curiosity. Build independence. Shape a lifelong love of learning.

At Guidepost Montessori, our Lead Children’s House Guides empower children ages 3–6 to grow into confident, capable learners through thoughtfully prepared environments and respectful, individualized guidance.

If you’re passionate about early childhood education and excited to lead a classroom where independence and joy take center stage, we’d love to meet you.

Your Role

As a Lead Children’s House Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age preschool classroom in a Montessori environment designed to nurture concentration, confidence, and deep learning.

Montessori guides carefully prepare their classrooms to spark curiosity and independence. Through close observation, individualized lessons, and intentional language, you’ll support each child’s academic, social, and emotional development meeting them where they are and helping them grow.

Children in Montessori classrooms have the freedom to choose meaningful work, repeat activities until mastery, and take pride in their accomplishments. Your guidance helps every child develop focus, confidence, and a strong belief in their own abilities.

What You’ll Do

• Observe each child closely to understand and support their physical, intellectual, and emotional development

• Prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly classroom that fosters concentration and independence

• Encourage self-confidence by supporting children as they learn to “do it themselves”

• Provide individualized and small-group lessons in practical life, literacy, math, and beyond

• Build strong, respectful relationships with children and families

• Communicate and collaborate with parents to support each child’s growth

• Lead your classroom with warmth, professionalism, and purpose

The Montessori Prepared Environment

Every Guidepost Children’s House classroom is fully equipped with high-quality Montessori materials and designed around the principles of beauty, order, and accessibility.

A Guidepost Children’s House environment includes:

• Child-sized furniture and ample floor space for independent and small-group work

• Practical life materials for sweeping, food preparation, table setting, and care of the environment

• Curriculum that builds independence in dressing, feeding, and self-care

• Hands-on materials for literacy, math, science, and cultural studies

• Low shelves and child-level artwork for full accessibility

• Cozy reading spaces, real plants, and abundant natural light

• Beautiful, breakable materials made from wood, metal, and glass

What We’re Looking For

• Montessori diploma for ages 3–6, or willingness to obtain certification (fully sponsored)

• Experience working with children ages 3–6 in a group learning environment

• Alignment with child-led philosophies such as Montessori or Reggio Emilia

• Required ECE or Child Development credits

• Bachelor’s degree in (Child related field)

What We Offer

• Sponsored Montessori diploma training through the Prepared Montessorian Institute

• Ongoing professional development and mentorship

• Competitive salary: $40,000 - $50,000 depending on education and experience

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off and paid holidays

• 75% tuition discount for up to two children at any Guidepost school

• A supportive network of passionate educators

• Clear opportunities for career growth and leadership advancement

About Guidepost Montessori

Guidepost Montessori is a growing network of over 100 schools across the U.S. and Asia, serving children ages 3 months to 6 years in our Nido, Toddler, and Children’s House programs.

We believe children are capable. Our mission is to transform education by designing learning environments that cultivate independence, joy, and lifelong curiosity for children, families, and educators alike.

We will not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, color, creed, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, alienage or citizenship, disability, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under applicable federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. Our leadership is dedicated to ensuring the fulfillment of this policy. When requested, we are committed to reasonably accommodate employees and applicants with disabilities or special needs that may require an accommodation.

jobs.title: Seasonal Assistant Teacher
jobs.description:
Seasonal Assistant Teacher (Montessori), Holiday Break Support

Imagine a classroom where a toddler pours her own water for the first time, a four-year-old proudly finishes a puzzle he’s been working on all week, and every child is trusted to show what they can do. That’s a normal day at Guidepost Montessori, and this holiday season, you could be part of it.

We’re looking for warm, dependable Seasonal Assistant Guides to support our classrooms over the holiday breaks. You might be a college student home for winter break, an experienced caregiver looking for flexible work, or someone who has always wondered what teaching in a Montessori classroom is like. If you love young children and want to grow in a supportive, purpose-driven place, we’d love to meet you.

This could be more than a seasonal job. Many of our team members start out as seasonal or part-time staff and find a long-term career with us. Strong seasonal Assistant Guides may be offered a full-time position.

Your Impact

As an Assistant Guide, you’ll support our Infant, Toddler, and Children’s House (ages 3–6) classrooms. You’ll help create a calm, engaging environment where children explore, learn, and grow at their own pace.

In a Montessori classroom, the environment and the guide work together to support each child’s development. You’ll help prepare beautiful, intentional learning spaces and support children in individual and small-group activities, always with respect, patience, and care.

Most importantly, you’ll help children build confidence and discover what they’re capable of.

What You’ll Do

• Help keep classrooms running smoothly and consistently during the busy holiday break season

• Observe children closely to understand and support their individual needs

• Help prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly classroom

• Support individual and small-group learning activities

• Build warm, respectful relationships with children and families
