jobs.title: Grant-Community Partner Manager
jobs.description:
The Community Partnership Manager serves as a primary ambassador for WorkSource Oregon and the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) program throughout Lane County. This position is responsible for developing and maintaining strategic relationships with community organizations, educational institutions, employers, and workforce partners to expand access to workforce services, increase WIOA enrollment, and improve participant employment outcomes.

The Community Partnership Manager leads community outreach, employer engagement, job development, workforce education, and partnership initiatives that connect job seekers with meaningful employment opportunities. This position works collaboratively with Case Managers, program leadership, and workforce partners to identify employment opportunities, secure job postings, facilitate employer referrals, and create pathways to employment through On-the-Job Training (OJT), work-based learning, and direct hiring opportunities.

The position is also responsible for developing and facilitating job readiness workshops within the WorkSource Oregon job center and throughout the community. The Community Partnership Manager will coordinate with industry sector experts, employers, and workforce partners to provide specialized training, career exploration opportunities, and industry roundtable discussions. Workshops will empower participants with the knowledge, skills, and resources necessary to achieve employment, career advancement, financial stability, and digital competency.

The position promotes the full range of WIOA services, including career services, employment support, training opportunities, work-based learning, and supportive services, while ensuring that community and employer partnerships contribute to program enrollment, participant engagement, job placement, and employment retention.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

1. Community Partnership Development and Outreach

• Develop, establish, and maintain strategic partnerships with community-based organizations, educational institutions, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and workforce partners throughout Lane County.
• Serve as a primary point of contact and ambassador for WIOA services within the community.
• Increase awareness of workforce services and expand community referrals into WIOA programs.
• Educate community partners regarding WIOA eligibility requirements, available services, referral procedures, and enrollment processes.
• Develop and implement outreach strategies that increase program visibility, participant enrollment, and access to workforce services.
• Coordinate, facilitate, and participate in community workshops, workforce information sessions, resource fairs, hiring events, and other outreach activities.
• Expand community-based service delivery through partnerships and collaborative initiatives.
• Promote the full range of WIOA services, emphasizing career services, employment support, work-based learning, supportive services, and occupational training rather than tuition assistance alone.
• Maintain regular communication with community partners to identify service gaps, strengthen referral relationships, and improve access to workforce resources.

2. Employer Engagement and Business Services

• Develop and maintain relationships with employers throughout Lane County to identify workforce needs, hiring trends, and employment opportunities for WIOA participants.
• Conduct employer outreach, business visits, and engagement activities to promote LWP services and establish sustainable hiring partnerships.
• Educate employers regarding available workforce services, including OJT, work-based learning, hiring assistance, and other applicable workforce development resources.
• Identify employer workforce needs and collaborate with Case Managers and program leadership to develop customized strategies that connect qualified WIOA participants to employment opportunities.
• Establish employer partnerships that generate:On-the-Job Training (OJT) opportunities.Work-based learning placements.Direct hiring opportunities.Employer referrals and job interviews.Industry-specific employment pathways.
• Maintain ongoing communication with employers to support successful placements, address workforce needs, and strengthen long-term partnerships.
• Identify opportunities for employers to participate in hiring events, workforce workshops, career exploration activities, and other participant engagement initiatives.
• Collaborate with employers to identify opportunities for participants to gain occupational skills, relevant work experience, and industry-recognized credentials.
• Engage industry sector experts and employers to participate in job readiness workshops, industry-specific training, career exploration activities, and roundtable discussions.
• Develop and maintain partnerships with industry representatives to ensure workforce education activities reflect current employer expectations, hiring trends, and occupational skill requirements.

3. Job Development, Job Postings, and Employment Referrals

• Actively identify, develop, and secure employment opportunities for WIOA participants through employer engagement and business development activities.
• Obtain current job openings, hiring requirements, and employment opportunities from employers throughout Lane County.
• Develop and maintain a centralized process for communicating employer job postings and hiring opportunities to Case Managers and appropriate program staff.
• Ensure job postings shared with Case Managers include relevant information such as employer name, job title, location, wages, qualifications, required skills, application instructions, and hiring timelines.
• Collaborate with Case Managers to identify participants whose skills, qualifications, career goals, and employment readiness align with available job opportunities.
• Facilitate direct referrals of qualified WIOA participants to employers for interviews, hiring events, and employment opportunities.
• Coordinate employer introductions, interview opportunities, and recruitment activities to support participant employment outcomes.
• Follow up with employers and Case Managers regarding referrals, interviews, hiring decisions, and employment placements.
• Identify and address barriers that may prevent participants from accessing employment opportunities, coordinating with Case Managers to connect participants to appropriate workforce services and supportive resources.
• Maintain an active pipeline of employer relationships, job postings, referrals, interviews, and placements.
• Monitor the effectiveness of employer referrals and job development activities to identify opportunities to improve placement outcomes.
• Support employment retention by maintaining employer relationships and collaborating with Case Managers regarding participant employment challenges and follow-up services.

4. Workforce Readiness Workshops and Career Education

• Develop, coordinate, and facilitate job readiness workshops within the WorkSource Oregon job center and throughout the community to increase participant employability, employment readiness, and career success.
• Create and implement a minimum of three new workshops each quarter, ensuring that workshop content reflects participant needs, workforce trends, employer expectations, and program priorities.
• Develop workshop topics, learning objectives, instructional materials, presentations, and participant activities that support measurable skill development.
• Deliver workshops in accessible and engaging formats, including in-person sessions, community-based presentations, and other approved delivery methods.
• Develop and facilitate workshops addressing topics such as:Job readiness and workplace expectations.Resume development and application completion.Interview preparation and professional communication.Job search strategies and employment resources.Career exploration and occupational pathways.Labor market information and high-demand occupations.Financial literacy and personal financial management.Digital literacy and technology skills for employment.Workplace professionalism, communication, and soft skills.Career advancement and employment retention.
• Empower participants with financial literacy education, including budgeting, understanding wages and benefits, managing personal finances, and accessing appropriate financial education resources.
• Promote digital literacy by providing participants with opportunities to develop skills in computer use, email, online job applications, digital communication, and other technology essential to employment.
• Coordinate with Case Managers to identify participant skill gaps and develop workshops that address employment readiness barriers.
• Evaluate workshop effectiveness through participant feedback, attendance, skill development, and other appropriate measures.
• Maintain accurate documentation of workshop development, delivery, attendance, and outcomes.

5. Industry Sector Engagement and Workforce Education

• Identify and engage industry sector experts, employers, business leaders, and workforce partners to support participant career exploration and workforce readiness.
• Coordinate industry-specific training sessions, employer presentations, career panels, and roundtable discussions within the job center and community.
• Develop opportunities for participants to engage directly with industry professionals and learn about occupational requirements, workplace expectations, career pathways, and advancement opportunities.
• Facilitate industry roundtable discussions that allow employers and workforce partners to share current workforce needs, hiring trends, skill requirements, and employment opportunities.
• Collaborate with employers and industry experts to identify opportunities for participants to gain relevant skills, credentials, and occupational knowledge.
• Coordinate with Case Managers to identify participants who may benefit from industry-specific workshops, training sessions, or employer engagement activities.
• Maintain partnerships with industry representatives to support ongoing workforce education and employment placement opportunities.
• Ensure industry engagement activities are aligned with labor market information, regional workforce priorities, and participant career goals.

6. Workforce Development and Participant Support

• Serve as a workforce development subject matter expert by assisting customers, community partners, and employers with workforce resources and employment strategies.
• Provide workforce information and resources related to:Career exploration and career pathways.Resume development resources.Interview preparation.Career assessments and occupational exploration.Labor market information (LMI).Job search strategies and employment resources.Community resources and supportive services.Workforce training and work-based learning opportunities.
• Conduct community workshops and workforce information sessions to increase participant knowledge of employment opportunities and available workforce services.
• Collaborate with Case Managers to support participants enrolled in WIOA, special grants, and co-enrolled partner programs.
• Support participant engagement and employment readiness through employer connections, career exploration activities, and job development initiatives.
• Coordinate with program staff to identify employment opportunities aligned with participants' career plans, training objectives, and employment goals.
• Assist in connecting participants to appropriate community resources and workforce services when barriers to employment are identified.

7. WIOA Program Coordination and Performance

• Collaborate with WIOA program leadership, Case Managers, and workforce partners to support program enrollment, service delivery, and employment outcomes.
• Support WIOA performance goals through community outreach, employer engagement, job development, workshop delivery, and employment placement activities.
• Maintain an active pipeline of community referrals, employer partnerships, job postings, and participant employment opportunities.
• Monitor employer engagement and job development activities to identify trends, opportunities, and areas requiring improvement.
• Participate in program meetings, performance reviews, and strategic planning activities as assigned.
• Provide updates to program leadership regarding employer engagement, job development activities, community partnerships, workshops, and employment placement outcomes.
• Collaborate with Case Managers to identify opportunities for improving participant access to employment, training, and work-based learning services.
• Support continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen workforce partnerships and increase employment outcomes.

8. Documentation, Data Integrity, and Reporting

• Ensure all direct services, employer engagement activities, referrals, workshops, and other required program activities are accurately documented in applicable systems.
• Ensure service documentation entered into I-Trac accurately matches supporting documentation uploaded to EBridge for OJT activities and any direct WIOA services delivered by the Community Partnership Manager.
• Maintain accurate and timely documentation of employer contacts, community partnerships, job postings, referrals, hiring events, workshop development, workshop attendance, and employment placement activities.
• Ensure documentation is complete, accurate, and compliant with LWP policies, WIOA requirements, and applicable funding guidelines.
• Maintain appropriate records of employer referrals, participant employment connections, and follow-up activities.
• Support program reporting and data integrity requirements by ensuring activities are documented timely and accurately.
• Identify and communicate data discrepancies or documentation concerns to program leadership for resolution.

9. Rapid Response and Workforce Transition Services

• Coordinate, facilitate, and participate in Rapid Response activities in accordance with Lane Workforce Partnership policies and procedures.
• Establish relationships with employers experiencing layoffs, business closures, or workforce transitions to provide information regarding available workforce services.
• Collaborate with employers, workforce partners, and program staff to coordinate Rapid Response services for affected workers.
• Promote available unemployment assistance, reemployment services, career services, training opportunities, and supportive resources.
• Assist in coordinating workforce information sessions, job fairs, and employment transition activities for impacted workers.
• Maintain required documentation of Rapid Response activities and employer engagement.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in business administration, workforce development, human services, education, communications, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Minimum of three years of experience in workforce development, community engagement, employer relations, business services, career services, training, or a related field.
• Demonstrated experience developing and maintaining professional partnerships with community organizations, employers, or workforce stakeholders.
• Experience conducting employer outreach, job development, recruitment, employment referrals, workforce placement activities, or workshop facilitation.
• Knowledge of workforce development programs, employment services, and community resources.
• Strong communication, presentation, relationship-building, and organizational skills.
• Ability to independently develop and facilitate workshops, coordinate industry engagement, and manage multiple priorities.
• Ability to work independently and meet program performance expectations.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to maintain accurate electronic records and reports.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience working with WIOA-funded programs or other federally or state-funded workforce development initiatives.
• Knowledge of WIOA eligibility requirements, performance measures, OJT, work-based learning, and supportive services.
• Experience developing and delivering job readiness, financial literacy, or digital literacy workshops.
• Experience working with individuals facing barriers to employment.
• Knowledge of Lane County employers, labor market trends, and community resources.
• Experience using workforce case management systems, customer relationship management systems, or employer engagement databases.
• Experience facilitating industry roundtables, employer presentations, or career exploration events.

Core Competencies

• Community partnership development.
• Employer engagement and business development.
• Job development and employment placement.
• Workshop development and facilitation.
• Industry sector engagement.
• Financial and digital literacy education.
• Workforce program knowledge.
• Communication and relationship management.
• Data integrity and documentation.
• Strategic outreach and problem-solving.
• Performance accountability.
• Collaboration and customer service.

Performance Expectations

The Community Partnership Manager is expected to contribute to measurable program outcomes through:

• Increased community referrals and WIOA enrollment opportunities.
• Increased employer engagement and active employer partnerships.
• Increased number of current job postings secured and shared with Case Managers.
• Increased participant referrals to employment opportunities.
• Increased job interviews and employment placements for WIOA participants.
• Increased OJT and work-based learning opportunities.
• Development and delivery of a minimum of three new workshops each quarter.
• Delivery of job readiness workshops within the WorkSource Oregon job center and throughout the community.
• Engagement of industry sector experts, employers, and workforce partners to provide training and roundtable discussions.
• Increased participant access to financial literacy and digital literacy education.
• Timely and accurate documentation of employer, participant, and workshop activities.
• Effective coordination with Case Managers and program leadership to improve employment outcomes.

Performance expectations and individual goals will be established in alignment with program objectives, funding requirements, and organizational performance measures.

Other Duties as Assigned

• Perform other related duties and responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor or management to support program operations, contract requirements, organizational priorities, and workforce service delivery.

Travel Requirements

Local travel throughout Lane County is required to conduct employer engagement, community outreach, partnership meetings, workforce events, workshops, and other program activities. Occasional travel outside Lane County may be required for training, meetings, or organizational initiatives.

• Summer Fridays
• Weekly Wellness Sessions

• Employer 401k Contributions

• Company Picnics Volunteer Experiences

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Kastle is building the AI employee for financial services. We work with some of America's largest banks, helping them scale their operations using autonomous AI Agents that process payments, originate loans, and help customers get a world class experience during some of the biggest financial decisions of their lives.

We've processed over $2 billion in transactions and are backed by Insight Partners and Y Combinator. If you are interested in building AI that is applied in the real world where precision, reliability, and performance matter and redefine access to credit across the world, apply below.

We just raised a $24M Series A and are growing fast!




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:



At Kastle our Infrastructure team is responsible for building the underlying systems that help thousands of people daily, make their largest and most important financial transactions.

We're looking for a Senior Infrastructure Engineer with deep distributed systems expertise to design, build, and operate the infrastructure that powers Kastle's AI agents in production at banks, lender and other financial institutions. You'll work on the hard problems of distributed systems — consistency, fault tolerance, horizontal scalability, and low-latency coordination — across AWS/GCP/Azure, Kubernetes, and Terraform, keeping compliance-critical systems reliable as we grow. This is an onsite role working closely with platform, ML, and security engineering.




WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Design and operate distributed systems that power AI agents in production, with an emphasis on consistency, fault tolerance, and horizontal scalability

 - Architect service-to-service communication, coordination, and state management for systems spanning multiple regions and availability zones

 - Own Kubernetes cluster architecture, scaling, and security hardening across environments

 - Build and maintain Terraform modules and GitOps pipelines so infrastructure changes are reviewed, versioned, and repeatable

 - Design for the reliability and auditability bar that regulated financial institutions require: replication, failover, backups, disaster recovery, and change logs

 - Diagnose and resolve distributed-systems failure modes — network partitions, cascading failures, split-brain scenarios, race conditions — under production pressure

 - Build observability (metrics, distributed tracing, logging, alerting) so the team can see problems before customers do

 - Partner with ML, platform, and security engineering on capacity planning, data consistency guarantees, and architecture reviews

 - Participate in an on-call rotation for production infrastructure

 - Mentor other engineers on distributed systems design and review their architecture and IaC changes


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

 - 5+ years in infrastructure, platform, or backend engineering roles, with substantial hands-on distributed systems experience

 - Strong understanding of distributed systems fundamentals: consensus, replication, partitioning, consistency models (CAP/PACELC), and failure modes

 - Production experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure) at scale

 - Hands-on experience running Kubernetes in production, including cluster upgrades, networking, and security policy

 - Experience designing or operating distributed data stores, message queues, or event streaming systems (e.g. Kafka, etcd, Cassandra, CockroachDB)

 - Strong background in infrastructure-as-code (Terraform preferred) and CI/CD pipelines

 - Proficiency scripting/programming in at least one language (Go, Python, or Rust) for building distributed tooling

 - Experience owning production reliability: on-call, incident response, postmortems

 - Comfortable working onsite and collaborating closely with product, ML, and security teams

Your Day to Day*

Sales and profit

The role will execute floor moves based on those joint discussions.

Fashion Knowledge

jobs.title: eLearning Developer, Articulate Rise Contractror
jobs.description:
Contract eLearning Developer, Articulate Rise
 
CrossFit is looking to contract an eLearning Developer to audit, improve, and rebuild our library of existing online courses. You will evaluate 13 courses, ranging from two to eight credits, and make them more engaging, effective, and current for coaches around the world.
For this project, you will diagnose what works and what doesn’t, design the solution, and build it in Articulate Rise 360. You will also serve as a delivery adviser for new courses, reviewing full content packages and recommending the best way to bring them to life online. You will work closely with the EDU Content team and report to the head of EDU Content.
Key Responsibilities:
Course Audits:Take each course from the learner’s perspective and evaluate structure, pacing, engagement, assessment, accessibility, and overall learner experienceDeliver findings and recommendations document for each course using the provided template, with prioritized, practical recommendations a non-designer can act onFlag outdated content, inconsistencies, and gaps against current CrossFit methodology and brand standards for subject-matter reviewRecommend whether each course needs targeted updates or a full rebuild, with an estimate of effort
Course Updates and Rebuilds:
Update existing Rise 360 builds or rebuild courses from scratch based on approved recommendations
Design interactions, knowledge checks, scenarios, and assessments that reinforce learning and connect directly to real coaching practice
Integrate video, graphics, and other media effectively, and identify new asset needs for the team
Build courses that meet accessibility standards and perform well on desktop and mobile
Test published courses in the learning management system to confirm tracking, completion, and credit reporting work as intended
New Course Design:
Review full content packages for new courses and recommend the best delivery approach, including structure, sequencing, interactivity, media, and assessment strategy
Turn subject-matter expert content into clear, engaging online learning, and identify where content needs to be added, cut, or reworked
Build new courses in Rise 360 as the catalog grows
Localization Readiness:
Build courses with translation in mind, keeping text, media, and interactions easy to localize
Prepare courses for the localization workflow and support the team as translated versions are implemented and reviewed
Standards and Collaboration:
Collaborate with the EDU Content team to keep courses aligned with CrossFit methodology, voice, and brand standards
Create or refine reusable templates, build standards, and style guidelines so the course library delivers a consistent look and learner experience
Incorporate feedback from reviewers and stakeholders through iterative review cycles
Manage your own timeline across multiple courses, report progress regularly, and flag risks early
Knowledge and Skills
Deep grounding in adult learning principles and instructional design models (e.g., ADDIE, SAM, Merrill’s Principles of Instruction, Bloom’s taxonomy)
Advanced and current, hands-on Articulate Rise 360 skills, including blocks, interactions, quizzes, Storyline blocks, and creative design within Rise’s constraints
Experience auditing and redesigning existing courses, not only building new ones
Strong assessment design skills, including scenario-based questions and knowledge checks that measure application, not recall
Clear, practical written recommendations a non-designer can act on
Working knowledge of accessibility standards and SCORM publishing to a learning management system
Self-directed and organized, with a reliable record of meeting deadlines in a remote, part-time contract setting
Familiarity with fitness, coaching, or certification-based education is a plus; CrossFit Level 1 Certificate a plus
Experience with Articulate Storyline 360, video editing, or localization workflows is a plus
Education/Experience
Five or more years of instructional design experience

jobs.description:
Deep Sky est à l'avant-garde de l'un des plus grands défis de notre époque : les changements climatiques. Nous développons et opérons des infrastructures de captage de carbone, allant du captage direct dans l'air (DAC) à la minéralisation permanente du carbone et au stockage géologique. Notre site de Black Lake à Thetford Mines, au Québec, est un élément clé de notre expansion dans les opérations de surface et d'injection de CO₂ pour le stockage souterrain permanent, en tirant parti de la géologie unique de la région et de sa main-d'œuvre qualifiée.

Nous recherchons un Opérateur électromécanicien polyvalent pour se joindre à notre équipe au site de Black Lake. Relevant du chef des opérations, ce rôle combine une expertise électrique et mécanique dans un seul poste d'opérateur responsable de l'opération sécuritaire, de la surveillance, de l'entretien et du dépannage des équipements de surface et des systèmes d'injection. Vous serez le pilier technique du site — entretenant les systèmes mécaniques, diagnostiquant les problèmes électriques, opérant les interfaces opérateur (HMI) et assurant la stabilité des procédés sur l'ensemble des équipements. Il s'agit d'un poste permanent à temps plein, avec des quarts rotatifs de jour et de nuit (7 jours de travail / 7 jours de congé) dans un environnement industriel nécessitant le port d'ÉPI.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product Security
jobs.description:
1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.



About 1Password

At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.



If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.



We’re looking for an experienced security leader to lead and mature the Product Security function here at 1Password. You will be responsible for:

 - Application Security, overseeing our SDLC program.

 - Data and Device Security, ensuring that 1Password continues to deliver secure solutions that meet our customers needs.

 - Privacy Engineering, building systems and controls to ensure that our data management practices meet the highest privacy standards.

 - Security Research, enriching conversations in the security industry with credible and novel research and publications.



As the Sr. Director of Product Security, you will set the strategy, build and scale programs, and partner with engineering, product, and security leadership to reduce risk while enabling innovation. You’ll manage a team of highly skilled security professionals, serve as a trusted advisor to the CISO, and act as a thought leader both inside and outside the organization. As a member of the security leadership team, you will also partner with other leaders across security and the company to drive great security outcomes for our customers



You will report directly to the CISO.



How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.



This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.



What we're looking for:

 - 9+ years of progressive experience in security, with at least 5+ years leading security teams/programs at scale.

 - Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Computer Engineering, or related fields; or equivalent work experience

 - Deep expertise in Application Security, Privacy, and Secure SDLC programs.

 - Experience overseeing Security Research activities and engaging the security research community.

 - Strong track record of embedding security and privacy into engineering processes and influencing product development.

 - Proven experience leading security teams in high-growth technology or security-focused companies.

 - Passion for fostering psychological safety and stability in high stress environments.

 - Excellent communication skills with ability to convey complex security issues to technical and non-technical stakeholders, including executives and boards.

 - Thought leader with visibility in the security community (public speaking, open-source contributions, bug bounty engagement, etc.) a strong plus.

 - Experience leading security initiatives that support and/or incorporate AI capabilities.

 - Demonstrated software development experience with Go, Ruby on Rails, shell scripting, python, or other languages.

 - Experience collaborating across departments such as with internal business or engineering units, external incident response teams, and research teams. 
   





What you can expect:

 - People Leadership: Serve as a great people leader, managing managers, providing regular 1-1s, performance feedback, and career development. Hire security engineers and analysts who complement the team and bring new perspectives.

 - Program Leadership & Partnerships: Define and drive the company-wide Product Security strategy, with a focus on proactive risk reduction and enabling secure AI innovation. Build and scale world-class programs for Application Security, Data and Device Security, Privacy Engineering, Security Research and a Secure SDLC. Establish metrics, reporting, and dashboards to measure program success and risk reduction.

 - Application Security & Secure SDLC. Develop and oversee secure coding practices with an emphasis on AI adoption, threat modeling, security reviews, and code analysis practices. Partner with engineering leadership to embed security into the SDLC and CI/CD pipelines, ensuring security is integrated from design to deployment. Enable

 - Data & Device Security. Lead data security program, responsible for our underlying cryptography and cryptographic libraries across product offerings as well as codebase secrets management. Lead device security program, responsible for the development of security libraries and frameworks to support product feature development, security vulnerability remediation and minimization. Oversee security standards initiatives and critical security product features.

 - Privacy Engineering. Lead and mature the privacy engineering program, ensuring robust data management practices, controls, and compliance with high privacy standards across multiple product lines.

 - Cross-Functional Collaboration & Leadership. Partner with Product, Engineering, and other teams to balance security with business and product priorities. Represent Product Security in executive and board-level discussions, providing data-driven insights and recommendations. Mentor and develop a high-performing security team, fostering growth and accountability.

 - Security Research. Oversee a Security Research team focused on identifying emerging threats, new attack vectors, and innovative defensive techniques that support 1Password’s products and customers. Drive original research into product, application, and ecosystem-level vulnerabilities, publishing findings responsibly where appropriate. Engage with the broader security community to stay ahead of evolving risks and bring insights back into product security programs.



USA-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $272,000 USD and $408,000 USD, plus immediate participation in 1Password's benefits program (health, dental, 401k and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.



Canada-based roles only: The annual base salary for this role is between $254,000 CAD and $381,000 CAD, plus immediate participation in 1Password’s generous benefits program (health, dental, RRSP and many others), utilization of our generous paid time off, an equity grant and, where applicable, participation in our incentive programs.

At 1Password, we approach each individual's compensation with a promise of fair market value and internal equity commensurate with experience and specific skill set.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.



Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone https://blog.1password.com/inside-the-culture-powering-1passwords-next-chapter/. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results. 

How we work with AI
We are committed to leveraging cutting-edge technology—including AI—to achieve our mission. We also understand that thinking critically about AI in its current forms will help us create better solutions for our customers and ourselves with its future forms, which will help us continue to close the gap between security and privacy and achieve our mission. We want team members at all levels to take the approach of actively learning AI best practices, identifying opportunities to apply AI in meaningful ways, and driving innovative solutions in their daily work. Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.



This approach extends to our hiring process—candidates are welcome to use AI tools responsibly and thoughtfully during the application process. To us, this means we do ask that you join live interviews without using AI tools so we can get to know how you communicate, solve problems, and collaborate with others.

Our approach to remote work

While we are a remote-first company, travel for in-person engagement is a part of almost all roles, and we require our employees to be ready and willing to take part. jobs.title: Staff People Program Manager, Production
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Anduril, we're not just changing the game – we're redefining it. As our Staff People Program Manager of Production, you will partner with leadership and teams from across the business to unpack ambiguous problems and build lasting, scalable solutions for our production employees. The People Programs Team operates at the intersection of people strategy and operational execution, driving programs that enable Anduril to scale at the pace the mission demands.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Staff People Program Manager to join our People Program Team. As Anduril continues to scale its manufacturing operations and production footprint, this role will define and lead the strategic execution of people programs that enable production excellence. From workforce planning and labor strategy to production workforce readiness, you will create deep cross-functional alignment with our Production, Legal, and Operations partners.

This is a high-visibility, high-impact role. You will be the go-to expert on the People Team for production workforce programs, acting as a strategic thought partner to senior leadership while driving hands-on execution. You will proactively address systemic risks across production programs, and frame critical trade-offs for senior decision-makers. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in production or manufacturing environments, a commanding executive presence, and a relentless bias for action.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Define and lead the strategic approach to production-focused people programs, influencing high-level business priorities and ensuring alignment between People Team initiatives and Production org objectives.

• Own the end-to-end execution of multiple complex, cross-functional programs spanning workforce planning, onboarding, training readiness, and labor compliance across Anduril's manufacturing sites.

• Serve as the primary People Team interface to Production, Facilities, Operations, and Supply Chain leadership, building deep trust and translating production needs into scalable people solutions.

• Proactively identify and address systemic risks across production people programs, managing sensitive relationships and framing critical trade-offs for senior decision-makers.

• Build and maintain comprehensive program schedules, risk registers, and stakeholder communication plans, ensuring on-time delivery against aggressive production timelines.

• Partner with the broader People Team (Talent Acquisition, Benefits, Compensation) to design data-driven workforce strategies that support production scaling goals.

• Implement innovative program methodologies that simplify and streamline production people processes, cutting through complexity to deliver efficient, user-focused operations.

• Craft compelling narratives and executive-level communications that convey a clear vision, progress, and strategic recommendations to senior leadership.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 8+ years of experience in program management, operations, management consulting, or a related field, with significant experience in production, manufacturing, or industrial environments.

• Demonstrated ability to define and lead strategic program execution across multiple complex, interdependent workstreams with broad cross-functional dependencies.

• Deep expertise in workforce planning, labor strategy, or production operations within a high-growth or manufacturing environment.

• Track record of serving as a trusted advisor and SME to senior leadership, proactively navigating ambiguity and driving results without clear direction.

• Proven ability to mentor and develop program managers at earlier career stages.

• Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present complex information clearly and concisely to executive audiences.

• You are motivated by our mission. We are working to solve the biggest problems in defense. You have a keen interest in partnering with production leaders to accomplish manufacturing at scale.

• You are both high ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility.

• You do not wait on others to solve problems. You proactively step into the gap to offer solutions yourself.

• You are comfortable with high-visibility work that requires communications to large groups and senior leadership.

• Ability to interpret complex datasets and extract actionable insights that support business objectives.

• Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience supporting production ramp-ups, facility launches, or site expansions in a manufacturing or defense environment.

• Familiarity with production workforce compliance requirements (e.g., labor law, shift scheduling, safety training).

• Experience with change management methodologies and large-scale organizational transitions.

• PMP or equivalent program management certification.

US Salary Range

$158,000—$210,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.description:
About the role:

As a Software Engineer II on the storeLink engineering team, you will design, develop, and support key features for our cloud-native retail management platform. storeLink empowers grocery and drug retailers across three core operational capabilities: in-store price tag printing, Electronic Shelf Label (ESL) device management, and digital video screen display management. Operating within an Azure-hosted microservices architecture, you will work closely with dedicated feature sprint teams, our Principal Architect, and L2 Technical Support Engineers to deliver reliable, high-performance web applications and API integrations.

This is a hybrid position that requires 2 days/week in-office. Currently we are only considering candidates within a commutable distance to our offices in Little Rock, AR; Dallas, TX; Mentor, OH; Miamisburg, OH; and New Century, KS.

Key Responsibilities:

• Full-Stack Feature Development: Design, build, test, and maintain scalable microservices using .NET Core for backend web APIs and modern Angular for front-end web interfaces.
• Database & Cloud Infrastructure: Maintain and optimize MS SQL data structures, leverage Azure AI Search, and support applications hosted on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), Azure Service Bus, Blob Storage, Azure Front Door, and Application Insights.
• API Integration & Services: Integrate storeLink microservices with external systems via REST APIs, including custom rendering engines (such as UE2) for PDF and PNG media generation.
• CI/CD & Production Support: Manage GitHub version control, build/release pipelines using GitHub Actions, and partner with L2 support to triage and resolve escalated production issues.

• BS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related technical field with 4+ years of software development experience (or MS with 1+ years).
• Proven experience building enterprise web applications using .NET Core, C#, Angular, and RESTful Web APIs within a microservices architecture.
• Strong proficiency in MS SQL / T-SQL development, schema design, query optimization, and working with managed database instances.
• Practical experience with Azure cloud components (AKS, Azure Service Bus, Blob Storage, Application Insights) and continuous integration/deployment using GitHub Actions.
• Strong debugging, analytical, and communication skills to resolve complex technical issues escalated from support teams and articulate designs to engineering leadership.

jobs.title: Sr. Systems Engineer II
jobs.description:
Proconex is the exclusive Emerson Impact Partner for Emerson Automation Solutions in the Mid-Atlantic region. We provide a full portfolio of Process Automation Control Systems, Valves and Control Devices, and related technologies and services to a range of customers—in the Life Sciences, Chemical, Power, Refining, Oil & Gas, Food & Beverage, Paper, Metals, and other industries, as well as commercial enterprises and campus facilities. With three strategically located offices, Proconex maintains a deep dedication to its 200+ employees, a sharp focus on safety and quality, and the drive to deliver.

Senior Systems Engineer II

Position Summary

The Senior Systems Engineer II is a senior technical leadership role responsible for leading small to mid-sized automation projects, serving as a primary technical representative for customers, and developing scalable solutions that drive value beyond individual project assignments. This position provides technical leadership across project execution, commissioning, operations support, customer engagement, and engineering best practices while contributing to the growth and advancement of the broader engineering organization.

The Senior Systems Engineer II applies expert-level process control and automation knowledge to architect solutions, optimize manufacturing operations, mentor engineers, improve engineering standards, and influence customer technology roadmaps. This role builds trusted advisor relationships with customers, drives collaboration across technical and business teams, coaches developing engineers, and contributes to organizational initiatives that enhance engineering quality, efficiency, and long-term growth.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead the design, development, implementation, and optimization of industrial automation systems, including Distributed Control Systems (DCS), Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), SCADA systems, data historians, and related technologies.

• Develop control system architectures, control strategies, network designs, automation sequences, integrations, and software solutions that align with customer operational objectives and industry best practices.

• Evaluate customer processes, operational requirements, existing system architectures, and business objectives to develop practical and scalable automation solutions.

• Lead technical discussions, requirements workshops, design reviews, and solution development sessions with customers, vendors, and project teams.

• Serve as the primary technical point of contact for customers throughout project execution, operational support engagements, and consulting activities.

• Lead Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, startup, operational readiness, validation, and lifecycle management activities.

• Troubleshoot complex system issues involving software, hardware, process equipment, networking, integrations, and operational systems while developing sustainable solutions that improve reliability and performance.

• Partner with project managers to develop execution plans, project schedules, resource requirements, technical strategies, risk mitigation plans, and project performance improvements.

• Develop strong customer relationships through technical expertise, proactive communication, responsiveness, and strategic guidance that supports both immediate needs and future initiatives.

• Mentor Systems Engineers and Senior Systems Engineers through technical coaching, knowledge sharing, training, project leadership, and professional development activities.

• Identify opportunities for additional engineering services and collaborate with account management, leadership, and cross-functional teams to support customer growth and long-term partnerships.

• Contribute to engineering standards, department initiatives, process improvements, technical training, scalable solutions, and best practices that improve execution across projects, teams, and customer environments.

• Utilize emerging technologies and digital tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), to improve engineering productivity, technical documentation, troubleshooting, project execution, knowledge management, and business processes.

Travel Requirements

This role includes up to 30% travel to customer sites to support project execution, commissioning, startup, troubleshooting, testing, training, consulting, and other customer-facing activities.

Project assignments may require extended onsite support at customer locations. Individuals in this role must be open to temporary relocation or assignment-based relocation for project work based on customer, project, and business needs.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Engineering Technology, or a related technical discipline or equivalent experience

• 8+ years of experience designing, configuring, implementing, commissioning, troubleshooting, and supporting industrial automation and control systems within manufacturing, process control, engineering services, life sciences, or related technical environments.

• 8+ years of experience developing automation architectures, control strategies, system integrations, software configurations, engineering documentation, and technical solutions for industrial control systems.

• 8+ years of experience leading project execution activities, commissioning efforts, startup support, operational support, lifecycle management initiatives, and technical problem resolution.

• 8+ years of experience interfacing directly with customer stakeholders to develop requirements, provide technical recommendations, lead technical discussions, and support strategic initiatives.

• 8+ years of experience mentoring engineers, providing technical leadership, reviewing engineering deliverables, and supporting workforce development activities.

• 8+ years of experience supporting project planning, estimating, resource coordination, risk management, and technical execution within project-based engineering environments.

• 8+ years of experience using engineering software, business applications, and Microsoft Office tools, including Word, Excel, Teams, SharePoint, Visio, and Project.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with Emerson DeltaV, Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Ignition, Wonderware, OSI PI, PLC, SCADA, or similar automation platforms.

• Experience developing and supporting integrated manufacturing architectures involving control systems, industrial networks, historians, and enterprise integrations.

• Experience leading automation projects within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, life sciences, chemical, energy, utilities, food and beverage, or advanced manufacturing environments.

• Experience leading Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), commissioning, startup, qualification, validation, and operational readiness activities.

• Experience developing technical scopes of work, project estimates, work breakdown structures, and proposal support deliverables.

• Experience with industrial networking, cybersecurity, virtualization, cloud-connected manufacturing systems, databases, system integration, or industrial communication protocols.

• Experience serving as a recognized technical lead, subject matter expert, or trusted advisor for customers and engineering organizations.

• Experience leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) tools to improve engineering productivity, technical documentation, software development, troubleshooting, data analysis, project execution, or other business and engineering workflows.

We are proud to be an employee-owned organization. Through our ESOP, every team member shares in the growth and success of the company, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and long-term rewards.

Proconex offers a standout culture, fantastic work environment, and has very competitive benefits to include premium medical, 401K match, tuition reimbursement, and other unique incentives.

When receiving e-mails from a Proconex or Valspec recruiter, you will only receive e-mails from addresses ending in @proconexdirect.com, @proconex.net or @valspec.net.  Any other domains are impersonations and should be ignored.

Candidates must be legally eligible to work in the United States without company sponsorship.  Also, we are not interested in working on a corp-to-corp basis with other companies at this time.

Any third-party unsolicited resume submission(s) will immediately become the property of Proconex. Proconex will not pay any fee to a submitting employment agency, person, or entity unless a signed agreement is established.

Proconex is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, color, religion, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other protected class. We are committed to providing a professional environment free of any discrimination or harassment, and we are proud to be a Drug-Free Workplace.

jobs.title: Remote Mental Health Therapist – Older Adults (LICSW, LMFT, LMHC)
jobs.description:
Do the work you trained for, without the parts that burn you out. Sailor Health is hiring licensed mental health therapists to provide telehealth therapy to older adults, fully from home. We fill your caseload, handle billing and admin, and give you real clinical support, so your time goes to patients. Don’t just take our word for it: read what our therapists say in our Indeed reviews.

 


🌊 ABOUT SAILOR HEALTH

Older adults are too often overlooked by mental healthcare. Sailor Health exists to change that. Through Medicare-covered therapy, care navigation, and healthcare advocacy, we help older adults move through grief, loss, isolation, and life’s hardest transitions with more ease and peace of mind.

Our model is built around their needs and yours:

 - We handle everything outside the session. Care Navigators and Healthcare Advocates take on patients’ non-clinical needs, so your work stays clinical.

 - You’re part of a team. Clinical Quality Leads provide ongoing consultation, and our provider support team answers questions as they come up.

 - Demand is steady. We serve patients in all 50 states, with a consistent flow of referrals.

 


⭐ THE POSITION

Location: Fully remote, anywhere in the U.S. | Schedule: You set it, 7 days a week available

We’re hiring independently licensed therapists for part-time or full-time roles, paid per session. Choose the setup that fits your life:

 - 1099 contractor: starting at 15 hours per week

 - W2 employee: starting at 25 hours per week, with full benefits

 


💙 WHAT WE OFFER

 - A full caseload, built for you. Share your availability and we’ll match you with patients who fit. No marketing, no chasing referrals. Most clinicians have a full caseload within a few weeks.

 - Your schedule, your call. Work the days and hours that suit you. No on-call, no required evenings.

 - Support that’s actually there. A dedicated clinical lead and live admin help. Our providers tell us it’s the most supported they’ve felt in telehealth.

 - Less paperwork, more therapy. Our telehealth platform and AI documentation assistant handle the busywork.

 - Room to grow. Free CEUs, geriatric-focused training, and clinical consultation with experienced directors.

 - Pay that works for you. 1099 clinicians earn competitive per-session rates, paid as full cash compensation.

 - Full benefits for W2 clinicians (25+ hours/week). Health, dental, and vision coverage, plus a 401(k) with up to 3.5% employer match.

 


💻 YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Provide evidence-based psychotherapy to older adults via telehealth

 - Build individualized treatment plans around each patient’s goals and needs

 - Manage your own caseload and clinical decisions, with a supportive care team behind you

 - Complete documentation in our EMR, with AI-assisted notes

 - Join regular, paid case consultations with experienced clinical leaders

 


📋 QUALIFICATIONS

 - Must be located in the United States

 - Active, independent clinical license (LCSW, LMFT, LPC, LMHC, or equivalent) in the state where this role is posted

 - Master’s or doctoral degree in social work, counseling, psychology, or marriage and family therapy

 - Experience with older adult or geriatric populations preferred

 - Comfortable with telehealth platforms and electronic health records

 - Medicare billing experience a plus (we handle billing either way)

 


✅ WHO THRIVES AT SAILOR

 - You care about the mission. Supporting older adults through grief, loss, and the challenges of later life feels meaningful to you.

 - You understand this population. Maybe you’ve spent years working with older adults, or you’re later in your own career and chose this work on purpose.

 - You do your best work on a team. You want colleagues, a clinical lead, and real support, not just a login and good wishes.

 - You like independence with backup. You trust your clinical judgment and want infrastructure behind you, not oversight on top of you.

 


🚀 APPLY TODAY

If you want a full caseload, a flexible schedule, and a team that has your back while you do meaningful work with older adults, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today, and our recruiting team will guide you through every step of the process.

Learn more: https://www.sailorhealth.com/careers/therapy

jobs.description:

If you require a reasonable accommodation as part of the application process, please contact our recruiting team (recruitment@voxmedia.com).

WHAT COMES NEXT

jobs.title: Clinical Research Coordinator II or III (CRC 2-3) Peoria
jobs.description:
About Us:

Arizona Liver Health (ALH) is dedicated to driving high standards of care and advancing medical innovation through leading clinical trials, ensuring patient safety and regulatory compliance, and generating high-quality clinical data. Our network of multiphase, multitherapeutic research, standard of care, and VEN Centers sites is staffed by skilled providers, research, clinic, pharmacy, and patient outreach professionals. ALH operates state-of-the-art facilities and programs to meet the evolving needs of clinical research and overall patient treatment.

Job Summary:

Arizona Liver Health/Arizona Clinical Trials is looking for qualified candidates for the Clinical Research Coordinator II or III position in Peoria

Title: Clinical Research Coordinator II or III (CRC 2 or 3)

Compensation: $27.50 to $36 per hour, depending on experience

Status: Full-time, Non-exempt, Hourly

Location: Peoria, AZ (N. 83rd Ave.)

Schedule: Monday-Friday, 7am-4pm (set schedule)

Essential job functions/duties:

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

• Under the direction of the Principal Investigator or sub-investigator, manage the conduct of clinical research activities.

• Responsible for coordinating and implementing assigned protocols in compliance with FDA CFR, GCP and company SOPs.

• Collects and records clinical research data, assists in patient assessments, scheduling, maintain study files, study supplies and study medication accountability.

• Review with the Principal Investigator the inclusion/exclusion criteria, overall structure and requirements of each protocol

• Responsible for the recruitment and screening of potential participants, which includes chart review of patients and schedules, contacting leads from outside recruitment efforts, and following up on referrals from all sources.

• Responsible for meeting recruitment goals for each study.

• May assume primary responsibility in the implementation and management of new clinical trials in a knowledgeable and collaborative manner.

• Performs all functions according to established policies (SOPS), procedures, regulatory and accreditation requirements, as well as applicable professional standards.

• Provides educational information to subjects. Serves as a resource and support person for subjects and families by being a consistent person they can contact within the clinical research program.

• Provides all employees and research subjects with an excellent service experience by consistently demonstrating professional decorum.

• Serves as a liaison to all physicians, employees, and third-party vendors.

• Record data and study documentation

• Keep the clinical trial management system updated with newly recruited subjects, tracking completed visits and stipends for the participants and investigators and ensuring status of each patient is accurate. Assign patient stipend pay card at screening Document reason for screen-fail in real time

• Plans, prepares and performs tasks required by protocol, which may include, but not limited to the following:

• Record data as directed using the appropriate media or platform

• Follow procedures for access and security for electronic data entry

• Review keyed data for accuracy as needed

• Send data to the data collection center on a timely basis

• Maintain source documentation for all data entered, including clinic chart visit notes, lab data and procedure reports

• Develop and/or edit source as needed independently or with Quality Assurance / Quality Control team to ensure compliance with protocol and EDC.

• Correct and edit data as directed and as appropriate.

• Informed Consent

• Obtaining patient medical history and medication lists

• Phlebotomy and basic laboratory tests

• Processing & shipping labs for central and local labs

• Patient education and training

• ECG

• Administer questionnaires and assessments

• Vital signs

• Collect information for adverse event reporting

• Assist with efficacy assessments

• Data Entry and Query Resolution

• Study drug administration, including injections

• Tracking study supply inventory and reordering when necessary

• Schedule patient visits in appropriate electronic systems

• Documenting all patient visits and communications in progress notes

• Document and record all AEs and SAEs as outlined in protocol

• Monitor and report adverse events

• Triages adverse events and communicates with the research physician regarding the occurrence of adverse and serious adverse events within 24 hrs. Follow-up with the subject and collaborate information as needed.

• Responsible for administrative duties including filing documents related to subject’s participation in research, regulatory, lab results, receipts, invoices, calibration reports, etc.

• Ensure W-9 and medical release forms are signed by subjects annually.

• Management of site activities during audits and inspections

• Management of ancillary staff as assigned Train and supervise support staff (e.g., CRC I) Mentor for externs Train newly hired employees as either Research Assistant and/or CRC

• Prepare for quality assurance audits and regulatory inspections as needed

• Act as contact person before, during and after audits and inspections

• Provide all required documentation to auditors

• Make all appropriate corrections as requested by auditors

• Coordinate site response to audit/inspection findings.

• Participates in monitoring visits from sponsor provided appointees, ensures monitors are able to meet/speak with PI and ensures all concerns are addressed in a timely manner.

• Other responsibilities as delegated by manager.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities required:

• Minimum (2) years of experience working previously as a Clinical Research Coordinator for late phase clinical trials.

• Experience and training in the conduct of clinical research (specific experience and/or training in clinical research, including IRB submissions, reporting and source documentation, trial management).

• A thorough understanding of regulatory requirements, principles of GCP and biomedical research ethics.

• Interpersonal and communication skills—interact effectively with professional, administrative staff, sponsor and regulatory representatives, patients, potential subjects and referral sources.

• Possess a sound and in-depth understanding of each protocol that has been assigned as a primary responsibility protocol deviations, serious adverse events and other reporting requirements.

• Able to perform all Job duties listed for Job Description for Phlebotomist

• Know and understand all regulatory requirements associated with the conduct of the study assigned.

Travel requirements:

• Some interoffice travel may be required with use of company vehicle or mileage reimbursement

Education, credentials, and/or trainings required:

• Associates or Bachelor's degree in healthcare, clinical research management, or related required.

• Master’s degree or study-specific training preferred

• GCP certification required at hire.

• Experience and training in the conduct of clinical research and basic knowledge of medical terminology.

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Job Name: Spring 2027: Product Integrity Co-op, (January through June)

Location: Needham, Massachusetts, USA

Work Period: January through June

Location & Schedule: This is a full-time, 40-hour-per-week position with 5 DAYS per week onsite in Needham, MA. There is no relocation or housing assistance for this position.

Compensation Range: Ranges from $28/hr - $34/hr. Specific compensation is set according to a standardized scale aligned with your educational level at the time of hire.

Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you're in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. You’ll dive into meaningful projects and tasks that sharpen your skills and deepen your knowledge. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Your time with us will culminate in an opportunity to showcase your contributions and learnings to SharkNinja leaders because this is a program for those ready to shape what’s next — fast.

This role: Product Integrity Co-op

Are you fascinated by how products work and equally determined to make them better? Do you enjoy hands-on experimentation and creative problem solving? Are you ready to apply your engineering mindset to real-world challenges that impact millions of consumers? If so, we invite you to learn more about the Product Integrity Co-op role at SharkNinja.

As a Product Integrity Co-op on the Shark team, you’ll play a key role in delivering durable, high-performing products across a wide range of categories—from floorcare and beauty to home environment solutions. Working closely with engineers and cross-functional teams, you’ll design and build custom electro-mechanical test rigs, perform rigorous evaluations, and extract insights that directly impact how we develop, refine, and launch Shark products. Whether you're simulating real-world wear or diagnosing root causes of failure, you’ll be central to ensuring Shark products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. If you’re hands-on, curious, and excited to be part of an innovative, fast-paced development process, we want to hear from you!

Here are some of the EXCITING things you’ll get to do:

· Design and build custom electro-mechanical test rigs that simulate real-life usage and push our products to the limit

· Develop creative, science-backed test methods to evaluate performance, reliability, and user experience

· Analyze large sets of test data using statistical tools to uncover insights and spot trends that drive engineering decisions

· Document findings with clarity and precision to influence next-gen product improvements

· Tear down Shark and competitor products to understand how they work—and how they can work better

· Collaborate with engineers across product development, quality, and advanced testing to turn data into action

· Gain hands-on exposure to high-impact testing that directly affects the products you’ll see on shelves and in homes

· Explore failure modes and troubleshoot issues to help elevate overall product quality

· Contribute to the continuous improvement of our test lab processes and capabilities

· Build a portfolio of real-world test systems, reports, and cross-functional contributions that bring tangible value to the team

ATTRIBUTES & SKILLS:

· Education: Current student in a related bachelor's or master’s program or has graduated from such a program within the past year

· Must be able to work a full-time, 40-hour-per-week schedule with 5 DAYS per week onsite in Needham, MA

· Prior experience designing or analyzing electromechanical systems

· Excellent oral and written communication to create reports, write business correspondence, & develop procedures

· Change agent with energy, passion, and enthusiasm to drive change

· Analytical, problem solving, and root-cause analysis skills

· Ability to multi-task and handle tasks with competing priorities effectively

· “Hands-on” -building of prototypes, experimental testing of some sort, either in the workshop or in a science context.

· Proficient in all MS Office

Please note that, due to the high volume of applications for early talent roles, response times may vary depending on the specific role and timeline. Our team appreciates your patience!

The Company offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements: medical insurance, health savings account (HSA) with company contribution, sick time, company holidays, employee product discount, product testing opportunities, referral bonuses, and more.

Our Culture

At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day.  Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home.

What We Offer

We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. We empower your personal and professional growth with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community. Together, we won’t just launch products—we’ll disrupt entire markets.
