• Basic computer skills and a comprehension of practice management software and electronic medical record keeping

• Excellent communicator and calm under pressure; ready to lend a hand to support those around you

• Fine motor skills for handling patients and medical equipment

• Ability to stand for prolonged hours, kneel, and work on the floor as well as ability to lift up to 25 kg on own and able to support up to 40 kg with assistance

• Must be willing to work in a noisy environment with strong or unpleasant odors.

• Availability to work nights, weekends, and holidays on a rotating or as needed basis based on hospital needs

• Work well in a fast-paced environment with people from all backgrounds and different personality types

WHO YOU ARE

• Empathetic, instinctively taking a people-centric approach, whether supporting your colleagues or making an effort to understand different perspectives

• Have a sense of humility; acknowledging mistakes, sharing credit with others, and lifting up your team’s’ accomplishments

• Feel a strong sense of ownership over your work, taking responsibility for outcomes and staying committed to achieving long-term, impactful results

• Curious by nature; you ask insightful questions and continuously seek out opportunities to learn and grow your skills and knowledge

HOW WE INVEST IN YOU

• Comprehensive health and wellness benefits that start on day one, including QPR training and access to free therapy or counseling

• Based on your role, you may be eligible for equity after one year of full time, active employment with VEG, so you can share in our growth and success

• A BIG focus on learning and growth, from VEG-created clinical and leadership programs to unlimited ER CE + travel stipend (no really!). Full-time credentialed VEGgies receive a $2,500/year travel stipend. Full-time uncredentialed VEGgies receive a $1,000/year travel stipend.

• Flexible work schedules to support your life outside of work

DEI

At VEG, diversity is not just a word—it's a strength that fuels innovation and kindness. Our mission is “Helping people and their pets when they need it most.” And we do that better when our VEGgies (employees) feel valued, respected, and empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. That's why we're devoted to creating an environment that reflects the diverse communities we serve—where different perspectives are not only welcomed but celebrated.

We are focused on providing equitable opportunities for growth, promoting inclusive decision-making, and ensuring that everyone's perspective is considered. Saying yes to VEG means helping us build a culture where your unique experiences and background contribute to a shared vision: being the world’s veterinary emergency company.

jobs.title: Compute Systems Architect - Expeditionary AI/HPC Data Centers
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril Expeditionary Systems (AES) is building AI Factories and Command/Control centers—specialized, high-performance computing centers designed to process petabyte-scale data and convert it into decisions at machine speed from forward operating bases. These are not traditional data centers. They are air-transportable, power-constrained, hardened systems optimized for AI inference at the tactical edge and deeply integrated with Lattice.

We are seeking a High Performance Compute Systems Architect to design and build these tactical AI/HPC data centers from the ground up. This is a new and highest priority role. You will architect the complete electrical infrastructure—compute node selection, power distribution, thermal management, battery backup system, and physical hardening—that enables AI processing in austere, contested, and DDIL (degraded/denied/intermittent/limited) environments. This capability does not exist today as a fielded system. You will define what this category looks like and build systems that will be deployed in some of the most challenging environments on earth.

Exact candidate title and leveling to be determined based upon technical acumen, professional experience, leadership ability, and assessed capabilities through the interview process.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Own the end-to-end architecture of AI Factory tactical data centers from compute hardware through power architecture, networking, and thermal cooling systems

• Design GPU-accelerated compute clusters optimized for AI inference and training workloads at the tactical edge (NVIDIA H100/A100, AMD MI300, or similar)

• Engineer advanced thermal solutions for high-density compute without traditional data center infrastructure (liquid cooling, immersion cooling, hybrid systems)

• Design air-transportable, modular systems (containerized, palletized, vehicle-mounted) that are rapidly deployable and operationally credible

• Build infrastructure optimized for austere and contested environments—extreme temperatures, limited grid power, SCIF-accreditable, electromagnetic hardening

• Work in tight coupling with Lattice and AI/ML teams to ensure physical infrastructure meets mission-critical software requirements

• Partner with defense customers to translate operational requirements and needs into technical architectures

• Lead prototyping, field testing, and operational validation through military exercises and real-world deployments

• Drive systems from concept through production at scale, working across hardware, software, supply chain, and program teams

• Define standards and best practices for tactical AI compute infrastructure across AES product lines

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related technical field

• 5+ years of experience designing and deploying data center infrastructure, HPC clusters, large-scale compute systems, or tensor / accelerator compute nodes.

• 8+ years of engineering experience designing and deploying electrical products

• Deep expertise in GPU-accelerated computing architecture for AI/ML workloads (NVIDIA, AMD, or similar platforms)

• Strong understanding of power distribution systems for high-density compute including PDUs, power shelves, UPS systems, generators, chillers, power distribution, and energy management

• Experience with thermal management for high-power-density systems—liquid cooling and chiller systems.

• Proven track record building and deploying production infrastructure from concept through operational scale

• Systems thinking ability to optimize across competing constraints (performance, power, thermal, weight, cost, reliability)

• U.S. Person status required (U.S. citizen, permanent resident, refugee, or asylee)

• Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance (U.S. citizenship may be required)

• Must be able to travel up to 15% of the time

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Background in AI/ML infrastructure supporting large-scale inference, computer vision, or autonomous systems

• Experienced with high speed compute infrastructure networking and network topologies

• Familiarity with edge computing architectures, distributed inference systems, or autonomous vehicles

• Background in 3-phase power distribution or HV battery systems

• Experience with tactical military systems, ruggedized computing, or deployable infrastructure in austere or contested environments

• Knowledge of military environmental standards (MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-461) and expeditionary deployability requirements

• Hands-on experience with containerized or modular data center designs (ISO containers, mobile facilities)

• Experience with expeditionary or forward operating base (FOB) infrastructure

• Knowledge of electromagnetic hardening and operation in GPS-denied or communications-contested environments

• Experience with SCIF design or accreditation for classified environments

• Background in aerospace, defense, autonomous vehicles, EVs, or safety-critical industries with rigorous qualification requirements

• Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in relevant engineering discipline

• Holds Active Secret Clearance or higher

US Salary Range

$146,000—$222,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.description:
Technical Program Manager

Location: San Francisco, CA / Remote (US) · Full-Time



About Andromeda

Andromeda is a market and infrastructure platform to buy, sell, and operate compute.



We believe demand for compute will grow exponentially. So fast that a handful of vertically integrated providers won't be able to scale across operations, capital, supply chains, and politics to serve it. The result is a massive wave of fragmentation, with AI factories of every shape and size coming to market to fill this demand. Our job is to enable all of that fragmented compute to flow through one platform, delivering reliable capacity to model builders, research labs, and inference providers when they need it.



We believe every spare electron should be made productive for AI and we're building the platform that makes that possible.



We sit at the center of three forces:

 - Companies that need reliable, high-performance compute fast

 - A fragmented global supply of GPUs across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and independent data centers

 - Capital, risk, and operational complexity that most teams are not equipped to manage 



When we succeed, trillions of dollars of compute will flow through Andromeda. Builders get capacity when they need it. Providers get a reliable way to monetize, operate, and finance infrastructure at scale. Capital gets an easy way to deploy, hedge, and underwrite. In five years, Andromeda won't just participate in the AI infrastructure market. We will shape it.



The Role 

Andromeda's infrastructure team designs, deploys, and operates large-scale GPU clusters for AI labs and compute providers. The Technical Program Manager runs program delivery across our cluster builds. You hold the integrated plan for each build, track dependencies and risks across vendors, and keep the team and customers on one schedule. You report to the Head of Infrastructure.



What You'll Own

 - Build plans: An integrated plan per build covering site readiness, procurement, logistics, deployment, and acceptance.

 - Hardware delivery: Vendor lead times and delivery schedules, tracked with procurement so servers, network gear, and optics arrive on site when the build needs them.

 - Risk and dependencies: Site milestones, power and cooling readiness, and handoffs between teams, with early escalation.

 - Cadence: Regular status reporting to leadership and customers.

 - Program tooling: Tracking and reporting that scales across builds.

 - Process: Templates, checklists, and post-build reviews that make each build faster than the last.



What We're Looking For

 - Infrastructure programs: You have run data center construction, hardware deployment,or large infrastructure programs.

 - Multi-vendor delivery: You have managed OEMs, contractors, and integrators against a fixed date.

 - Technical fluency: You can follow the detail of power, cooling, networking, and server bring-up well enough to spot schedule risk.

 - Clear communication: Your status reports are short, accurate, and early.



Strong Candidates May Have

 - GPU clusters: Program management on GPU cluster builds.

 - Tooling: Experience automating program tracking and reporting.

 - Certification: PMP or equivalent.



Why You'll Love It Here

 - Run delivery on large-scale GPU cluster builds

 - Build the program function from the first hire

 - High talent density, high trust team shaping the compute market

 - Comprehensive benefits for you and your dependents, including healthcare, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and unlimited PTO

jobs.title: Auto Mechanic Supervisor
jobs.description:
Pay Rate: $29.00 and up, based on skills and experience

About Carvana
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period. To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website. Using our Carvana Certified 150-point inspection process, we’re able to verify that every vehicle meets our rigorous mechanical and cosmetic standards.

We strive to provide only the highest quality vehicles to our customers in our mission to deliver a no-hassle, better car buying experience. We are actively looking for passionate and talented individuals who can help us deliver on that promise.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Keep reading below to see what we’re looking for!

Position Overview:
Line Lead is a front-line supervisor role, responsible for directly managing and developing a team of hourly associates in an Inspection Center to regularly achieve production targets.

What you’ll be doing:

• Manage the movement of cars into and out of the Inspection Center safely for repairs, while meeting or exceeding set production and quality goals.

• Meet or exceed inventory production goals on a daily, weekly and monthly basis.

• Oversee day-to-day activities of assigned team; identify team’s strengths and weaknesses; determine areas of opportunity and the appropriate steps to improve.

• Engage assigned team, provide appropriate coaching, development and performance management; offer feedback and demonstrate desired skills.

• Create a work and team environment that inspires positive communication, team cohesion, and adherence to Carvana’s Values.

• Proactively communicate information to team members, providing clear understanding of expectations, performance measures, and goals.

• Prevent and resolve conflict among team members.

• Monitor and ensure adherence to systems, policies, procedures, and performance standards.

• Review and approve identified mechanical and physical defects of incoming inventory.

• Lead a team of production associates and partner with the Inspection Center General Manager to repair or reject inventory based on estimated cost of repairs and/or the overall quality of the vehicle.

• Train a team of production associates using Quality Control standards to identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, minimizing re-checks and delays in production.

• Identify and complete repairs effectively and efficiently the first time, to minimize re-work and delays in production.

• Conscientiously work in ways that decrease the possibility of injury to yourself or other team members in the shop due to spills or other preventable hazardous conditions.

• Effectively manage multiple associates, including ensuring appropriate employee development and performance management.

What the job requires:
To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

• High School Diploma or GED equivalent

• Experience using computers

• Must be at least 18 years of age

• Demonstrated functional expertise in one or more areas pertaining to Carvana’s reconditioning process

• Demonstrated understanding of our current reconditioning processes and lean principles

• Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).

• Must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently; majority of lifting from knee to shoulder heights; other lifting required from various levels

• Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance.

• Requires use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to effectively delegate tasks to team members.

• Ability to communicate and interact with others effectively in a professional, courteous manner.

• Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both written and oral.

• Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.

• Ability to resolve complex issues with guidance from others.

• Ability to work overtime and on weekends.

• Ability to work variable schedule(s) as necessary.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

What we’ll offer in return

• Full-Time Position with a competitive salary

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits

• 401K with company match

• A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more

• A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy, both physically and mentally

• Access to opportunities to expand your skillset and share your knowledge with others across the organization

• A company culture of promotions from within, with a start-up atmosphere allowing for varied and rapid career development

• A seat in one of the fastest-growing companies in the country

Legal stuff
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer.  All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.  Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

jobs.title: Engineering Associate
jobs.description:
Position Purpose:

The Engineering Associate will support the planning, design, permitting, and construction of capital water and wastewater projects, with an immediate focus on PFAS treatment systems (e.g., GAC, IX, and membrane technologies) across the New York Business Unit (Rockland, Orange, Putnam, Tioga, and Westchester Counties). Under the guidance of senior engineering staff, the associate coordinates cross-functionally with Engineering, Operations, contractors, and consultants to deliver projects safely, on schedule, and in compliance with regulatory standards. Key responsibilities include providing construction oversight and inspection services, participating in short- and long-term system planning, and ensuring Asset Owner satisfaction by meeting key project criteria, including operational performance, budget, schedule, and regulatory compliance.

Projects will cover water treatment upgrades, pump stations, storage tanks, pipelines, and wastewater upgrades for plants, lift stations, and collection systems.

Primary Duties/Responsibilities:

• Support the development, design (either internal or external), and delivery of capital improvement projects in accordance with engineering guidelines and procurement policies.
• Ensure corporate Technical and Environmental Health and Safety/Security standards are incorporated into the design specifications.
• Review contractor and consulting engineers submittals, including design drawings, specifications, calculations, and other submittals (RFI, shop drawings) for PFAS treatment systems.
• Coordinate environmental and health department permit applications with local business unit staff for local, state, and federal agencies.
• Conduct on-site field inspections during construction of treatment plants, pump stations, storage tanks, and pipelines to ensure conformance with design plans and EHS standards.
• Track project metrics, schedules, and expenditures against approved budgets, assisting project managers in reporting and forecasting. Ensure they are aligned with budget and prioritize projects based on available funding and risk assessment.
• Drive efficiency into project delivery through the monitoring of delivery metrics and utilization of alternate procurement and delivery methods.
• Support the oversight of construction management personnel to ensure timely completion of assignments, budget compliance, asset management documentation and adherence to applicable standards.
• Provide technical expertise on engineering and operational issues and support facility condition assessments for our water/wastewater operations.
• Ability to work independently and transversally with corporate and local business units.
• Candidate to be a self-starter and demonstrate a strong willingness to grow within the organization.
• Position offers a trajectory for increasing levels of responsibility as merit justifies.

Work Environment:

• Ability to drive independently to and from worksites.
• Ability to traverse active construction sites, walk on uneven ground, climb stairs/ladders, and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

Education/Experience/Background:

• Bachelor’s Degree in Civil, Mechanical or Environmental Engineering or related field, commensurate experience may be considered.
• 0-3 years of related engineering or project management experience in water/wastewater or environmental engineering.
• Hydraulic modeling experience a plus.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

• Strong project management skills (initiating, planning, executing, monitoring, controlling and closing).
• Superior personal effectiveness skills, visible “leadership by example” utilizing participative management involving employees and teamwork whenever possible.
• Strong communication, presentation and reporting skills.
• Familiarity with alternate project delivery methods (design-build, integrated project delivery) and contracting methods (guaranteed maximum price, reimbursable).
• Computer skills (MS Project, Google Suite, AutoCAD, Bluebeam, Oracle Peoplesoft, Hyperion or other planning/performance/budgeting tools a plus).
• Familiarity with local, state, and federal permitting.

Required Certification/Licenses/Training:

• Engineer in Training (EIT) certification (preferred).
• Valid U.S. Driver's License with an acceptable driving record.
• Stormwater Control Inspection certification (preferred).

Physical Requirements:

• Traversing uneven terrain, climbing ladders/stairs, lifting field equipment (e.g., up to 25 lbs.)

Pay Ratee: $85000 to $90000 per year.

Benefits: Veolia’s comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager, Release Marketer
jobs.description:
Hi 👋 I’m Rosalia https://www.linkedin.com/in/rosaliacefalu/, and I look after our Product Marketing team at Ashby.

I started my career in Product Marketing and helped build the Sales Enablement function at HubSpot during its journey from startup to IPO. Since then, I’ve worked across RevOps and Customer Marketing at Procore and Meta, partnering with incredible teams to bring differentiated products to market. I first heard of Ashby through our Head of Content, Anum https://www.linkedin.com/in/anumhussain/ with whom I’d spent those early days at HubSpot, and was inspired by the level of thoughtfulness https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/thoughtful-communication and operating principles https://www.ashbyhq.com/blog/culture/ashbys-operating-principles I saw and read about. I joined Ashby in April of 2024 back in Product Marketing - bringing all these experiences together to help build a thoughtful, high-impact team.

We’re a growing, tight-knit team - and we’re just getting started 🚀 We work closely with Product, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, and every level of leadership, including closely with our CEO Benji https://www.linkedin.com/in/benjaminencz/. We’re seen as strategic partners, not a service desk. PMM at Ashby means influence, visibility, and ownership - and this role is a chance to get in early on a team with strong internal momentum at a company growing fast.

We value technical curiosity, editorial clarity, and first-principles thinking. We avoid jargon, favor plain English, and aim to genuinely help customers understand what our product does and how it can help them. You don’t need a decade in PMM to succeed here - but you do need strong product instincts, clear writing, and a bias for building systems that scale.

We’re looking for a Release Marketer who is excited about owning product releases.

This role is for someone who thrives on the details but understands the bigger picture – someone who can clearly explain how a new feature or product benefits prospects and customers in their daily workflows and approach to talent acquisition. Someone who wants to work closely with Product and Engineering to understand how a feature works, and act as a translator for the front-line teams. That means translating product specs into the materials, messaging, and demos that power our releases. This person should feel excited about selling with value and obsess over customer use cases and how we tell our product story. From crafting one-pagers and recording crisp, clear product videos and walkthroughs, to running our product updates newsletter, to building internal enablement that keeps our whole team informed on what’s changed, you’ll help us tell our differentiated story and keep our launch velocity high.

You’ll work across multiple product lines, so you’ll need to context switch easily. Organization, attention to detail, and the ability to juggle and coordinate across multiple teams are among the most important skills for this role. On any given week, you’ll be keeping several releases moving, each with its own Product Manager.

Because we’ve built deep relationships with a thoughtful, engaged customer base, we’re often co-creating with them - sharing product materials that are actually read, used, and appreciated by people who see us as partners, not just vendors.

This is a great fit for someone who enjoys being in the weeds of technical products, but also has a sharp editorial voice, a strong eye for design, strong product instincts, and loves to always be shipping.

While this role will flex across multiple products, you’ll have the opportunity to grow into eventually owning a full product line. This role is also a great opportunity for someone who wants to flex across PMM and enablement skills, and work on product marketing initiatives that create more leverage for our teams.



Your Background

There is not a single background that is the perfect fit for this role. We care more about the skills and intrinsic capabilities you bring to the table, and could see someone from a number of different backgrounds being a good fit, including:

 - A Solutions Engineer who loves narrative and wants to shape more than just demos

 - An Early-stage AE who worked closely with Product

 - A Product-minded builder with a technical background and customer empathy

 - A GTM specialist with a strong lean for product taste

What You’ll Do

Release Products and Features

 - Own go-to-market planning and execution for feature releases across multiple product lines.

 - Work closely with Product Managers to shape value propositions, messaging, and demo strategies.

 - Produce polished feature videos for use across social media, the website, and other marketing channels.

 - Create assets including blog posts, one-pagers, demo videos, internal launch docs, and enablement materials.

 - Turn features into clear customer value through videos, product walkthroughs, and content that make the benefit obvious.

 - Partner with other product marketers on larger and bundled launches where support is needed.

Keep the release engine moving and create leverage for your team

 - Serve as a product expert and go-to resource for how features work and how we position to the market.

 - Coordinate release promotion with Solutions Engineering, RevOps, Sales, CS & Support teams to ensure audiences across the organization are best-equipped through their channels.

 - Own initiatives that keep the whole team informed on product changes, including our product updates newsletter to customers.

 - Help maintain our product launch velocity by leveraging AI, automation, and building scalable systems to manage a high volume of releases, giving yourself time back for more high-leverage work.
   

You Might Be a Fit If You

 - You’re highly organized, and can keep multiple releases, owners, and deadlines moving at once without anything slipping.

 - You’ve got an exceptional eye for detail - people consistently trust you as the final eye on something because you catch more than just typos every time.

 - You can switch between products and contexts easily, and pick up a new feature quickly enough to explain it well.

 - You’re the person people ping and say, “Can you just explain this feature in normal words?” and you actually can.

 - You know how to shape a good demo or walkthrough that tells a story. Not just “click here, then here” but “here’s how this solves your problem.”

 - You are comfortable owning your own copy and collaborating with design teams to produce well-polished assets.

 - You can read a launch plan and immediately hear the voices of Sales and CS in your head “but what about XYZ?”, and you’ve already worked with technical and product teams for the answer.

 - You can follow a playbook but are not afraid to go back to first principles thinking and build something from scratch without much direction.
   

You Might Not Be a Fit If:

 - You’re drained by the strive for perfection. If a letter is out of place or a font is off by a size point, it won’t bother you.

 - You’re not a natural relationship builder and don’t feel comfortable working across Product and GTM folks.

 - You aren’t the person people go to when they’re trying to understand the complexities of a new product.

 - You find stakeholder and project management more draining than satisfying.

 - You’d rather not weigh in on or be the final call on creative because someone else will catch it (noting you will have design support, but that someone to catch it is you :)

Interview Plan:

 - 30 min with Michelle (Recruiting)

 - 45 min Rosalia (Hiring Manager) 

 - 30 min with Harriet (VP of Marketing)

 - Assignment

 - 30 min with Benji (CEO and Co-founder)

 - Final Round Interview (1-1.5 hours)

Benefits

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year stock option exercise window. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - Unlimited PTO with a strong culture of actually taking time off.

 - 12 weeks of fully paid family leave (US).

 - Generous budget for equipment, software, and office setup. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - $100/month learning budget, with conferences covered with manager approval.

 - Top-tier health insurance for US employees (100% premium covered).



Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Client Partnerships (Local Advocacy & Public Affairs)
jobs.description:
The big picture: Axios is a media company dedicated to providing trustworthy, award-winning news content in an audience-first format. We are hiring an Associate Director, Client Partnerships to join our growing Public Affairs advertising team, with a dedicated focus on expanding Axios' state and local advocacy business. This role will report to the Head of Public Affairs, Client Partnerships.

Why it matters: As policy decisions increasingly play out in state capitols and at the ballot box, organizations need effective ways to reach influential audiences in local markets. In this role, you will drive new revenue by building partnerships with advocacy organizations, political and public affairs agencies, trade associations, coalitions, and other policy-driven entities seeking to influence the conversations shaping state and local communities.

You will play a key role in expanding Axios' presence in the state and local advocacy advertising market, leveraging Axios Local and our broader portfolio of advertising, custom content, and event solutions.

Go Deeper: Ideal candidates will bring an entrepreneurial spirit, a strong hunting mentality, and a passion for Axios' mission. This is a high-energy, business development-focused role requiring an understanding of state and local politics, the advocacy advertising landscape, and the ability to translate client priorities into creative, effective media partnerships.

In this role you'll:

• Drive new business: Identify, prospect, and secure new advertising partnerships with organizations investing in state-level public affairs, issue advocacy, ballot initiatives, and legislative campaigns.

• Build strategic relationships: Develop and maintain relationships with political and public affairs agencies, trade associations, advocacy organizations, corporate government affairs teams, coalitions, and other stakeholders managing state and local advocacy budgets.

• Own the state and local opportunity: Identify priority markets, legislative calendars, ballot initiatives, and emerging policy issues that create opportunities for Axios advertising partnerships.

• Develop integrated solutions: Work with clients and agencies to build strategic advertising programs leveraging Axios Local newsletters, digital advertising, custom content, and experiential opportunities to reach influential audiences.

• Grow Axios' market presence: Represent Axios at industry events, conferences, and networking opportunities to establish the company as a valuable partner for state and local advocacy campaigns.

• Manage the full sales cycle: Lead prospecting, discovery, proposals, negotiations, and closing, while developing long-term relationships that create repeat business.

• Collaborate across teams: Partner with Axios Local, integrated marketing, advertising operations, and other internal stakeholders to develop and execute successful client campaigns.

• Deliver against revenue goals: Build and maintain a strong sales pipeline, identify opportunities for growth, and consistently achieve individual revenue targets.

Worthy of your time: Ideal candidates will embody an entrepreneurial spirit and a growth mindset, with a proven ability to build relationships and generate new revenue. This position requires the following:

• 5+ years of experience in advertising sales, digital media, campaigns, political advertising, public affairs, or agency business development at the state level.

• Existing relationships with state-level political and public affairs agencies, advocacy organizations, trade associations, or other entities investing in state and local issue campaigns.

• Strong understanding of the state legislative landscape, ballot initiative campaigns, and the dynamics of state and local advocacy advertising.

• Proven experience in outbound sales, new business development, and managing the full sales cycle.

• Experience developing multi-market advertising campaigns or selling local and regional media.

• Familiarity with digital advertising, media planning, audience targeting, and integrated marketing solutions.

• Ability to identify business opportunities around legislative sessions, elections, ballot measures, and other policy-driven moments.

• Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.

• Ability to work collaboratively across teams and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• Willingness to travel to priority markets and attend relevant industry events.

• Track record of successfully meeting or exceeding revenue targets.

Starting salary for this role is in the range of $66,000 - $87,000 and is dependent on numerous factors, including but not limited to location, work experience, and skills. jobs.title: Manufacturing Specialist, Silicon Assembly (Starlink)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

MANUFACTURING SPECIALIST, SILICON ASSEMBLY (STARLINK)

One of the most ambitious missions that SpaceX has undertaken to date, the Starlink satellite constellation, is our solution to providing reliable internet to the entire world. In true SpaceX fashion, Starlink is taking the next step in vertical integration by bringing integrated circuit packaging and assembly in-house for development and manufacturing. You will work closely with IC packaging engineers, test engineers, equipment manufacturers, and leadership.

The success of Starlink depends on the quality, reliability, cost, manufacturability, throughput, and security of the products that you deliver. If you seek a fast-paced, dynamic environment; if you thrive on solving difficult problems where resolutions have high impact; and if you love the challenge of building something from scratch, then this role will be an ideal next career step.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own a production room that runs multiple process types. Move across those processes and hold every one of them to the same standard.

• Own output, yield, safety, and 5S on your shift. When performance is off, contain the issue and stay with it until the corrective action is in place.

• Troubleshoot from first principles. Distinguish actual process behavior from alarm indications, present the supporting evidence, and identify the root cause.

• Take on a new process in the room. Learn its constraints, recipe rules, and failure modes, then run it and train technicians to the same standard.

• Drive continuous improvement. Identify the limiter, change the process with engineering, document the change in the work instruction, and measure the effect on throughput or first-pass yield.

• Train technicians until they can run the process independently. Qualify them only to a standard you would defend.

• Keep the room safe and in 5S, and hold that standard on every shift.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 3+ years of professional experience in a hands-on manufacturing environment

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience with high volume or high mix manufacturing, or design for manufacture and product development life cycle, or quality tools including root cause and corrective action, PFMEAs, QMS, process auditing, and statistical analysis of quality metrics

• Experience training technicians across more than one process type

• Able to prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment with ongoing drive for continuous improvement in all aspects of work

• Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal) and ability to succinctly present recommendations to stakeholders, the customer, and management

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Shift: 1st (day shift). Overtime as needed

• Must be able to maneuver in tight spaces

• Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted

• Must be able to stand for extended periods – 8 hours minimum

• Will sometimes be working directly with the hardware on the floor and will have to be comfortable stooping, bending, and standing

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

Our model blends clinical expertise, thoughtful design, and a modern operating platform that supports physicians, patients, and payers alike. We believe innovation and empathy go hand in hand, and by combining cutting-edge AI tools with a relentless focus on human care, we can transform heart health at scale.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Chamber is hiring its first dedicated Financial Associate to help build the financial infrastructure behind our next stage of growth. As a key member of the Strategic Finance team, you’ll turn complex data into clear recommendations that influence provider strategy, growth priorities, corporate development, and executive decisions.

You’ll partner across Finance, Growth, and Network Operations to evaluate provider economics, build financial plans and scenarios, and improve KPI reporting. Your analysis will help Chamber assess new markets, structure provider partnerships and incentives, and allocate resources with greater confidence.

This is an opportunity to shape both the work and how it gets done. You’ll use tools such as Claude to create faster, more flexible models, automate recurring reporting, and deliver timely insights—helping establish a lean, modern finance function that scales with the company.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




STRATEGIC & GROWTH FINANCE

 - Partner with the Growth team to build provider pitch decks and financial cases for network diversification and enterprise opportunities.

 - Evaluate provider deals and other strategic opportunities, including revenue, contribution margin, costs, and profitability.

 - Build business cases and financial models for new initiatives and partnerships.




PROVIDER ECONOMICS & FINANCIAL PLANNING

 - Rebuild and continuously optimize Chamber's provider performance model, including incentive structures that drive sales conversion.

 - Build market-level P&Ls and support how Chamber pays providers, support, and admin staff.

 - Support budgeting, forecasting, and reforecasting processes, including scenario and sensitivity analysis.

 - Support ELT on budgeting, spend, and resource allocation.




REPORTING & DECISION SUPPORT

 - Support month-end close, corporate P&L, and variance analysis.

 - Own and maintain recurring financial and operating KPI reporting for leadership.

 - Drive financial automation — leveraging Claude and other AI tools to deliver real-time insight into business performance.

 - Perform ad hoc financial and strategic analysis for leadership as Chamber scales.




WHAT YOU’LL ACCOMPLISH IN YOUR FIRST 90 DAYS

 - Develop a strong understanding of Chamber’s business model, provider economics, and establish relationships with key partners across the business such as Growth and Network Operations.

 - Rebuild the provider performance model and equip the Growth team to use it for pricing and incentive decisions.

 - Put Claude or another AI tool into practice to improve the speed, accuracy, or usefulness of recurring financial reporting.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, or a related field, along with a working knowledge of accrual accounting.

 - 2–4 years of experience in FP&A, strategic finance, consulting, or investment banking, including at least one year in healthcare.

 - Advanced Excel modeling skills and the ability to translate complex analysis into a clear, compelling PowerPoint narrative.

 - Experience using AI tools such as Claude to build, refine, or stress-test financial models and reporting workflows.

 - Based in Nashville, Tennessee, with the ability to work from the office one day per week.




CHAMBER VALUES

Our values guide how we lead, collaborate, and care:

 - Low Ego: We stay grounded, curious, and open to feedback.

 - Empathy: We build trust through compassion and thoughtful communication.

 - Courage: We take action, think critically, and challenge ideas respectfully.

 - Ownership: We follow through with integrity and hold ourselves to high standards.

 - Grit: We push through ambiguity, move with urgency, and solve problems with horsepower and heart.




LOCATION

Based in Nashville, TN. In-office one day per week.

jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart.

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Mechanical Engineer is responsible for owning the mechanical design and analysis from concept through flight, working closely with electrical/RF engineers, systems engineers, and program management to deliver flight hardware that survives launch and performs in the space environment. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who wants to see a design through its full lifecycle from early trade studies and requirements, through analysis, drawings, fabrication, test, and flight.

The position reports to the Mechanical Engineering Manager and is part of the Engineering department based in San Diego, CA. This role is 100% onsite.

• Own hardware through its full lifecycle — from concept and requirements through design, analysis, build, test, and delivery.

• Design mechanical enclosures, structures, systems, and mounting solutions for spacecraft hardware.

• Perform structural and thermal analysis to verify design margins against launch loads, on-orbit thermal environments, and mission requirements.

• Generate detailed part and assembly drawings suitable for fabrication and inspection.

• Collaborate closely with electrical and RF engineers on PCB layout, packaging, and mechanical-electrical integration.

• Develop manufacturing instructions and work with fabrication/assembly technicians to build flight and engineering hardware.

• Write environmental test procedures (TVAC, sine/random vibration, shock) and support test execution and data review.

• Actively contribute to the enhancement of team tools, templates, processes, and standards.

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

Basic Qualifications

• BS or higher degree in mechanical or aerospace engineering, or equivalent work experience.

• 6+ years of mechanical/electromechanical design experience.

• Knowledge of space flight requirements, standards and environments is required.

• Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals: statics, dynamics, heat transfer, structural mechanics, materials, and fabrication.

• An excellent communicator and proficient in development and delivery of presentations across a range of settings, including formal design reviews.

• Experience with FEA (SolidWorks, Ansys, or similar) to validate structural, thermal, vibrational, performance against program requirements.

• 3D CAD proficiency in SolidWorks and ability to understand and apply GD&T per ASME-Y14.5 to create high-quality engineering drawings.

• Understanding of machining and mechanical assembly as it impacts design.

• Experience writing manufacturing instructions.

• Highly motivated, self-starting, and able to perform duties autonomously without supervision.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience integrating electronic components (PCBAs, motors, sensors etc.) into mechanical designs for space or military applications.

• Structural or thermal testing experience – TVAC, thermal cycling, random vibration, shock.

Government Mandated Requirements

• Must be a U.S. citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance

The good faith base salary range for this role is $125,000–$167,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

jobs.title: Social Media Strategist
jobs.description:
About Seen Health

At Seen Health, we are revolutionizing the way senior care is delivered through the PACE (Programs of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly) model. Backed by top VCs, Seen Health is a culturally-focused, technology-enabled healthcare organization that integrates comprehensive medical care and social support with a high-touch, interdisciplinary approach.

Our mission is to empower seniors to age-in-place with dignity and provide their families peace of mind. We are building upon a proven Home and community based services model to create a culturally-competent and scalable PACE program. We are also building a comprehensive operating system focused on data and workflows that span across systems, processes, people, and care contexts. We want to empower our clinicians and staff with tools that deliver relevant data at the time and site of care and enable them to deliver exceptional care to our participants, which improve clinical outcomes, participant & provider satisfaction, and ultimately our strength as an organization.

We are a mission-driven, multidisciplinary team with deep healthcare, technology, and operations expertise, each inspired by our own personal stories of caring for seniors in our lives. Our name, Seen Health, was chosen to reflect our commitment to provide the highest standard of care to underserved older adults while respecting and incorporating their individual beliefs, heritage, and values, so that they can truly be seen.

About the Role

Our Brand & Marketing team is building a brand that reflects the dignity, warmth, and cultural roots of the care we give. Social media is one of the main ways families first meet us — on Xiaohongshu (RedNote), WeChat, Douyin, Instagram, LinkedIn, and more.

We’re looking for an experienced, self-driven social media strategist to own our channels day to day. You’ll plan and publish content, edit short-form video, grow our community, and make sure every message from an interested family gets a warm, timely reply and reaches our Outreach & Enrollment team. You'll help shape our voice, not just publish it. We want someone who understands what matters to seniors and their families and takes initiative to turn insight into action.

Responsibilities

• Own our Chinese (Xiaohongshu/RedNote, WeChat, Douyin) and U.S. (Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook) channels, with a weekly content calendar and posting cadence for each.

jobs.description:
Site Selection Lead

Location: Remote (US) / San Francisco, CA · Full-Time · Travel up to 50%



About Andromeda

Andromeda is a market and infrastructure platform to buy, sell, and operate compute.



We believe demand for compute will grow exponentially. So fast that a handful of vertically integrated providers won't be able to scale across operations, capital, supply chains, and politics to serve it. The result is a massive wave of fragmentation, with AI factories of every shape and size coming to market to fill this demand. Our job is to enable all of that fragmented compute to flow through one platform, delivering reliable capacity to model builders, research labs, and inference providers when they need it.



We believe every spare electron should be made productive for AI and we're building the platform that makes that possible.



We sit at the center of three forces:

 - Companies that need reliable, high-performance compute fast

 - A fragmented global supply of GPUs across hyperscalers, neoclouds, and independent data centers

 - Capital, risk, and operational complexity that most teams are not equipped to manage



When we succeed, trillions of dollars of compute will flow through Andromeda. Builders get capacity when they need it. Providers get a reliable way to monetize, operate, and finance infrastructure at scale. Capital gets an easy way to deploy, hedge, and underwrite. In five years, Andromeda won't just participate in the AI infrastructure market. We will shape it.



The Role

Andromeda's infrastructure team designs, deploys, and operates large-scale GPU clusters for AI labs and compute providers. The Site Selection Lead finds, qualifies, and secures the data centers our clusters are deployed into. You own the full cycle from market screening through diligence, lease negotiation, and handoff to delivery. You report to the Head of Infrastructure.



What You'll Own

 - Market screening: Assessment of markets and inbound opportunities on power availability, scalability, cost, permitting, and tax.

 - Pipeline: An accurate pipeline of sites, deal status, documentation, and milestones, with risks and delays flagged early.

 - Diligence: Site-level diligence on power capacity and utility timelines, cooling (direct liquid cooling readiness, CDUs, facility water), structure, connectivity, zoning, andpermitting, including on-site evaluations.

 - Lease negotiation: Negotiations with landlords and operators from LOI through execution, working with Legal and Finance.

 - Relationships: Brokers, landlords, utilities, consultants, and development partners across markets.

 - Handoff: A clean handoff into delivery, buildout, and operations, with technical requirements, commercial commitments, and timelines aligned.



What We're Looking For

 - Experience: 6+ years in data center site selection, infrastructure development, or commercial real estate with technical diligence.

 - Market knowledge: Strong knowledge of US data center markets, utility infrastructure, and regional regulatory frameworks.

 - Negotiation: You have led commercial lease negotiations and complex due diligence through to execution.

 - Technical depth: You can read single-line diagrams and MEP drawings and spot gaps in power and cooling redundancy.

 - High-density cooling: You understand liquid-cooled deployments at 100kW+ per rack.

 - Judgment: You make clear recommendations from incomplete information and stand behind them.



Not A Fit

 - Brokerage only: Real estate experience without technical diligence.



Strong Candidates May Have

 - Power: Utility interconnection, power procurement, or behind-the-meter generation experience.

 - International: Site work in Europe, the Middle East, or Asia.

 - Credentials: PE license or equivalent engineering qualification.



Why You'll Love It Here

 - Set the site evaluation standard for every deployment

 - Work across new AI data center capacity in multiple markets

 - High talent density, high trust team shaping the compute market

 - Comprehensive benefits for you and your dependents, including healthcare, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and unlimited PTO



Andromeda Cluster is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
